# Complexity audit

DESIGN.md Part G, "Six standing rules", requires every algorithm to be of low complexity:
O(n log n) or better, O(n²) only with a recorded reason, nothing cubic or worse outside a
polynomial procedure with no known algorithm of lower degree, run only on the connected part
of its input a question mentions, and nothing cut short by a budget, a threshold or a count
of steps. This file lists every place an audit of
2026-10-30 found that breaks the rule, and the state of each. An item is closed when its
fix is in and a scaling test (size n against 8n, in instructions and, since SCALE-bytes, in
bytes allocated) passes, or when the reason it stays is recorded here. Since TESTS-scaling-limit-10_5
(author, 2026-11-13: "13 was too high anyway, I retract that. Let's keep things under 10.5 for
8x scaling." and "Under 10.5, but ideally under 9") the test requires T(8n)/T(n) < 10.5 for work
of order n, and 10.5 × 8^(k−1) for order n^k (`zed_tests::scaling::limit`), whatever n is; a
ratio from 9 to 10.5 (9 × 8^(k−1) to 10.5 × 8^(k−1)) passes and prints a note naming the test.
It replaces TESTS-scaling-limit-13 of the same day, which allowed 13. Where no instruction
counter is open and the test falls back to processor time, it allows twice the limit, as
before. A count that is linear in n by its construction and does not change with the load
(calls of a function, nodes entered, bytes printed) is held to 9 as well
(`scaling::hold_linear`): such a count measures near 8 times on every run, so 9 still finds an
extra log n factor that 10.5 lets through; the six tests that use it held their count under 9,
or under 5 at 4n, before. One limit holds every
order n and n log n test, the radix conversion and gcd sites of C31 among them: n log n is
10.4 times at n = 1000 and under 10.5 from n = 777, n log² n under 10.5 from n = 1,587,343,
n^1.13 is 10.48 times and passes at every n, n^1.14 is 10.70 times and fails at every n. The
tests over 10.5 at their sizes were moved to 8 times those sizes where that passes within 60 s,
or ignored with a plan row that owns the fix (TESTS-scaling-limit-10_5). The limit of 13
replaced SCALE-ratio (2026-11-07), which allowed
8^k ln(8n)/ln(n) × 1.1 (15.4 at n = 16, 11.4 at n = 1000), with 8 (ln(8n)/ln(n))² × 1.1 for C31
(author decision A47, 2026-11-09, `check_log_squared`, now removed), and the limit of
24 × 8^(k−1) before it. Setting `ZED_SCALING_RATIOS` to a file makes
every check append its sizes, order, limit and ratios there.

Status: `open`, `fixed` (with the test that checks it), `kept` (with the reason).

| S2 | `product::Scope::join` builds `Or(R∧A, R∧B)`, copying the common prefix | 2^k in connectives | fixed: `Scope::join` (product.rs) finds the conjuncts the two sides do not share by the difference of their persistent sets (`Conjuncts`), keeps the shared ones once, and puts in place of the rest one `Formula::either` (presburger.rs) of the two sides' remainders, which takes out any conjunct both still hold, with the equalities of two or more atoms both sides hold (Karr's join, `Scope::hull`); the cost follows the conjuncts the sides differ in, not the relation. No cap: replacement 4 removed `Formula::bounded` and its 64 constraints and 64 conjunctions, so a scope keeps every conjunct and each join of sides that differ adds one disjunction. Precision limit: a relation with disjunctions is decided by a greedy choice with one level of lookahead (`Refusal::Disjuncts` where both fail) and projected per disjunction (S16), not split into all its conjunctions. Tests in `l01_39_reduced_product::scaling`: `a_scope_keeps_every_clause_of_a_relation` (k = 1, 4, 40 clauses give 2k constraints), `narrowing_by_a_conjunction_of_disjunctions_scales` (k = 8 → 64; 953 → 8,917 problems solved, docs/thresholds.md 4), `a_join_keeps_the_equalities_of_its_sides_and_scales` (sides that fix k = 32 → 256 names). | S4 | `revision::forward` and `IntervalSet::lift2` multiply piece counts with no cap; `cap` is O(n²) | P^k pieces | fixed, with no piece limit since replacement 3c (`PIECE_LIMIT` and `IntervalSet::lift2` removed): `revision::forward` (revision.rs) and the `*` case of `revision::backward` take their images through `revision::map2` (revision.rs). For operands of k ≥ m pieces, the one with fewer is capped to ⌈(k + m)/k⌉ ≤ 2 pieces and split at 0 again into at most 4 parts, the other into at most k + 2, so at most 4(k + 2) pairs are taken, O(k), and each sign region of the image is capped to the most pieces either operand has in one region, so a chain of operators never multiplies piece counts (S14); the images are sorted, so the work is O(k log k). `IntervalSet::cap` (interval.rs) merges the closest neighbors by a heap, O(n log n). Precision limit (the Complexity tradeoff comment at `map2`): merged pieces fill the gaps between them, so an image can hold values no pair of operand values gives; on 2,000 random pairs of 1 to 6 pieces its members are within 4% (`+`) and 8% (`*`) of exact (docs/thresholds.md 3c). Tests in `l01_24_refinement_lattices::scaling`: `cap_follows_the_merge_rule`, `join_and_contains_agree_with_membership`, `a_chain_of_operators_keeps_to_its_operands_pieces` (`+` over eight-piece operands, k = 200 → 1,600), `an_image_holds_every_result_and_keeps_to_the_most_pieces_of_a_region`, `an_image_with_a_one_piece_operand_is_the_join_of_the_pieces_images`, `the_interval_operations_scale` (cap, forward `*`, join and membership at 4,000 → 32,000 pieces). Before the first fix: old `cap` ratio 65; old chain 64 pieces after one `+` |
| S5 | Omega test: real and dark shadow both recursed with no step budget | 2^V per leaf | fixed, with no count of problems and no limit on variables since replacement 4 (`INTERMEDIATE` and `VARIABLES` removed): `Omega::run` (presburger.rs) is one loop with no recursion into the shadows, which eliminates only while the rows hold no more terms than the input gave, exact eliminations first. At the first inexact elimination the real shadow is tested once (`relaxed_empty`, called from `Omega::run`: real-shadow eliminations while each adds no terms, then the box test); empty, it shows the problem empty, and from there the dark shadow is solved. When the dark shadow has no point, `search` (presburger.rs) tries the splinters of each dark elimination one level deep, those of the side with fewer bounds, and stops at the first point or refusal. Cost: steps polynomial in the rows, not in the bit length of the coefficients (module comment); the cases still above n log n are in S18. Precision limit: two refusals, each a property of the system's shape and each keeping the written constraint: `Refusal::Shadows` when a splinter leaves a gray shadow of its own, and `Refusal::Growth` when every elimination left would add terms and the box test decides nothing. Tests in `l01_38_presburger::scaling`: `chains_of_inexact_eliminations_are_answered` (1 to 15 variables), `a_chain_of_inexact_eliminations_with_a_point_scales` (32 → 256 variables), `an_empty_chain_scales` (256 → 2,048), `a_rising_chain_scales` (128 → 1,024), `a_long_chain_with_a_point_scales` (4,096 → 32,768), `a_long_empty_chain_scales` and `a_long_rising_chain_scales` (2,048 → 16,384). The first fix measured 15 variables: 1.03 s → 2 ms |

Negative controls, run once and not committed: the UTVPI simplex fails both random unit row tests by passing 60 s, and the old splinter search fails the chain test by passing 60 s. Not fixed: on rows with three or more terms and coefficients up to 5 whose integer point is tight (`tight` probe family, refused with Growth), `decide` takes 0.2 s at 32 variables, 0.7 s at 36 and 5.2 s at 48, with about 2,700 pivots in 16 simplex runs at 48: the time per pivot grows with the coefficients the dark-shadow eliminations build, and is spent in i128 `gcd` of the rationals. Since T4 repair 3 (measured at load 2 to 5): the splinters of a refused dark shadow are not searched, which removed a factor of about 13 (tight 48: 4.4 s to 0.34 s; `a_chain_into_a_refused_block_scales`, 64 → 512, catches the old search at 33.5 times the work). What is left is the simplex itself, which is not O(n log n) on these rows: at 64 variables one run takes 1,153 pivots on 99 rows with 19-digit entries (6.7 s), at 96 one takes 2,042 pivots with 30-digit entries (59 s); the tableau fills, and the entries pass i128, so each pivot costs 6 to 29 ms. Running the simplex on the input rows instead is worse (64: 383 pivots, 25 digits, 7.2 s for that run alone). Removing the general simplex (keeping only the UTVPI one) refuses far more: the oracle's 400 four-variable systems go from 229 sat, 21 unsat, 150 Growth to 163, 2, 235, and four step tests fail. No near-linear exact LP exists, so this needs a design decision or a cross-review: a structural criterion that refuses before the simplex, or acceptance of a polynomial simplex outside the O(n log n) rule. Measured in T4 repair 4 and left to the cross-review (the simplex and the Growth criterion are not changed in T4): the family is `l01_38_presburger::tight`, ignored (64 variables: 9.7 s at load 19); a fill rule (a pivot that leaves the tableau with more terms than the rows were given is refused, Growth) with violations kept in ordered sets brings it to 2 ms at 64 and 0.22 s at 4,096 and leaves the oracle's tally at 229, 21, 150; the patch is `/home/luke/Work/wt/xt-t4-simplex-fill-rule.patch`. **Design R (XT-R, 2026-11-03, from the xt round-2 synthesis):** the simplex and `Q::mul`, `lt` and `abs` are removed from `store/simplex.rs` (now `store/linear.rs`), which keeps `Term` and the rest of `Q`. In their place: box stages, O(T) in the terms of the rows (each variable's bounds tightened once per row from the original bounds; an empty box shows the rows empty; the point of the box nearest zero, checked against every row, is a model; else Growth); the column quotient, O(T log T) (proportional columns merged by a unimodular substitution, models lifted by the Bézout factors); and UTVPI potentials in topological order when the graph of unit rows is acyclic, O(V+E), with Bellman–Ford–Moore, O(V·E), left for the cyclic case (since UTVPI-GOR Goldberg and Radzik's search, C24). The cyclic hub measured 42.5 and was not a test; since UTVPI-GOR it is (`stages::the_cyclic_hub_scales`, 7.9). Option A (STATUS.md, L1.38): decisions only the linear program made are now refused; the two L1.38 asserts that counted them were changed, since they measured the LP's strength, not correctness. **BOX-5pt (XT3 B3, 2026-11-03):** the box stage tries five points of the box in turn, the point nearest zero, the lower corner, the upper corner and the midpoints rounded down and up, each taken variable by variable; each costs one pass over the terms, so the stage stays O(T) (five times one point). The oracle goes from 213 sat, 3 unsat, 184 Growth to 255, 3, 142, and the corner oracle from 2,550, 9,282, 168 to 2,586, 9,282, 132. The dispatch on three live variables is a structural class like the one on two (`twovar`), not a size switch. `stages::three_variables_in_many_rows_scale`, 64 → 512 rows, is now Ok(true) with a model that holds: 12.1 times the work (89.2M → 1,082M instructions; 8 · log 512 / log 64 = 12); `hull3::the_shadow_scales`, tangent planes of two paraboloids, 128 → 1,024 pairs of planes: 13.1 (947M → 12,353M). Still refused: three live variables with no unit side, or four or more (three variables since covered by LIVE3; four or more stay refused). Open: cross-review xt round 3 (XR3) for the 18 rationally empty oracle systems still refused **LIVE3 (2026-11-03, author decision: a fixed-dimension linear program at three live variables only):** `store::live3` decides a part with three live variables completely: Megiddo's prune-and-search linear program in dimension three, O(m) in the rows with a constant of the dimension; a simplex of six such programs rounded with a fixed ratio; exact LLL on three vectors, giving Babai's point or a direction of width at most w(3), a constant of dimension three; at most w(3) planes, each two variables by a unimodular completion and `twovar::point`, O(m log m) each. Work O(m log m) in the rows. It runs at the box stage. **HULL3-subsumed (2026-11-05):** the `hull3` stage and `store/hull3.rs` are removed, so `live3` decides every part left with three live variables, with a unit side or not. Measured on `decide` (instructions; load 47 to 57): rows of `stages::three_rows` with coefficients up to a million, summed over 3 seeds, at 64 / 512 / 4,096 rows, 261M / 3,705M / 38,929M with the stage against 203M / 501M / 1,369M without it; the tangent lens of `live3::tangents` over (5000, 5000), 64 / 256 / 1,024 pairs, 355M / 2,198M / 11,712M with it against 941M / 4,092M / 7,163M without it. The stage was faster on small lenses (at most 3.5 times the time) and at worst 28 times the work, and grew 10 to 14 times per factor 8. Its tests moved to `l01_38_presburger::live3` with every case; `a_lens_of_tangent_planes_away_from_the_origin_scales`, 128 → 1,024 pairs: 4.8 times the instructions, 6.9 times the bytes; negative control, run once and not committed: all pairs of the bounds of `z` (Fourier–Motzkin) in place of the stage fail it at 53.2 times the bytes (load 45). `stages::three_variables_in_many_rows_scale` moved to 128 → 1,024 rows, since at 64 `live3` finds the point by a shorter path (6.7M instructions against 210M at 128): 1.9 times the instructions, 3.2 times the bytes. **LIVE3-lp-tangents (2026-11-05):** `live3::point` alone on the lens over the origin (591M, 1,464M, 42,632M, 32,486M instructions at 128 to 1,024 pairs; 41.6 times the bytes) changes path as the size grows; the cost per step does not grow. At 128 pairs the rounded vertex of the first linear program holds the rows, so `point` stops after one linear program on numbers that fit in 128 bits; at 512 and 1,024 pairs it runs five and three, the later ones along directions with 12 to 23 digits, on numbers that do not fit. Each linear program is linear there (35k to 345k pieces visited by `solve1` from 128 to 1,024; `solve2` drops about one piece in eight per round). Every number is an expression of fixed depth in the entries of a few rows (Cramer's rule), and the entries of `tangents` lie below 4·10^6 at every size, so the size of the numbers has a bound that does not grow with the row count. No code change. `satisfiable` does not reach `point` on that lens, since a box point holds it. Test `a_lens_of_tangent_planes_scales_in_point` runs `point` on that lens cut by the slab 10^6 + 1/4 <= Z <= 10^6 + 1/2 (no integer point, so every size runs all six linear programs, the reduction and the slices), 64 → 512 pairs: 8.1 times the instructions and 9.4 times the bytes (83.2M → 782.2M), 10.6 s, load 57 to 60, limit 24 (128 → 1,024: 17.6 and 13.6). Negative control, run once and not committed: a copy of the three pieces at each cut of `solve2` fails it on bytes at 27.3 times (129.6M → 3,532.3M; load 55 to 57). Checked at merge on the lens alone over the origin, at sizes where `point` takes the same path: counting the linear programs at 16 to 512 pairs by 8 and at 2,880 to 8,192, only 24 and 32 (six and five) and 360 to 512 (four, five at 504 and 512) take three or more below 4,096, and 2,880 to 8,192 take one or two, so no pair 8 times apart under 60 s takes three or more. 32 and 512 both take five, with directions of 13 to 25 digits: 19.4 times the instructions (2,196M → 42,544M) and 24.2 times the bytes (36.5M → 885.4M) for 16 times the rows, load 47 to 52; `a_lens_of_tangent_planes_over_the_origin_scales_in_point_on_its_long_path` holds that within 48 (24 for 8). The largest direction has 25 digits at 32 pairs, 23 at 512, 12 at 1,024, and no vertex entry has more than 33 at any size counted. With one linear program, 128 → 4,096 pairs gives 41.9 times the instructions for 32 times the rows. The same negative control fails the new test at 70.3 times the bytes (45.9M → 3,228.6M), and the slab test again at 27.3 (load 43 to 45); after the rebase the slab test gives 8.06 times the instructions (3.59e9 → 2.90e10) and 9.4 times the bytes (load 34 to 43). Now `splinters` splits again a splinter whose own dark shadows have no point when each of its dark eliminations leaves fewer live variables than the elimination it came from, and refuses it with Shadows otherwise ("could lie only in a splinter of their projection that would have to be split again with as many variables left"): such a splinter adds its fresh variable for the one it eliminates, so splitting it need not end (the four-variable example in `omega.rs` ran 41 levels deep, rows 8 to 992, with no rule). The rule depends only on the problem: the depth is at most the live variables less three, and the search is a tree (0 repeated child systems in 10,806, over 32,000 chained systems with coefficients 2 to 11), exponential in the depth in the worst case, as Pugh's test is. The most splinters searched for one question was 8, 9, 18 and 32 for chains of 5, 6, 7 and 8 variables, the mean 2.0 to 2.3. Of those 32,000 systems the new rule decides 30 more (21 with a point, 9 empty; z3 agrees on all 30, and disagrees on 3 flipped answers), at depth 1 and 2. Chained blocks, a tree of blocks and weighted windows (`q1_local`, refused with Growth before any splinter) take the same instructions as before within 0.01%, 9.58, 9.49 and 9.31 times from n to 8n. Negative control, run once and not committed: the old fixed depth fails both new tests with Shadows. |
| Q1-ROWBOX | `presburger.rs` box stage, `box_empty_in` and `row_box_empty`: a test that two rows bound a variable past each other must not compare every pair of rows, nor every row with every other row of a shared variable (a hub) | O(T) in the terms of the wide rows | fixed (cross-review XR3 Q1, 2026-11-03): one pass over the rows; each row is read twice (its largest value over the box, then the rational bound it gives each variable with the other terms at their largest) and each variable keeps the greatest lower and least upper bound seen so far, so a crossing is found at the later of its two rows whatever the order. Exact: `Q` with unbounded `Int`, no rounding. Tests in `l01_38_presburger::scaling`, n and 8n in instructions (limit 24): HUB-SCALE `the_box_stage_with_a_hub_in_one_row_per_block_scales`, Gemini's relaxed blocks with a hub in one row of each block, refused (Growth) after a pass over every row, 64 → 512 blocks (9.3; 9.1 from 16 to 128); `the_row_test_of_the_box_scales`, the same with a crossing block, Ok(false), 64 → 512 (9.2; 8.7). Negative controls, run once and not committed: `row_box_empty` run again over every row of each variable of a row fails both (175.2 and 209.5 at 64; 44.6 and 46.5 at 16); the bounds rebuilt for each row from the rows before it fail the hub family (49.6 at 64, 32.8 at 16) and not the crossing family (21.3), where the crossing is found after about a third of the rows. Precision limit: a system with no rational point that no single pair of rows shows over the tightened box is refused; the resolvent stage that finds more was not adopted (XR3 Q1) |
| Q1-LOCAL | `presburger.rs`, systems of four live variables or more: (1) `pivots` and `Omega::equality` took the pivot of an equality by color alone; (2) an exact elimination was taken only when `Sides::fill`, a count kept per row, showed it adding no terms | (1) on the chain `o[i+1] == o[i] + l[i]` the pivot was a variable the next equality also holds, so the rows grew to 3, 4, ..., n + 1 terms: Θ(n²), 23.4 times the instructions and 32.4 times the bytes from 64 to 512; (2) systems whose exact eliminations add nothing (an opposite pair `l <= a·x <= u` combines to a constant, shared terms cancel, a row written is held already) were refused with Growth at every size | fixed (Q1-LOCAL phase 2, 2026-11-08). (1) The pivot is the least coefficient, then a variable no other equality holds, then color; `Equalities::repivot` chooses again when a variable comes to be held by one equality or two. A step along such a chain then costs O(t log n) for an equality of t terms (proof at `pivots`). `l01_38_presburger::q1_local::growth_of_offsets_laid_end_to_end`: 16.8 times the instructions and 16.2 times the bytes from 64 to 512 (n log n gives 12; 2.37, 2.53 and 2.81 times per doubling, rising; load 27), and after (4) below 9.3 times the instructions and 8.0 times the bytes from 256 to 2,048 (2.09, 2.15 and 2.08 times per doubling; load 14). (2) When no elimination is left by `Sides::fill`, the variables of exact elimination whose real shadow adds no terms counted by the rows it writes (`System::shrink`, renewed for the variables whose rows changed, `System::refresh`) are taken, least count then color, none when two of least count share a row. The stage runs after the inexact eliminations, so the systems decided before keep their path (placed before them, it changed one: `one_scope` answered true incrementally and Growth whole). `System::touch` keeps only the variable of fewest rows of a row added or removed, and `refresh` marks from its rows when it runs: marking at once made each row added beside a long sum cost O(n) (`omega::eliminating_the_terms_of_a_long_row_costs_the_row_each_time` 26.7 times, `scaling::a_cycle_of_rows_scales` 63 times, `stages::a_box_point_held_by_many_rows_scales` 30.3 times). (3) `System::add` drops a row of two terms that another row over the same two variables implies strictly within their bounds, and drops the held rows the new one so implies (`System::dominated`, `implies_in_box`; the rows over the pair are found in `System::pairs`, a hash index from each pair of variables to its held rows of two terms kept by `add` and `remove`, O(1) expected, where the rows of the variable of fewer rows were scanned before, O(d), and the new row is compared with each of the p rows kept over the pair: p was at most 10 in the families of `q1_local` with no growth in n, and 5 in the oracle's, Complexity tradeoff at `dominated`); before, eliminating a convex chain carried rows `k·x - (k - 1)·y >= -N`, all through one corner of the box, one more per step: `q1_local::growth_of_a_convex_valley` took 38.1 times the bytes from 64 to 512 (negative control: the test fails without it). (4) `Omega::flush` resolved every definition of a chain in full before writing the rows (1, 2, ..., n terms along `o[i+1] = o[i] + l[i]`), and `System::refresh` read a row of n terms once for each of the n variables `System::touch` kept in it: both Θ(n²) on offsets, 34.2 times the instructions and 30.4 times the bytes from 256 to 2,048 (2.88, 3.28 and 3.63 times per doubling; the test now starts at 256 and fails on that code). `resolve` now expands the definitions a row reaches in order of their places and ends a path whose coefficient sums to zero (Complexity tradeoff at `resolve`: rows that reach a long chain and cancel it late cost O(m n); prefix sums would remove it), and `refresh` reads each row once per call. Found by counting the operations of each stage at n = 64 to 1,024: the resolved terms and the rows read by `refresh` grew 4.0 times per doubling, every other count 2.0 times; `perf record -e cycles:u --call-graph dwarf` failed ("Failure to open any events for recording") until `--user-callchains` was added, and its call chains were then one or two frames deep. Determinism: `q1_local::the_answer_of_each_family_is_free_of_the_order_of_its_rows` and its three siblings (grid squares, the oracle's 400 systems, fresh seed 1's 2,000) decide each system as written and in five seeded orders with the variables renamed, at once and incrementally (eight prefixes, then the whole as kept conjunctions), and every answer agreed. `decide` sorts the constraints and `solve` puts them in the order of `canonical`, so the order of the rows never reaches the pruning; negative controls, run once and not committed: with `solve` taking the rows as given and `add` leaving in place the held rows a new one implies, no answer changed; a refusal keyed to the first row failed the oracle's and fresh seed 1's tests. `Equalities::subst` keeps `of[j]` exact while it rewrites, since the pivots of an equality not yet rewritten count the equalities that hold `x[j]`. Two opposite rows (kept by `System::add` in `opposites`) and a bound with another row are counted without writing a row; a pair of rows of s and t terms writes at least |s - t| terms, and the sum of these over the pairs past the longest other held row (`apart`) leaves out a long row's growing elimination before any row is written. `q1_local::sliding_windows_of_four_are_decided`: 9.3 times the instructions and 8.4 times the bytes from 64 to 512, refused with Growth at every size before. Negative controls, run once and not committed: without the shortcut for opposite rows and bounds, offsets took 17.2 times the instructions and 28.5 times the bytes (fails); without the bound from the lengths and the marking of `System::touch`, sliding windows were decided at 64 to 256 and refused at 512; with the bound taken over every pair, sliding windows were refused at every size, since pairs that write one row twice or a row held already made the bound exceed the terms removed. Tried and removed: taking dark shadows by the same count decided none of the inexact families and turned weighted sliding windows at 256 into a Shadows refusal at 11.4 times the work of 64. Kept: weighted sliding windows, a band of four, chained and tree blocks of five, sums over grid squares (treewidth about the side) and sparse random rows of 3 and 4 variables (3-SAT is such a system over 0 and 1) are refused with Growth though each has a point (ignored tests in `q1_local`, see the Complexity tradeoff at `Refusal::Growth` in `Omega::run`). Experiment, not kept: taking, where the solver refuses with Growth, the variable of least fill on the primal graph of the rows (exact shadow on a unit side, dark shadow and splinters otherwise). Largest bags of the min-fill and min-degree orders: 4 for weighted windows and the band, 5 for chained and tree blocks, 19 to 55 for grid squares (growing with the side), 36 to 295 for sparse random rows (growing with n). The band was decided at every size, about 13 times the instructions from 64 to 512 without the cost of the probe's choice; weighted windows (except at 256) and both kinds of blocks ended in Shadows, a splinter of a splinter, which the solver searches to a fixed depth of one (a fixed limit of the kind the no-thresholds rule forbids, pre-existing; Complexity tradeoff in `search`); grid squares from n = 36 and sparse random rows from n = 16 ran past 60 s. Inside a bag of 4 or 5 variables an exact answer needs an exact method in fixed dimension 4 or 5; `live3` covers 3 (XR3). |

Since S22b the comparison also accepts the cases of a defect the transfer before shares: it inverted `c - x` as the forward image of `{c} - z`, whose `map2` cap merges the pieces it moves across zero, and kept the merged box exact (`abs(12 - x) >= 5` gave every integer, exact). `c - x` is now inverted as `c - z`, each piece reflected and moved by `c` in one step in `i128` (`reflect`, `preimage.rs`), O(p log p) for p pieces (test `l01_25_preimage_catalog::constant_minus::a_comb_of_pieces_scales`: 8.91 times at 4,096 and 32,768 pieces, instructions, load 74; a reflection that joins one piece at a time took 62.6 times). The comparison finds 16 such boxes, each narrower and checked by the interpreter (2 corner cases, 6 and 7 random guarded chains, 1 random term), and one more inexact box made narrower in the random guarded chains; the counts are held by the tests. Since S22b-rest the summary also reads `c - u` for every constant `c` (as the affine map `-u + c`; before only `c = 0`), and the clip reads `c - x` by `reflect` too: the family j−t over a domain with no finite end (`chain_jt_range_live_scales`) took 66 ms, 0.29, 3.36 and 8.64 s at k = 64, 128, 256 and 512 when `c - u` fell to the transfer before, now 1.1, 2.4, 8.8 and 21 ms, and 10.6 times the instructions at 256 and 2,048 (63.4 times on main 4a2686f; `5 - t` live 10.6, j−t narrow 7.5; load about 85 to 111). On one interval the forward image the clip used gave the same set as `reflect` in all 2,925 cases tried, but raised the rounding flag in 16 (`c = i64::MIN` with the demand unbounded above, `c = i64::MAX` unbounded below), so `MIN - x` with `x >= 0` gave up and listed the box (`constant_minus::the_clip_of_a_reflection_at_the_ends_of_i64`). The comparison counts are unchanged. Since PA-affine-i128 the summary keeps its coefficients and constants in `i128` and gives up an affine step only where one leaves `i128` (each step still O(1); since PA-plus-if no step is given up, below); `pa_if` and `invert_piece` gave it up where a value it is read at left `i64` (until S22-WIDE, below). So `i64::MIN - (u + 3)`, `i64::MAX - (u - 3)`, `-(u + c)` and `2 * u + c` at both ends of `i64` are summarized, checked against enumeration through the test hook `store::summary_preimage` (`l01_25_preimage_catalog::wide_constants`). Until S22-WIDE `preimage` itself took the transfer before on these terms: `Tx::fits` measured the literals by their values. `Tx::reach` summed the magnitudes of the literals, so a constant built as a product (`-2147483648 * 4294967296`, which is `i64::MIN`) passed `Tx::fits`, and the summary read the `i64` end that stands for an infinite domain end as an input: `if (u <= -3) { ((-2147483648 * 4294967296) + 5) - u } else { u }` over all `u` with demand `[0, 10]` gave `u` in `(-inf, MIN + 5] ∪ [0, 10]`, marked exact, though `u = MIN - 100` gives 105. `reach` now also counts each constant part by the magnitude of its value (one cached `constant` call per primitive, linear), and the answer is `[MIN - 5, MIN + 5] ∪ [0, 10]`, exact (`a_product_of_literals_near_an_end_of_i64_is_measured_by_its_value`). After the merge of ST-arms-quad (fa57422) both failed again: `presburger::settle` now joins a disjunction left with one disjunct to the base within the round (ST-arms-quad repair 2, 873f1a8), and on the chain the base becomes one group as long as the chain, which each later disjunct was solved with (k = 256: 1022 solves of 261 constraints in one call; cross 6 to 48 26.2 times the instructions, cross_live 32 to 256 48.6 times the bytes). `settle` (CATCHUP-cross) keeps its point a point of the growing base and first asks `local_repair` whether the disjunct has a point near it and `local_refute` whether its constraints, its atoms' bounds and the base's constraints over its atoms alone have none; each answer is exact, and only when both fail are the groups solved. The points come from `pick` on a test's parts with the disjuncts no point holds yet tried first, and each is checked against every part (`point_with`). `cross_dead` takes 0.177, 0.434, 1.05, 2.57, 6.63 and 18.18 G instructions at k = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 and 256 (`chain_cross_dead_scales`, 8 to 64: 14.5 times; the old `probe`: 158 times, fails; 32 to 256: 17.3 times, the ratio per doubling rising 2.45, 2.58, 2.75), 2.88 G at k = 66. `probe` makes 9 calls of `settle` and 11 of `point_with` per call at every k from 16 to 256 (verifier's counters), so the growth left is outside `probe`; cross_live, which never calls `probe`, grows the same way (0.68 to 11.11 G from 32 to 256, 2.44 to 2.63 per doubling). That it is the bisection of `project_each` is inferred, not measured. `l01_38_presburger::repair::a_chain_whose_point_is_at_an_end_scales` (32 to 256) holds the same for `decide`. Checked identical: a test build that ran the old and the new `probe` on every call and compared their results found 0 differences in 5,047 calls from `l01_25` and about 5,500 on random formulas of 4 variables. A disjunct that no point holds was still tested by one propagation of the whole formula, so `r` disjuncts that propagation removes cost `r` propagations; on cross from k = 51 to 99, `r` is about k - 50, and each settle of the whole formula costs about k, so about k (k - 50) in all (9, 89 and 185 settles per `probe` call and 2.0, 15.1 and 52.8 G instructions at k = 52, 72 and 96, against 1.05 G at 48). Fixed in LIN-probe-refute: at k = 96 the formula implies `i >= 47`, and the disjuncts without a point are the bounds `i <= j - 1` below it. When propagation removes a disjunct, `presburger::learn` tests each bound of one atom it writes, `x <= v`, for weaker values `w` taken from the bounds the other disjuncts write, by an exponential and then a binary search, and records `x >= w + 1` for the greatest `w` the formula has no point with; each later disjunct that breaks a recorded bound is removed without a propagation, and the bounds are added to the parts `pick` searches. A bound is tested first by `bounds_refute`, which propagates bounds of single atoms through the constraints and through the hulls of the disjunctions in two readings, in reverse breadth-first order over the parts that share atoms (leaving out `x`) and then in that order, so a chain of definitions is read from its far end to its start and back, in `O(n log n)`, and then by `settle`. Trail-based undo was measured out first: each refutation on a chain needs every level below decided, so its own propagation is O(k) and the total stays O(k²); `learn` with `settle` alone gained 3 levels per search (36.6 times the bytes), since `settle` does not carry bounds through open disjunctions. `chain_cross_above_its_width_scales` (12 to 96, no longer ignored) passes at 10.1 times the bytes (99.5 M to 1.00 G; 3.98 G and 40.0 times with one propagation per refuted disjunct, the negative control) and 12.3 times the instructions, and l01_38 `probe::guards_beyond_the_inputs_scale` (k guards on inputs 3k/4 wide, symbols whose names do not sort in chain order, 16 to 128) at 11.0 times (41.7 times with one propagation each). cross_live 11.4, cross within its width 8.1, cross_dead 12.5 and cross 7.2 times the bytes, unchanged. The whole `Preimage` is equal with and without `learn` on 2,851 cases of all families (k up to 96 for the cross families, three random domains each). Still polynomial (`// Complexity tradeoff:` at `probe` and at `bounds_refute`): disjuncts without a point that share no bound of one atom are each tested by one propagation, and `learn` adds, for each bound of one atom in a refuted disjunct, an exponential and a binary search over the `m` bounds the other disjuncts write on that atom: up to about `2 log2 m + 1` tests, each one propagation of bounds (`bounds_refute`) and, when that does not refute, one `settle` (the search usually ends on a bound that has a point, which always costs a `settle`), so up to `O(r log m)` settles for `r` refuted disjuncts when no learned bound removes another, against `r` before (verifier's counters: `guards_beyond_the_inputs_scale` 5 calls of `learn` and 16 settles in them, cross 2 and 2); bounds are not propagated until none moves, which can take rounds that grow with the bounds on a cycle. `stage::ends` then still walked a shared term as a tree in `run_closed`, `exact_preimage`, `witness` and the build stage (ledger ENDS-dag); since row ENDS it reads each distinct part once. A join and a monotone operator (`+`, `-`, negation, `min`, `max`) keep their operands and the bounds of their result, `O(1)`, the bounds being those of the operator on the hulls; the pieces are listed only when a reader asks for them (`Ints::set`: a test `==` or `!=`, `mod`, `div`, `*`, the backward projections, the summaries of calls), each set once, on an explicit stack, by the same `IntervalSet::join` and `revision::forward` as before, so every answer is the same. Each run keeps one set for each input domain, each literal and each operator on two sets (`SharedInts`, keyed by the operands' addresses, which the entry keeps alive), so the `k` guards' `x mod 1024` is taken once. Each kernel is put in one form before it keys the memo: each atom that is neither an atom of the disjunct nor a symbol asked for, and not a factor of a product, is shifted by the integer `q` (`a -> a - q`) that brings the constant of its row with the smallest coefficient into `[0, \|coef\|)`. The shift is a one-to-one map of integer points that changes no atom the answer reads, so the answer is unchanged. Disjuncts with a product atom are not shifted. The key also records whether the disjunct was read with the projected base or with the base's groups, so the two never share an entry. An exact fix in O(n log n) is open (xv Q8 report) (`a_band_after_a_disjunction_is_a_known_precision_limit`). Repair 2 (verifier): narrowing by tests on names apart was still Θ(k²), since `atom` conjoined each test into the whole relation as one formula, `join` ran `stated` and `either` over both whole relations, and `project` rebuilt the blocks over all conjuncts each time. Fixed: the relation is a persistent set of conjuncts (`conjuncts::Conjuncts`, `imbl::OrdSet`) with an index from each name to the conjuncts that mention it and one for the tighter-bound rule; a reduce projects only the connected components reached from the names and conjuncts changed since the snapshot taken before the last `project`, and drops the cached parts of a removed conjunct by a range query; a join diffs the two conjunct sets and runs `stated` and `either` on the differing conjuncts alone, and takes the Karr hull only over the equalities reachable from them; enumeration visits only the written terms, names and enumerated entries that changed. Measured, M instructions at k = 100/200/400/800, against 78ddc7e: k disjunctions on names apart in one conjunction 621/1,275/2,601/5,326 against 1,702/5,943/22,050 at 100/200/400; a conjunction of k tests 102/208/425/867 against 125/323/966; k disjunctions assumed one by one 457/932/1,911/3,942. Test `l01_39_reduced_product::scaling::tests_on_names_apart_narrow_in_time_near_their_number`, at k = 50 and 400. Negative control, run once and not committed: at 78ddc7e the test reads 53.1 times the work (867 to 46,082 M; limit 24). Precision against the previous commit on 3,000 random nested tests: 2,998 equal, 2 narrower, both checked sound by enumerating every integer point in a box. `enumerate_exactly`, under `@exact` only, was still O(written) per reduce; fixed by ST-exact-enum, row S40. B4 and the walk stay open as above. Repair 3 (verifier): tests assumed one at a time on one linked component were Θ(k²), since each `project` rebuilt the blocks of the component and projected all of them (M instructions at k = 50/100/200/400 on e658011: chain 100/308/1,099/4,128; star 112/372/1,372/5,423; or-chain 479/1,347/4,411/15,699). Fixed: `Conjuncts` keeps its block-cut forest up to date as conjuncts come and go (`conjuncts::Blocks`, persistent maps; a union-find of trees, the smaller tree rerooted on a link, a merge along the tree path moving the smaller blocks into the largest; a leaf block is removed in O(log n), any other removal rebuilds its component, O(component)); `project` runs a worklist over the due blocks in the order of their least conjuncts, and a block that moves a name puts the other blocks that mention it on the worklist. When a block moves the name whose move put it there (an echo, as with a parity the intervals do not hold), the tree's conjuncts are projected together once, O(tree), and the worklist stops. Measured on the branch: chain 52/108/223/459, star 55/115/241/496, or-chain 213/437/904/1,876; a chain as one conjunction and the tightening of one pair unchanged. Negative control, run once and not committed: at e658011 the chain reads 41.0 times the work (100 to 4,126 M; limit 24). Precision: on 300 random three-name tests none is unsound; 14 are wider than at e658011 and none narrower is guaranteed (the mechanism of e658011 that gave the narrower results is not identified). Re-projecting every part of a block that gained a constraint closed those 14 and B4, but made `narrowing_by_a_conjunction_of_disjunctions_scales` quadratic (66 times at 8 and 64), since each case of each clause re-projects all earlier parts; it is not kept. Kept, hard, the same order at e658011: one block grown one test at a time on two names is quadratic by constraints (22/80/297/1,201 at k = 12/25/50/100; e658011 23/83/313/1,279) and cubic by alternating constraints and disjunctions (e658011 126/1,073/7,765/68,357), since each new conjunct of the block is projected with all its constraints; a fix needs incremental projection Repair 4 (verifier): (a) k `if` statements joined one after another on a linked chain were Θ(k²) (M instructions at k = 50/100/200/400: 326/876/2,733/9,719), since `Scope::join` removed each conjunct of the changed block first, which cut the chain's tree, and `Blocks::remove` then built the blocks of the whole component again. Fixed: `Conjuncts::swap` takes the old conjuncts out of the indices only and gives each new conjunct with the same atoms the place of an old one (`Blocks::replace`); only old conjuncts left over are removed: 241/497/1,026/2,095 (8.7 times for 8 times; `l01_39_reduced_product::linked::if_statements_joined_one_after_another_on_a_linked_chain_take_time_near_their_number`; negative control, the old join: 270 M to 9,240 M, 34.2 times). (b) `assume(a && b)` with `a` and `b` on names apart was wider than `assume(a)` then `assume(b)` (37 of 1,500 random cases, seed 7). Three causes: a conjunct of no atoms (`!(0 == 0)` from `x != x`) was kept and never projected, so even `x != x` alone did not empty the scope; `!(t >= 0)` stayed a negation, so it and an equation on the same names were split into different parts; `relation_of` of the whole conjunction fails when one side has a `mod`, so the side with an `if` lost its relation. Fixed: a conjunct of no atoms is decided when it joins and a false relation empties the scope; `!(t >= 0)` becomes `-1 - t >= 0`; `narrow_linear` takes the sides of a conjunction at the root one by one when the whole has no linear relation. Now 0 of 7,500 (seeds 1–4, 7) are wider; some are narrower, since inside a conjunction a test such as `y != 3` joins the relation (`nests::a_conjunction_of_tests_on_names_apart_narrows_as_the_tests_one_after_the_other`, `nests::a_test_no_value_meets_gives_an_empty_scope_however_it_is_written`; both fail on e60c977). (c) A bound that echoes no longer stops the worklist: it projects its tree once, and the tree's other blocks are skipped while the blocks of other trees go on. Open: the tree sizes kept in `Blocks` are never reduced when conjuncts leave; they only choose which tree is rerooted on a link, so this affects balance, not results. Repair 5 (verifier): after the chain `x_i - x_(i+1) >= 1`, k `if x_i - x_(i+2) >= 3` statements joined one after another cost about k^4 (M instructions at k = 5/10/15/20: 141/1,867/8,743/28,333 at 78ddc7e, 117/1,779/8,489/27,903 at b54d2a6), since `Formula::either` kept the disjunction of the test and its complement, `x_i >= x_(i+2) + 3 \|\| x_i <= x_(i+2) + 2`, which holds at every point, and each later test split into cases on all of them. Fixed: `Formula::or` gives `true` when two disjuncts are complements, `g` and `!g`, or `t >= 0` and `s >= 0` with `t + s` a constant of at least -1, found by one hash lookup per disjunct, so in time linear in the disjunction and with no satisfiability question: 11/27/44/60 M. The joins were then still near k^2 (join alone 83/356/1,599/6,948 M at k = 50/100/200/400), since removing the test's conjunct from the cycle it closed with `x_(i+1)` built the blocks of the whole chain again. Fixed: `Blocks::split` removes a conjunct from a block of names by placing the block's other conjuncts again, in time near the block, when they still link all its names; the tree stays one tree, and only the pieces of the names below the block are rerooted. Join alone 11/26/56/120 M; the whole family 180/375/776/1,592 M at k = 50/100/200/400 (8.8 times for 8 times; was 253/713/2,346/8,552 with the first fix only). The random block test passed 12,000 further cases (4 seeds); the verifier's soundness probe gives 0 unsound of 1,500 nested sequences and 0 wider of 1,800 `a && b` on names apart. Kept, hard, the block grown one test at a time as above: a ladder, the chain with every `x_i - x_(i+2) >= 2`, is one block of 2k constraints, and one test on it projects the whole block, O(k^2) (19/80/359/1,680 M at k = 10/20/40/80); k `if x_i - x_(i+2) >= 2` statements on the chain, each implied, so each join keeps the true arm and grows the ladder, cost O(k^3) (16/89/608/4,869 M at k = 5/10/20/40). The ladder is item ST-ladder below. Fixed: only constraints and negations of constraints are looked up (`HashSet<&Con>`), O(1) per disjunct; a compound `g \|\| !g` is not found and stays a disjunction, sound (Complexity tradeoff comment at `Formula::complementary`). Verifier with this fix: 5/8/25/29 ms at d = 500 to 4,000; program 0.58/1.5/5.5/20.6 s, as at b54d2a6. Test `l01_39_reduced_product::linked::a_nested_or_and_formula_is_built_and_mapped_in_time_near_its_size` (d = 250 and 2,000, order 1); correctness `a_nested_or_and_formula_keeps_every_case` (every integer point of an 8x8 window), `a_compound_disjunct_and_its_negation_are_kept_as_written`. Negative control, run once and not committed: the deep `HashSet<&Formula>` restored reads 62.6 times the work (191 to 11,977 M instructions; limit 24) and the compound test fails. Open, pre-existing: `map_cons` and the other traversals of `Formula` recurse, and a nest of depth 4,000 overflows the 2 MB stack of a test thread, so the test uses d = 250 and 2,000; `product::arms` on a deeply nested condition is quadratic at b54d2a6 as well (0.38 to 27.3 s at d = 250 to 2,000), to be its own item. ST-ladder (merged in part; what is open goes to ST-ladder-incremental): `presburger::project_parts` gives every name of a linked group made only of difference constraints and bounds its hull from two Dijkstra searches, the solver's point serving as the potential (`difference_hulls`; Shostak, J. ACM 1981), O(m log n), in place of O(log d) solver questions per name over the whole group; other groups are asked as before. One test on the ladder: 3/6/11/23 M instructions at k = 10/20/40/80 (31/117/482/2,028 before; `linked::one_test_on_a_ladder_takes_time_near_its_size`, k = 10 and 80, order 1). k `if` statements growing the ladder: 12/38/128/465/1,839 M at k = 5/10/20/40/80 (29/145/911/6,764 at k = 5 to 40 before), O(k^2): each test still builds its block's part from all the block's constraints and projects it once, O(k log k). Near-linear in all needs a projection kept from one test to the next (a potential kept in the scope and repaired for a new edge, Cotton and Maler 2006): done by ST-ladder-potential below. Exactness: equal to `hull_from` on 1,500 random systems over 5 names (`presburger::tests::difference_hulls_are_those_the_solver_finds`); the l01_38 and l01_39 groups pass unchanged. `project_block` now compares each part with the snapshot of its own names, as its comment said, not the whole block's. The walk is still quadratic: 165/835/2,475/12,061/56,474 M at n = 5/10/20/40/80 (13,418 at 40 before), since each case of clause i fixes `w`, which every earlier part mentions, so the i earlier parts are projected again; its result equals the fixed point with the clauses reversed and with the start first (n = 3, 8, 20). B4: keying each part by all its constraints, not only the equalities, empties the scope in both orders, but `scaling::narrowing_by_a_conjunction_of_disjunctions_scales` then reads 68.3 times the bytes at 8 and 64 (limit 24), as in repair 3; not kept. The ladder total, the walk and B4 all need a block's projection to change by the conjunct that changed rather than be computed again (open: ST-ladder-incremental). Negative control, run once and not committed: with the code before this attempt the one-test case reads 52.7 times the bytes (limit 24) and the ladder 231.9 times the work (limit 192); the walk's order checks pass there too, so they guard against a regression and are not a control of a change. ST-ladder-potential: `conjuncts::Blocks` keeps two counts per tree, its conjuncts that are not difference constraints or bounds and its names whose integers have holes or a class (`Blocks::differences_only`, O(log n)). A tree with neither, outside a whole-scope projection, is no longer projected: `Scope::shortest` repairs a potential kept in the scope (a feasible point of the tree's difference constraints) for the new edges by Dijkstra on reduced costs from each edge's head (Cotton and Maler 2006; a path back to the edge's tail is a negative cycle and empties the scope), then moves the bounds by Dijkstra up and down from the changed names over the same potential, O((names changed + their edges) log n) per test. The choice is by the tree's structure, never its size. Exactness: when the intervals of a tree with no holes satisfy every edge's relaxation, the upper corner is a point, so they are the projection; a tree with a name with holes stays on the projection, since `x >= z >= y`, `z` in {0, 10}, then `y >= x` moves no bound but gives `x = y = z` in {0, 10} (`linked::a_name_with_holes_keeps_its_tree_from_shortest_paths`). Review (2026-11-07): the potential is repaired at every edge added at each projection, whichever way its tree is projected (`Scope::repair`), so it holds at every edge of the relation as of the last projection except those of names it lacks (invariant V, doc of `Potential`); a projection of every block empties it. Before, the repair ran only on trees projected by shortest paths, so an edge added while its tree went block by block (a hole or a sum in it) was never put in the potential: a probe on the random test below found 2 edges read with a negative reduced cost, caught by the check at the read, and 17 names with no potential, each a reseed; with the fix, 0 negative reads. Soundness of checking each edge as it is read (doc of `Scope::repair`): under V each edge read has reduced cost >= 0, so Dijkstra keys never fall and names settle in order of distance; an edge keeps reduced cost >= 0 when neither end falls, when only its head falls, and when its tail settled (its edge was read then), and the new edge gets 0; a negative cycle through the new edge u->v is a path P from v to u with w(u->v) + rc(P) < 0, every prefix of which has reduced length < 0 below the new edge's, so the search from v reaches u and reports it. The check at the read therefore fails only at a name the potential lacks. `bound_pass` (doc there) finds the same bounds whatever the potential, a label-correcting fixpoint that pushes a lowered name again; the potential bounds only its cost. A name new to the tree takes the potential its first edge gives when every edge between it and another name was added; otherwise the tree goes to the projection and the potential is set again from `presburger::satisfiable` on the tree's difference constraints and bounds (Complexity tradeoff comment at `Scope::reseed`, not the projection's own solver point). By V this happens once per tree after a projection of every block, never once per test: k `if`s each after an `if` on `x_i + w_i >= 0` read 661 M to 5,576 M bytes at k = 40 to 320, 8.4 times, as before the fix, with no reseed (`linked::if_statements_that_leave_a_ladder_block_by_block_between_rungs_are_linear`, order 1). The same mix with `x_i != 5` in place of the sum reads 303 M to 17,626 M, 58.3 times, as at the base d798ac47 (463 M to 28,036 M, 60.6 times) and with no reseed: the holed tree is projected block by block from the whole tree at each test (profile: `presburger::stable_colors`, `System::count`, formula comparison), pre-existing and outside this item; without the rungs, 27.8 times. Open, not in code touched here: `Scope::projected` is keyed by a conjunct, the equalities it is projected with and its star leaf (`PartKey`); `due` drops the keys of conjuncts removed and a join keeps only keys on both sides, but the key of a conjunct still present stays after its equalities or star leaf change, so the map grows by one entry per such change along a scope's lineage until `forget_projections` or a top relation (read from `due`, `join` and `project_block`; not measured). Measured, bytes at k = 40 and 320: the ladder of k `if` statements 21.9 M to 272.8 M forward and 21.8 M to 271.3 M with the last rung first, 12.4 times for 8 times (`linked::a_ladder_grown_by_k_if_statements_is_linear`, order 1, both orders; was `..._is_quadratic`, order 2). Results: every reduce of the groups l01_39*, l01_38, l01_25 and zedc_preimage was run once both ways and compared (bottom, every name's product, refusals; 361 pieces, 0 mismatches); `linked::shortest_paths_give_the_intervals_of_the_projection_block_by_block` compares 150 random difference ladders, in both orders, with equalities, negations and joined `if`s, against the projection from scratch; `linked::the_counts_of_a_tree_of_differences_are_those_of_the_definition` and the random block test check the counts against their definition. Mutations caught: no lower-bound pass fails the random ladders; ignoring holes fails the counterexample. Negative control, run once and not committed: the new path switched off reads 51.8 times the bytes (91 M to 4,740 M; limit 24). B4 and the walk are unchanged (both have conjuncts that are not differences). ST-hole-project (2026-11-07), fixed: the hole mix above had two causes. (1) A tree with one name with holes went block by block at each test; now `Scope::lone_hole` takes it by shortest paths when that name's holes are each one integer, it has no class, no edge at it lies on a cycle of weight 0 (the potential's weights are pairs, `(w, -1)`, or `(w, 0)` for an edge tied into such a cycle, doc of `Potential`; `Scope::repair` ties the cycles it closes, and the two edges of an equality before either is put in, else a chain of k equalities is O(k²)), and it is the only such name: shortest paths over its hull, then its interval met with the result, then a second pass from it if it moved (`Scope::project_lone`, whose doc has the argument; inferred, not reached by any test: the second pass). Two names with holes interact (`x, z` in `[w, w+1]`, `x <= z <= x+1`, `x != 5`, `z != 6`), so they stay block by block. The arms where the tests hold, folded with rungs: 65 M to 1.19 G instructions at k = 40 to 640, 2.07 times per doubling (was 0.94 G to 67.9 G). (2) A join keeps the last projection of its first arm (`seen`), whose tree had the hole, so the next rung's names were unsure (`Seeds::unsure`) and the tree went block by block; now a seed is unsure only when its tree then held a conjunct other than a difference constraint or a bound: a tree of those alone, holes or not, was projected to a fixed point of single-edge blocks, each exact, so its bounds were a fixed point of its edges. With (1) alone the joined mix still read 62.6 times. Test: `linked::if_statements_that_put_a_hole_in_a_ladder_between_rungs_are_linear` (each name in its own ten values, arms by `assume_case`, order 1 at k = 40 and 320): 104 M to 978 M instructions, 9.4 times, and 19.9 M to 168.7 M bytes, 8.5 times (limit 24; SCALE-ratio 13.76); negative control on the base 20245204, run once and not committed: 328 M to 20,389 M bytes, 62.2 times. Results: `linked::a_hole_in_one_name_of_a_tree_of_differences_gives_the_projection_block_by_block`, 150 random trees, three hole tests a step both ways and 109 joined `if`s, against the projection from scratch: 6,095 tests moved an interval, 2,330 left holes, 662 empty, 77 cycles of weight 0 from pairs of inequalities, 0 mismatches. Left: the mix with x0 alone bounded (`x_i != 5`) is quadratic in its output, the arm where x_i is 5 moving the names below it. Open, pre-existing: holes that pile up in one tree, `k` tests `x_i != 5` that each hold between rungs, read 0.46 G, 3.3 G and 25.6 G instructions at k = 10, 20 and 40 on the base and with this item alike, and 206 G at 80 (cubic), block by block with whole-tree projections (Complexity tradeoff comment in `Scope::project`). ST-holes-many, fixed in part: holes piled in many names of one tree (`k` tests `x_i != 5` between rungs) read 0.72 G, 5.09 G and 38.2 G instructions at k = 10, 20 and 40 on the base 2433d52d (cubic: every hole projected the whole tree block by block). The potential now holds a gap per name (`Potential::gap`): each edge is lowered by the gap of the name it enters, so a hole no wider than that gap leaves the tree to shortest paths; `Scope::raise` widens the gap at a name and puts its out-edges in again (`put_in`, the search `Scope::repair` used), and the search for bounds snaps each bound to the nearest integer of its name, which subsumes the second pass of `Scope::project_lone`; `Scope::lone_hole` and `project_lone` are removed, and a tree is kept from shortest paths only by a name with a class or holes past its gap (`Scope::off_paths`). Test: `linked::holes_piled_in_the_names_of_a_chain_take_quadratic_time` (order 2 at k = 40 and 320): 168 M to 2,527 M instructions, 15.0 times, and 33 M to 398 M bytes, 12.0 times; negative control on the base, run once and not committed: k = 320 did not end in 120 s. Open, item ST-holes-moves, not approved: each hole costs in proportion to the names whose potential it lowers, about k / 2 on a chain whose edges have no slack in the potential (quadratic in all), and `m - 1` on an `m` by `m` grid, `n^1.5` in its `n` names: `linked::holes_in_every_name_of_a_grid_take_time_m_cubed` (order 3 at m = 4 and 32), 45 M to 5,221 M instructions, 115.2 times, and 8.2 M to 870 M bytes, 106.6 times. Shifting a range of the potential at once in a tree over one order of the names was tried and rejected: it is exact on chains and out-trees only; on a grid the names a hole moves are no range of one order (7, 15 and 23 names a hole at m = 8, 16 and 24), and each shift raises the slack of many edges at once. Results: the random test cited above is renamed `linked::holes_in_a_tree_of_differences_give_the_projection_from_scratch` (150 trees, 0 mismatches; since SPLIT-l01_39-rest three tests of 50 trees each, `::{cases_0_to_49, cases_50_to_99, cases_100_to_149}`), and `linked::holes_piled_in_many_names_of_a_tree_give_the_projection_from_scratch` (split the same way) piles holes in many names (6,773 tests moved an interval, 4,803 left holes, 2,296 piled holes in more than one name, 763 empty, 0 mismatches). Left, pre-existing and unchanged: a band `10 <= x_i - x_(i+1) <= 11` with holes `x_i != 10 (k - i) + 5` and joined rungs `x_i - x_(i+2) >= 20` reads 138 M, 4,115 M and 110,524 M instructions at k = 5, 10 and 20 here and on the base (about k^5; 12 M to 28 M at k = 5 to 10 with no hole), since a hole in a cycle of weight 0 still sends the tree block by block (Complexity tradeoff comment in `Scope::project`). Known precision limit, closed by PRES-overlap-fast (2026-11-13: the join of row sums answers these systems exactly), found by cross-review xst round 2 (META2 rows L3 and C1): a value that the holes of two names leave out together, and neither hole alone, was kept, in every order of the tests; sound. Tests: `holes::two_holes_that_together_leave_out_a_middle_value_are_found_exactly` (`a` in {3, 4, 5}, `b` in {5, 7}, `c` in {6, 8}, `b - c <= 0`, `c - a <= 3`, `a - b <= -2`: exact `a` in {3, 5}, kept {3, 4, 5} before) and `holes::two_holes_on_a_cycle_that_together_leave_out_a_value_are_found_exactly` (`x`, `y`, `z` in 0..=6, `z <= y <= x <= z + 1`, `x != 5`, `y != 4`: exact `z` in {0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6}, kept 0..=6 before), each in three orders and checked sound against the interpreter. The tests of cross-review xst rounds 3 and 4 are merged in `l01_39_reduced_product::xst` (XST-unified-tests): nine holes tests that main does not pass waited for ST-holes-moves (two pass with it, seven do not, below), and the S4 scaling families at n and 8n (cycles of weight 0 and 1, open chain, walk, C26, base churn, chain raise) give the exact answer on main but grow 24 to 95 times in time or bytes, so they wait for ST-B4. ST-holes-moves (META4 result 1 of cross-review xst): a tree with holes past the gaps is projected by the ends of its names (`holes::solve`, called by `Scope::by_holes`): equalities joined by union-find with offsets, then the strongly connected components in topological order; a component of one name is O(1) and a search, one cycle composes the maps `t -> snap(min(c, t + w))` round it and takes the greatest `t` with `F(t) >= t`, a component of more cycles with at most two names with holes is contracted onto them by shortest paths (CT), and any other component is refused with a warning of its own (`Cause::Holes`, Complexity tradeoff comment in `holes::Run::component`); the least ends are the greatest of the negated system; O(N log N) in names, edges and pieces. Gemini's Bellman-Ford condition is not used. The block's own projection still runs after the ends, as before, so a value between the ends that it left out stays out (CE-A's `a = 5`). The raises of a tree's gaps (`Scope::raise`) stop at the first that fails, since the tree then goes to the ends, which do not read gaps; when the ends refuse, every name is raised, and if every raise holds the tree is projected by shortest paths with no warning. The cause was the potential (`product::Potential`), not the linear rows the profile named: one value for every name, feasible on every edge and built with no slack along a chain, so each test lowered every name below it, O(k) a test and O(k²) in all. Now `Formula`'s children are `Arc`s (`Not(Arc<Formula>)`, `And` and `Or` of `Arc<Vec<Formula>>`), so a clone is O(1) and a part used in several places is one node. Each pass reads a shared node once: `fold` (`map_cons`, `forget`, `nnf`) keeps a node's result per context, `holds_as` keeps its value, `walk` (`atoms`, `cons`) keeps a visited set, `Ord` and `PartialEq` skip a pair on the same node and keep the shared pairs found equal, and `Hash` hashes each node once, bottom up, so equal formulas hash alike however they are shared. These memos are keyed by `deep::Id`, an owned clone of the node compared by its `Arc` address, and only nodes held more than once (`Arc::strong_count > 1`) are kept. `Drop` frees a part only when it holds the last handle. `nnf` sorts a node in place only when it is the only handle (`Arc::get_mut`); a node held elsewhere is already sorted. `Parts::of` makes a shared disjunction used as a conjunct, or a shared disjunct, once, as an `Rc<Parts>`. `unbounded`'s disjunction search keeps a visited set, and its pairing of each constraint with its cone is `map_cons`. Printing (`Display`, `Debug`) writes the formula out, so its text is the size of the formula written out; a shared conjunction used as a conjunct and a shared disjunction used as a disjunct, flattened into each place at first (O(d k) for k parts used at d places), are now kept whole where the program names them (S31b, fixed by ST-formula-wide). After: 0.49, 0.96, 1.90 and 3.77 G at d = 30, 60, 120 and 240 (1.97 times per doubling), hulls unchanged. | S31b | `presburger::Formula::and` and `Formula::or` (found by ST-formula-share verify#1): a shared conjunction used as a conjunct, or a shared disjunction used as a disjunct, was flattened into the node around it, copied one level deep at each place (`into_parts`), and `Parts::of` and the solver after it (`settle`, `pick`, `witness`, `project_parts`) read its k parts once per place; a shared disjunction used as a conjunct (found by verify#2) was made once, but `Parts::of` copied its list of k disjuncts into each place and the solver read them once per place | O(d k): quadratic in the program's size when k is about d | Fixed by ST-formula-wide. `Formula::and_keeping` and `Formula::or_keeping` keep a part whole where the program names it: the translator keeps the formula of a name (`Node::Var`) used as an operand of `&&` or `\|\|` or in an `if` arm (`preimage::Tx::formula_at`), and `rebuild` and `nnf` keep a kid that was a kept node of the same kind, so keeping never depends on how many handles hold a part. `Parts::of` assumes by key only the parts reached through two or more parents inside the formula (`deep::Id::reached_twice`), not by reference count, so its parts follow the formula alone. Two readers read a kept part at each path to it, which made a chain of names each joining the two before it cost about 1.618 to the d (82 s at d = 28 before the fix): `project_parts` now answers a disjunct once per base and set of symbols (`Below` memo, keyed by its `Rc` address, the base constraints it is read with and the symbols), and `Conjuncts::and_held` reads on an explicit stack and reads a shared conjunction at its first place alone; `Formula::chooses` keeps a visited set. Repair 4: `Formula`'s `Ord` and `PartialEq` compared a kept part as flattened, at each path to it, so comparing a chain of d names, each joining the two before it, with an equal or extended chain built apart cost the number of paths, about 1.618 to the d: 229 ms (conjunctions) and 74 ms (disjunctions) at d = 28 on 33ecd783. Now `cmp` reads the two sides in step (`deep::Side`, `deep::Level`): two kept parts of the level's own kind met at one point of the two flattened sequences are entered together, and when their parts run out together the pair is kept as equal, keyed by the two nodes' `deep::Id`s, so the pair is passed over when met again; the order given is that of the sequences written out. 0.02 ms for both at d = 28. Left: (1) printing (`Display`, `Debug`) still writes a kept part out at each path (`deep::Flat`), so a chain of names prints in size about 1.618 to the d (57.8 KB at d = 16 to 18.6 MB at d = 28, 2.0 to 483 ms, on 33ecd783 and unchanged): messages have no syntax that names a part of a formula, and `Formula` holds no names, so the text cannot refer to a part printed before. (2) Fixed by ST-formula-shift, kept at O(n²) on one family with this reason. `cmp` on two sides that group one sequence at other places on each side, at many shared places, read a part entered on one side alone, or with a partner that runs out at another place, at each place, the size written out: `shared::shifted_chains`, 0.89, 3.5, 13.4, 52.3 and 211 ms at d = 12 to 20 (2^(d+1) - 1 constraints), measured by verify 5. Now `cmp` keeps a visited set of the shared parts of a level's own kind it enters, and when one is entered a second time it compares the parts both sides have left at that level as two sequences parsed bottom up in one arena per call (`deep::canon`; the parse of Mehlhorn, Sundar and Uhrig 1997: runs of one symbol, then chunks cut by deterministic coin tossing, so one sequence has one parse however it is grouped, and equal symbols are one arena entry; no hash decides equality). Until a shared part is entered twice the walk is the old one, linear and stopping at the first difference; a first version that parsed at the first shared part entered alone failed `named_test::arms_of_a_wide_named_disjunction_at_each_tier_take_time_near_linear_in_the_depth` at 48.0 times the bytes. Cost O(e log N) for e distinct edges and N parts written out; on `shifted_chains`, where log N is d, O(d²): 2.4 ms at d = 20, and 5.7, 25, 108 and 440 ms at d = 30, 60, 120 and 240, nearly all of it in building the parses (70,652 symbols and 374 levels at d = 240; the walk of the two roots about 1 µs); from d = 30 to 240, 74.5 times the bytes, under the limit of 192 for order n² (`one_sequence_grouped_at_other_places_on_each_side_compares_in_time_near_quadratic_in_the_depth`, `scaling::check_order` of power 2). Reason for O(n²): the exact methods known for comparing two such compressed sequences (this parse; signature encoding from a straight-line program, Nishimoto et al., MFCS 2016; recompression, Jeż 2015) cost at least n log N, and a hash of each part's sequence, linear, cannot decide equality alone; any locally consistent parse of `shifted_chains` has Θ(d²) distinct symbols (ST-formula-sig, measured on 9e80c1c5: 1,423 → 71,027 symbols, d = 30 → 240). The author accepted this on 2026-11-04: O(n log N) is always acceptable where no O(n) algorithm is possible, so this family stays at power 2 and ST-formula-sig builds nothing more. The parse is built once per call, so a pair compared again is parsed again; keeping each part's parse with the part would remove that. Control, not committed: on 6b01e145 the scaling test does not finish in 60 s, and at d = 2 → 16 it allocates 11,094.7 times the bytes. Tests also: `formulas_shared_and_regrouped_at_random_at_several_depths_compare_and_hash_as_written_out` (layered specs of depth 2, 4, 6 and 8, 60 rounds each; the parse is reached in it), the order of `shifted_chains` against the formula written out at d up to 12, and the unit tests `store::presburger::deep::canon::tests` (3,000 random sequences joined at random places against the parse from scratch, and compared against their order written out). The linked cases above (`rule && (x <= 0 \|\| y <= 0)`, s22) are not taken out and keep their answers. ST-formula-k2-rec: under recursion the memo kept nothing. `Tx::cached` stored a result only where its cut was at or above the stack height at which it was made, so where a call's argument stopped at a call of a function already being read, every chain, `let` and `if` in the body was read again at each place it was reached: a chain of k tests read at r places cost O(r k), and `if` arms that share one term, nested d deep, cost 2^d (relations 1.8, 5.2, 20.6, 82.9 ms at d = 8, 10, 12, 14, the lowest of the runs). Now each memo entry holds its cut (`preimage::Entry`). An entry made with its cut below the stack height is kept while the stack stays at least that high (`Memo::held`), a hit on it passes its cut to the caller as a new reading would, and `Tx::through` drops such entries when it pops below the height at which they were made. Verify 1 (ST-formula-k2-rec): an entry held below a stop depends on nothing that changes before it is dropped. Its key fixes its term and scope, and so the names of the parameters it can read, and each such name belongs to one summary key and so to one interval, so a read under other inputs differs only in names it cannot read; entries made within a call are dropped when that call returns, so none leaves it; and while an entry is held, the lambdas below the height at which it was made are still read at the same places. (1) `absorb`, before any settling, on every path (`decide`, `satisfiable`, `project_each`, renamed or tied): a top-level disjunction is removed when one of its disjuncts removes no point over atoms private to it. An atom is private when it is a symbol or an auxiliary atom, no product or factor of one, not asked for by `project_each`, occurs in no other top-level disjunction, and every row over it is `±x + r >= 0`; a disjunct `d` serves when every pair of a lower and an upper bound on such an atom that involves `d` sums to a constant `>= 0`. Then the bounds on the atom with `d` meet for every value of the other atoms, so over the integers (unit coefficients) the atom has a value with `d` wherever it has one without, and the disjunction removes no point; exact, no answer changes. `repair` gives each such atom a value between its bounds in the model found (its own value when that already lies between them). Only removals are skipped, so a point found is still a point of the formula, and when the search fails `probe` tests disjuncts without `search`. Projections and `probe`'s emptiness tests keep every removal. Tradeoff comment at `settle`: without `search`, or when no disjunct of a disjunction holds at the point, `n` such disjuncts over one linked group still cost `n` solves of it; testing each against one solved group needs an incremental solver. Does `decide` need a model for a disjunction? Yes, it keeps building one: the point of the base is what lets settling keep a disjunct by its own rows (`holds`, `local_repair`) at the cost of those rows; without it each disjunct needs a solve of its whole linked group, O(n) each and O(n²) in all, which is the cost removed here (the chain's 127 solves of 513 rows); and the search that answers `decide` reads disjuncts against a point. A `decide` with no model would need another exact emptiness test per disjunct that does not read the group, which the solver does not have. | PRES-small-point | `presburger::forced` (`forced`, `trial::Trial::holds`, `Graph::facts`, `Graph::point`) and `presburger::{satisfiable, decide, reduced}`: a formula that propagation leaves undecided though its bounded atoms have a point at their bounds (the chain of `max` definitions with its inputs left two values each, `x >= 6 && 7 >= x`) took the solver's whole front end, `satisfiable` 3,667,370 / 22,182,392 / 195,819,102 instructions at n = 8 / 64 / 512 (`decide` 3,345,842 / 21,147,348 / 188,173,744); 64 to 512 is 8.83 times, within O(n log n) (12 times), about 70 times the fixed inputs' cost; and the solver was given the formula as written, without what propagation had proved | O(n) in all. Rounds at the bounds: once propagation ends with the formula undecided, each round gives every unknown variable that gained a bound since the round before that bound (its lower one when it has two), all at once, and continues the same propagation, which may bound more variables; the rounds stop when one sets nothing, at a contradiction, or when the root is decided. Each variable enters the list of bounded variables once and is set at most once, and each round reads only the variables bounded since the last, so all rounds together cost one propagation; at most n rounds. No round tries a second value or undoes one: no search. The formula is answered only when it is true there (a `Point` with zero for each atom still not known; `Holds` for `decide`); a formula true before any round now gets its point directly when a point is asked. Proof that the rounds are monotone and order-free (doc comment at `Trial::holds`): the state is a product of finite-height lattices, each a type whose only changing method moves it one way: `Once<T>` (unknown above the values; `fix`), `Interval` (bounds that only shrink; `meet_lo`, `meet_hi`), `Latch` (`raise`), `Countdown` (`fall`); the fields are private to module `state`. Each rule kind (linear row, disjunction, conjunction, product atom as an atom of its own, contradiction) is monotone and deflationary on that state and fires whenever its condition becomes true, so every event order is a fair chaotic iteration and reaches the one greatest fixpoint below the start (Knaster–Tarski); a round's values are read off that fixpoint, the same in every order. Facts: the atoms propagation fixed before any round are replaced by their values (`Formula::map_cons`, each shared part once, O(n)), beside the sorted equations `a == v`, O(n + k log k); no value a round sets is passed, even as a hint (`Facts` is built before `Trial` takes the graph). A formula refused with the facts is asked again as written: at most two asks of one size. A ladder `x0 <= 5 && x1 <= x0 + 1 && ...`, one rung per round (`small_cost::bench_small_formulas`): `satisfiable` 231,221 / 2,051,765 at n = 64 / 512 (8.87 times), `decide` 161,010 / 1,215,465 (7.55 times). | PRES-nest-empty | `presburger::disjunction_hulls`, new `presburger::DeepHulls` (`join`, `base`, `disjunction`) with `join_bases` and `one_origin`, `Parts::atoms` with `AtomSet`, `union_of` and `union_sets`, `settle_tied` (audit follow-up F2: a nest of k levels `f[i] = (x[i] >= i + 1 && f[i-1]) \|\| (x[i] <= -2i - 3 && f[i-1])` from `f[-1] = z >= 1`, with `z <= 0` beside it, every one of its `2^k` paths empty, was refused with `Disjuncts` from k = 8) | O(n log n) for n rows: each part is read once, on an explicit stack, by its id; the hull of a part is its own rows' bounds met with the meet of its disjunctions' hulls, and that of a disjunction the join of its live disjuncts' hulls; a hull made from another records the forms it changed, so hulls with one origin are joined and met at those forms alone, O(r log n) for r changed forms. Two causes. (1) `disjunction_hulls` joined only each disjunct's own rows, so `z >= 1` at the bottom of the nest never met `z <= 0` at the top; now the implied rows of a disjunction come from the deep hulls of its disjuncts, a disjunct whose hull has crossing bounds is left out, and a disjunction left with none gives `0 >= 1`, so the base alone has no point. (2) A flaw found on the way: `Parts::atoms` merged sets small to large, O(n log² n) on a tree, but on a nest whose disjuncts share one part the sibling sets are equal in value and separate maps, so each level copied one into the other, O(n² log n); now each disjunct keeps its base (the union of its disjunctions' sets) with an id, and a disjunction's union is kept by the ids of its disjuncts' bases and their own atoms; a set made by adding atoms to one set records it as its origin, so sets of one origin are united at the atoms added, O(r log n) (impl#2: before this, a chain of two tests with atoms of their own, `chain_two_atoms`, cost 22.0M, 69.0M, 240.8M, 904.3M at depths 64 to 512, exponents 1.37, 1.65, 1.80, 1.91, and two tests each held by both disjuncts of both at the level above, `pair`, 21.3M, 55.5M, 163.3M, 539.4M, exponents 1.20 to 1.72; `check_order` failed at 18.2 and 13.2 times the bytes; this was the negative control, load 36, not committed). (3) Found by impl#2: a formula whose atoms no structure tells apart (`Naming::Tied`; `chain_two_atoms` and `pair` are such) is settled by `settle_tied`, which did not add the rows the disjunctions imply, so both were refused with `Unordered` from depth 8 although empty; `settle_tied` now first solves the base with them and answers false when it has no point; otherwise it settles as before, without them (settling with them in the base made 49 boxes exact instead of 53 in `l01_25_preimage_catalog::s22`). The rows depend on the rows of the formula alone, not on the names. Decision made unasked: the same test proves `(if a > 0 { 1 } else { 0 }) + (if b > 0 { 1 } else { 0 }) <= 2` raw, which `ladder::conditionals_are_refused_raw_and_proved_once_joined` and `ladder::the_verdict_does_not_depend_on_order_or_names` expected refused; both now expect it proved, and keep a refused case with `(if a > 0 { 2 } else { 0 }) + (if b > 0 { 2 } else { 0 }) != 3`, which the implied rows (each value in `0..=2`) do not decide. Answers depend only on the rows: hulls and sets are kept by id for speed only, and `nest_empty::the_answers_are_those_of_the_formulas_written_out` checks `decide`, `satisfiable` and `project_each` against the formula with a copy of each shared part (k = 1 to 6, six families; `pair` at k = 1 to 3, since written out it has `2^(2^k - 1)` paths).
