Cross-review round 2 (Gemini): `by_pairs` read a pair a rewrite had changed when only its terms were still opposite, so the rows of `v == (u + 2) div 3`, read through `u == (y + 3 v + 1) div 2`, became `y <= 3 v <= y + 5`, which leaves `v` two values, and `v <= 0 && v >= 1` read through them became `-2 <= y <= 0`: a sum of four tests that holds nowhere was answered true. A pair now also needs its constants to add to `m - 1` (unit test `extend::tests::by_pairs_reads_no_row_through_a_pair_a_rewrite_has_loosened` and Gemini's unit in `one_scope::summaries_of_definitions_give_the_answers_of_the_definitions` fail before). Cross-review round 2 (Claude): answers depended on the order the tests were asked in. With tests `h{i}(x: x) < x div 64 - 1`, the first numbers `x div 64` before the later links, and `Summaries::local`, finding it outside each link's summary, read the link beside and went on down, so each later test read the whole chain and was refused (`Growth`) from the fourth link on, where asked alone each was answered. Now the definitions outside the summary are read beside in the link's place, so what is read does not depend on the numbering: `one_scope::separate_tests_over_a_chain_of_largest_values_against_a_quotient_apart_from_it_scale` passes at 8.5 times the instructions and 8.3 the bytes from 25 to 200 links (passes no run within 120 s before), and two chains of such tests in the answers test (fail before, refusals in the unit's order alone). Cross-review round 2 (Gemini, I14): in the mixed family and `max(H div 2, x div 5 + x div 7 - 9)` one quotient of `x` was multiplied out of a piece and the other kept, so `lean` decided rows with coefficients `2^k`. Now `Summaries::make` retries a piece wide (keeping the symbols and the variables of definitions of symbols alone) as soon as such a variable is left after `by_pairs`, the whole shadow and `envelope`, and a summary made wide throughout is cached under its wide key too (`Made::Done(summary, key)`); `lean` replaces the steepest line of a form over two or more atoms by the bound `f <= c` past which the piece has no point (`q3 + q4 <= 9`; exact: the rows imply the bound, and the bound with the flattest line implies the steepest); free division pairs (a quotient in its pair alone) are dropped before deciding, and `decide_cons` merges the lower and upper hulls of each `(y, f)` by two pointers to find an empty interval of `f` before one `decide` (O(r log r); `group_lines`, `hull_of`, `without_free_pairs`). Instructions at 10, 20, 40, 80, 160 links (load 18 to 25): mixed 1.79, 3.35, 7.10, 18.0, 60.9 G (n^0.91, 1.08, 1.35, 1.75; 6.7 to 316 G at 80, n^2.42, before); `x div 5 + x div 7` 1.07, 1.87, 3.48, 6.70, 13.5 G (n^1.01 from 80 to 160; 7.6 to 356 G at 80 before); `x div 3 - 9` 0.34 to 5.34 G (n^1.05); `x - 9` n^1.03. Control, not committed: without the early wide retry, mixed 5.6 to 574 G and `x div 5 + x div 7` 6.9 to 1468 G from 10 to 160 (n^2.2). `hull_of`'s sweep from the front drops lines by a start index, O(h), where `Vec::remove(0)` made it O(h²). The chain `max(H div 2, x div 5 + x div 7 - 9)` is now in `one_scope::summaries_of_max_min_div_chains_give_the_values_of_the_chains` (seventeen chains). Controls, run once and not committed: `by_pairs` with 1 added to each combined row fails both answer tests; without `envelope` the `max(H div 2, x mod 5 + x div 7 - 9)` scale test passes no run within 60 s. Cross-review round 3 (Claude, Codex, Gemini): (a) `merge_pieces` merged a piece with no lower bound on a form and a neighbor above it with different rests without deciding the gap between them, since the side was read from a comparison of the lower bounds; the merged piece then held points of neither (`y >= x` for `x <= 5` and `y >= 2 * x - 10` for `x >= 10`, merged to a piece holding (7, 7), in one of the two orders); now each neighbor carries its side and the gap on that side is decided (`extend::tests::merge_pieces_checks_the_gap_below_a_neighbor_above_a_piece_unbounded_below`, red before); no wrong answer from source was found (every such case in the tests had touching intervals). (b) `without_free_pairs` counted the uses of an atom left after each dropped row by scanning its occurrence list, O(r²) on `y_i == x` (10100 entries read at 100 rows, 640800 at 800); now a count per atom is decremented, O(r t) (`single_use_equations_of_one_shared_atom_are_dropped_in_linear_work`, red before). (c) `merge_pieces` made a neighbor's forms again for each form tried, O(p r³) rows read (1200 at 10 atoms, 524800 at 80); now made once when a piece is put in (`forms_of`), O(p r²) (`forms_of_a_piece_in_a_merge_are_made_once`, red before). Both reviewers proved the ray cap, the dropped free pairs, the hull check and the wide cache exact. Mixed family measured by both on round 2's code: 1.80, 3.37, 7.15, 18.2, 61.1, 231 G at 10 to 320 links (n^1.92 from 160 to 320); big-integer arithmetic is 18 to 19% of the work at 80 links and 37 to 40% at 160, with at most 3 pieces and 5 key atoms per link, so the growth is the `2^k` coefficients' arithmetic. (c) `Walk::lin_called` binds multi-term call results to one `What::Value` variable, and `quotient_offsets` + `normalize_own_leaf` split bounded-offset quotients into residue cases: `H mod 7 + H` summarized in 7 pieces a link at 0.95 to 44.5 G from 10 to 320 links (n^1.03; `separate_tests_over_a_periodic_remainder_chain_scale`, red with `Growth` before). | LOAD-max-div-images | `presburger::extend::images::ScalarImages::residue_map`, `ScalarImages::arm_map`, `ScalarImages::residue_image`, `images::Frame::step`, `Frame::translate`, `front::linear_questions` (step L1.38's linear questions on separate tests over a chain of guarded remainder steps, `h{i}(x) = if H mod M == s { H + b1 } else { H + b2 }`, several exceptional residues, or an affine default `H + w * (H mod M) + C`, handoff item I49) | Before (main 7d96d3826, M = 1e9+7, instructions): two exceptional residues 3.08e9 at 10 links, 5.14e10 at 40 (exponent 2.0); 2 to 8 residues 1.01e11 at 40; affine default with an exception 1.17e9 at 5 links (exponent 4.5); two steps alternating 5.26e10 at 20 (exponent 4.4). Each step maps residue r to u r + c mod M except at the guards' residues; when u is a unit mod M the link's image is the integers less a set D of missing residues, kept in the frame F(x) = U x + T of the composed default maps on a persistent ordered set, so a step costs O(\|E\| log \|D\| + log M) and the chain O(n log n), independent of M | fixed for a unit default: `the_questions_of_a_chain_of_residue_maps_scale` (8.1x at n and 8n), `residue_map_images_agree_with_the_values_of_a_window_of_inputs`, `residue_map_images_at_a_large_modulus_agree_with_a_backward_search`; after: 8.4e7 at 40 and 1.37e9 at 640 links for two residues, 1.80e9 at 640 for 2 to 8, 1.13e9 at 640 for the affine default, 7.8e8 at 640 alternating (exponents 1.0 to 1.01). Fixed for a default u not a unit mod M (LOAD-max-div-unsolved; was 1.2e11 at 80 links for u = 2, M = 1000, refused from 40): the image is a coset K = c + d Z_M less missing points, plus residues outside K. A step with g = gcd(u, M/d) > 1 shrinks K by g, at most log2 M times on a chain; a point of the new coset is missing when all g of its preimages are. The residues outside K are keyed by p_inv (r - r0) mod M, with r0 a point of K moved by every default map. M is split by gcds only (no factoring) into coprime blocks, on each of which every u seen is a unit or divisible by every prime of the block. A step maps one by one only the keys that are nonzero on a block where u is no unit and folds u into p elsewhere, so each residue is mapped at most log2 M times: O(n log M (blocks + log n)) for the chain. Tests: `the_questions_of_a_chain_of_residue_maps_scale` (doubling by 1000 and the 2^40 default at 40 and 320 links, 8.0x; `nonunit_persist_chain` by 2^10 3^10 5^10 at 160 and 1280 links, 1.94e8 and 1.72e9 instructions, 8.9x, limit 12.4; at 256 and 2048 links 3.22e8 and 2.79e9, 8.7x), `residue_map_images_with_mixed_multipliers_agree_with_the_image_of_every_residue` (moduli 360 to 7056 against every residue). Negative control, run once and not committed: 346407a9f, which maps every residue outside K at each non-unit step, 1.95e8 and 2.55e9 at 160 and 1280 links, 13.1x (the test fails). The method was found in CD round 3 (start solution) and written for this code base. Fixed for interval guards `H mod M < s` (LOAD-max-div-unsolved, hybrid cross-review rounds 1 and 2; was 3.45e10 at 40 links, exponent 2.08, as an interval list grows by one per step on some chains): `images::shifts` and `images::intervals`, the image is a set of disjoint residue intervals in a persistent treap whose every node carries an offset added to its whole subtree, so a set moves by a constant in O(1). A step with p pieces cuts the set at each piece's end and at M minus its offset, moves each part by its offset (the part past M by the offset less M) and unites the parts; the union moves each maximal run of one set's intervals in the merged order by one split and one join, O((r + f) log n) expected for r runs and f fused intervals. Bound for any chain, periodic or not: with the potential Σ over gaps g between ends of log2 g, plus 2 log2 M per end, the runs and fusions of a chain of n steps number O(n p log M), so the chain costs O(n p log M log n) expected (Claude seat, round 1; the merge inequality log2(a + b) ≥ 1 + (log2 a + log2 b) / 2 checked by script on 20000 random merges, not machine-proved). Node priorities come from a per-thread splitmix64 counter, not from the ends: a repeated step makes nodes with equal relative ends, and equal priorities made the treap a path (17 to 33 times the work at n and 8n before the fix). Round 1's difference rule for periodic chains (ece80a15c) is removed: its seed at each change of period listed the whole image. Probes at n = 50, 100, 200 (and 400) and 8n on aperiodic, small-move, switching, prefixed, period-64 and wide-gap chains: R 8.1 to 8.6. Exactness: `shift_chain_images_agree_with_the_image_of_every_residue` (unit, against the image of every residue) and a random end-to-end test of 30 chains through the front end. Now the two-term rows over one pair of terms, their signs those of the first term made positive, are sorted by their terms and each run read as one disjunct (`residues::over` already merged the bounds of a disjunct's rows), so `x - 3 q0` in `-1..=0` keeps residues 2 and 0, `x - 3 q2` in `0..=1` keeps 0 and 1, and with link 3's own test the face is empty: `Ok(false)` from the faces at link 3, and every later link holds nowhere from its kept part, with no refusal and no question asked again. Exact: the quotient of a run is one atom left free, so the run's residues are implied by the rows (a relaxation, as every step of `read`), and a run of one row reads as before, so the change only empties more faces. Time: one sort of the two-term rows, O(r log r), the rest as LOAD-holes-mod. Now 0.036, 0.063, 0.119, 0.232 s at 50, 100, 200, 400 links (load 28), no refusal. Answers: on 364 random chains (300 of remainders, 60 of holes, the four chains of the scaling test at 14 links) in both orders, 6066 lines of answers against the old reading, 48 refusals became `false` and no other answer changed (measured once, not committed). Test `each_answer_of_a_chain_of_remainders_is_the_answer_of_the_relation_whole`: six bounded chains and 40 random ones, each answer with faces equal to the one without, refusals too, but where only the faces answer, and then equal to the one found point by point (38 such answers; 4 with the old reading); equal to `decide` on the relation written whole wherever that is decided (1156 answers of the random chains); and the four scaling chains through `answers_are_those_reading_bodies`. Not covered: rows over one atom and one quotient with other coefficients (`x >= 3 q` beside `x <= 6 q + 1`) are read apart, as they bound no `x - m q` together; rows whose atoms are each other's quotient by different moduli are not combined |

Cause, traced: with renamed atoms, `drop_jointly_empty` tests each disjunct against the rows the other disjunctions imply (`disjunction_hulls`), and `y == 0 \|\| y == 2` implies only `0 <= y <= 2`, which holds `y == 1`; with tied atoms (`sets`) no disjunct was removed before the projection at all. So `y[k] == 1` stayed and `z[k]` kept no lower bound | fixed. At the start of `project_parts`, on both namings and on the old path (it asks the solver nothing, so it refuses nothing), each disjunct whose own rows put a form outside the values left to it is removed, until none is: the values the base's rows on the form allow, met with the union of the ranges of each disjunction whose every remaining disjunct bounds the form, gaps kept. The result is the greatest set of disjuncts closed under the test, so no order of disjunctions, disjuncts or names changes it. Each form's values are the segments between the ends of its ranges, with a union-find each way for the segments left, a tree of minima over the ranges by first segment for those with no segment left, a lazy count of coverage for each disjunction and form, and buckets by count that let a disjunction constrain a form once all its remaining disjuncts bound it, so a removal can let a later one happen (`(y == 1 \|\| w == 4 \|\| w == 6)`): O(r log r) for `r` ranges. | TIGHTEN-each-whole | `presburger::tighten_each` (was `tighten`), called once by `project_parts` for all its finite hulls; `linked_conjuncts`, `Hull`, `point_of` with `greatest` | O(k N) for `k` symbols with finite hulls in a formula of size `N`: each symbol read the formula's rows again (`absorbed`, `disjunction_hulls`), searched for a point of them at each end (`point_of` over all rows), checked it with `Formula::holds` on the whole formula, scanned every point found so far, and asked each bisection question of the whole formula. Measured, all `y[k]` and `z[k]` of unchained `l01_38_presburger::omega::dead2`, 16 → 128 stages: 56.1 times the bytes (29.7 MB → 1.67 GB); chained 61.6 (51.8 MB → 3.19 GB); limit 15.4 | fixed for the tightening. `tighten_each` reads the rows once per group, not per symbol. The top-level conjuncts are put in groups linked by shared atoms (a union-find over conjuncts and atoms, a product linked to its factors, shared parts walked once through `Id`), O(N log N). When there are two groups or more and each is shown to have a point, each symbol is asked of its own group alone, which is exact: `f ∧ c(x)` has a point exactly when `x`'s group with `c(x)` has one and the other groups have points. When a group has no point, every finite hull is empty; when the solver refuses a group, every symbol is asked of the whole formula, as before. Each group keeps the least and greatest value of each symbol over the points found so far (O(1) per lookup), and each finite hull's bounds are added to the group's rows (the formula implies them), so one point with every atom least and one with every atom greatest (`point_of(rows, greatest)`) show every end that the rows decide at once. A question is skipped only where a point found has the symbol past the asked value, so the exact answer would be "has a point" and the bound would not move; no bound moves without a proof, as before. The attempt PROJECT-each-chain-all asked each disjunction only for the symbols it names (n^1.12 on `chain`) but lost 12 exact answers where symbols are tied by equalities (l01_39 linked, 4 xst::holes, 2 pendants, 5 l01_25 s22) | fixed (cross-review PROJECT-each-chain-xr, method C5). Each component of disjunctions and the base groups they link, whose base rows and disjuncts are all difference rows and bounds (no nested disjunction), is read as a constraint graph: tie classes are the strongly connected components of the base edges of reduced weight 0 at the base's point (Kosaraju; a cycle of tight edges fixes every difference on it, so each atom is its class's representative plus a fixed offset); the classes, joined by the base edges between classes and by each disjunction over two classes, must form a forest (union-find), with at most one disjunction per pair of classes; a disjunction over one class is met into that class's set. Two passes of arc revision over each tree (leaves to root, then root to leaves; Freuder 1982) give each class exactly the values it takes at some point of the component, since on a tree each value that survives both passes extends to a full point; the answer of each atom is its class's set moved by its offset, met with the hull main computes. The disjunctions of a component so handled are asked about no symbol. A component with a cycle, two disjunctions on one pair of classes, a disjunction over three classes, a row that is not a difference row or bound, or an empty set falls back to main's way, unchanged. Before the exact passes, the same two passes on hulls alone (each set one interval) bound every set, so a set built from the leaves holds only values inside the bounds the whole tree gives (`pinlast`: 1.23 → 1.15 per doubling). Cost: O(m log m) for `m` rows and disjuncts, plus the sizes of the sets, which are those of the answers: `steps` (`x[k+1] - x[k]` in `{0, 10}`) gives `x[n]` `n + 1` intervals, Θ(n²) in all, inherent in an exact answer (main gave hulls); subset-sum weights `2^k` are pathological. After, per doubling from 128 to 256 (main's exponent in brackets): `chain` 1.13 (0.65e9 instructions at 256 against main 32.9e9, 2.05), `both` 1.15 (2.08), `twoway` 1.15 (2.08), `pair` 1.15 (2.02), `mono` 1.13 (2.06), `mono1` 1.13 (2.06), `eqchain` 1.15 (2.02), `band` 1.16 (2.06), `wide` 1.15 (2.07), `slope` 1.15 (2.06), `steps` 1.18 (exact sets of Θ(n²) intervals; 1.31 from 64 to 128), `pinned` 1.14, `pinlast` 1.12; first answers equal main's on the ten families, exact (narrower than main's hulls) on `steps` and `pinlast`. All 12 tests the attempt lost pass. | PROJECT-box-half-open | `presburger::project_each_named` on a tied projection (`Naming::Tied`), new `twins_merged`, `functional`, `guard_atoms`, `numbered`, `con_renamed`; `Hull::asked` | not a cost item at first: the hull of a projection open on one side kept on its finite side only the bound read from the rows. The ledger's case, case 69 of row 1000 of `l01_25_preimage_catalog::s22` (`i <= 7` where the points are `{-6, -5}`), is exact on main cbfd0720 in both transfers (`[-6..=-5]`), so it no longer reproduces as written. The same kind remained in the transfer before: seed 1000 case 1185 gave `i` in `[..=4]` where the one point is `-9`. Cause: the transfer before (`preimage_ref`) writes a shared subterm once at each place it is used, so the formula holds twin definitions (`q2` and `q3` both `abs(i)`, `q9`, `q10` and `q11` all one `if`); `Renamed::of` cannot order the twins and gives `Naming::Tied`, the projection asks its questions with each disjunction kept as a set, `decide` refuses them (`Refusal::Unordered`), and `Hull::tighten` cannot move the finite end. A second cause: where the formula itself is refused but `f && side` has a point, `Hull::has` stayed false, so the end found was not used. Minimized: `l01_38_presburger::omega`'s `twin_absolute_values(1)`, two atoms `q0`, `q1` each `abs(i - 0)` written alike, `q0 + q1 >= 6`, `i <= 11`: main gives `[..=11]`, the points are `[..=-3] ∪ [3..=11]` | fixed (item PROJECT-box-half-open, 2026-11-10). (1) `Hull::asked`: an answer `true` to `f && side` sets `has`, since a point of it is a point of `f`. (2) A tied projection first merges atoms defined alike (`twins_merged`, value numbering): an atom defined by one top-level conjunct that allows at most one value of it for each value of the others (`functional`: an equation; a conjunction with such a part; a disjunction of two such parts separated by a guard the atom is not in, `guard_atoms`) is numbered by its conjunct written with itself as `#` and every other atom as its number, in topological order (Kahn); two atoms with one number are one atom. An atom of a conjunct that defines two atoms or more, of a strongly connected component of two or more (`zedc_solvers::utvpi::components`), a factor of a product, or a projected symbol, is its own number. The merged formula is projected and its answer met with the tied one, so no answer gets wider. Cost: each step O(N) or O(N log N) in the formula's distinct parts (`// Complexity tradeoff:` at `twins_merged`; the naive way compares each pair of definitions, O(A²)); `twins_merged` itself took 10.6 ms on 129 atoms. Answers, every box of the 4000 cases of `s22::random_guarded_chains_*` dumped before and after and each checked against the interpreter at every point in its range: the transfer now unchanged in all 4000; the transfer before 321 boxes narrower, none wider, none leaving out a value the interpreter finds, 122 made exact, none made inexact; case 69 `[-6..=-5]` exact in both. So `s22`'s `GUARDED` counts of boxes the transfer makes exact where the transfer before did not drop by those 122 (368 to 316 in the first half, 393 to 323 in the second), and five boxes of splits over many periods are newly listed as wider than the narrower box before (rows 250, 1000, 1250, 1500 and 2000); no other count changes and no unexplained difference appears. Time: the transfer before over the 4000 cases took 85 s against 46 s on main; the slowest cases 1084 (0.14 to 1.5-2.0 s), 1185 (0.035 to 1.3 s), 2458 (0.12 to 1.2 s), the time spent in projecting the merged formula, which no tie now refuses, and in the tightening's questions. Tests: `omega::twin_definitions_are_merged_before_a_tied_projection` (`twin_absolute_values(1)` gives exactly `[..=-3] ∪ [3..=11]`, equal to the solver's own values of `i` in `-40..=40`; case 1185 gives `(..., -9]` with `-9` its one value) and `omega::twin_definitions_merge_in_time_near_linear` (32 to 256 pairs: 8.7 times the work and 8.6 times the bytes, limit 14.08, load 27 to 45). Red before green: with both changes off, or the merge off, both tests fail; with only the `has` change off, case 1185 gives `[..=4]`. Negative control, run once and not committed: a pairwise comparison of the definitions failed the scaling test at 16.2 times the bytes (limit 14.1; at 16 pairs it passed, 12.5 against 15.4, so the test uses 32). Not fixed, open: (i) twin quotient and remainder definitions (`i == 3 * q0 + q1` with `0 <= q1 <= 2`, written twice) are not merged, since that conjunct defines two atoms (case 3640); (ii) projecting one nested chain of `abs` definitions, with no twins, takes 0.2 s at 16 levels and 3.4 s at 64, about n², a pre-existing cost that twin chains now reach (1.9 s at 32 and 6.6 s at 64, where main refused them in about 47 ms); fixed by PROJECT-abs-chain-quadratic (C47), 0.43 s at 1024 levels and 1.8 s with twins; (iii) ten boxes of the transfer before are marked exact though each holds values that are not points (cases 366, 463, 482, 1264, 1420, 1930, 2087, 2314, 3817, 3897, from 1 to 17 values each), the same with this item's changes off, so not caused here. Fixed by S22-exact-mislabel, row below. |
| S22-exact-mislabel | `preimage_ref.rs` (the transfer before S22a, used by tests only), the arm of `back` for `c - x` with `c` a constant; new `reflect` | not a cost item at first: the arm took the values of `x` from `revision::forward(Sub, {c}, z)`, which caps the pieces of each sign region at the most pieces either operand has in one region and so merges pieces, and the box kept `exact`. Ten boxes of `s22`'s 4000 cases were marked exact while holding values that are not points (cases 366, 463, 482, 1264, 1420, 1930, 2087, 2314, 3817, 3897: 1 to 17 values each, case 3897 `-25..=-9`) | fixed (item S22-exact-mislabel, 2026-11-10). The arm still uses the forward image `r` (no box changes width) but clears `exact` when the holes, `r` minus the exact reflection `c - z`, meet the memoized forward image of `x`. Cost: the reflection O(k) in the `k` pieces of `z`; `minus` and `meet` O((k + f) log(k + f)) at most with `f` the pieces of the image of `x`; the image is memoized by term and binding. The naive way, running the term at each point of the box, is linear in the width, not the pieces (`// Complexity tradeoff:` at the arm). Given up: a box whose holes meet the image of `x` though no input in it takes a value there (an enclosing guard removes it); deciding that needs the back transfer of the holes, two demands at each level of a chain of `c - x`, exponential in the depth. One such box (s22 row 250) was exact because a guard hid a wrong label below it and is now inexact. Exact reflection in place of `r` was tried and not kept: it narrowed 5 boxes that were already correct, an answer change. Scaling test `s22::constant_minus_holes_scale` (`c = 4n + 3`, `z` the pieces `[4j, 4j + 1]` for `j` in `-n..n`, the box exact): 256 to 2048 pieces, 8.7 times the work and 7.8 times the bytes, limit 12.10. Negative control, run and not committed: a quadratic loop in the arm failed it at 31.8 times the work. Answers: every box keeps its width; 12 boxes in `s22` (`GUARDED` rows 250, 1250, 1750, 2000, 2250, 3750 and `ends_of_i64`) and the one guarded box made inexact; `wide_ends` 25 boxes no longer refuted; `exact_oracle` 13 boxes refuted by the interpreter and one found wrong by a dense check made inexact. |

| ID | Where | Class | Status |

| K1 | `types.rs` `Dnf::not` (De Morgan by full product); also reached from `Display for Type` | 2^C | fixed: the tuple and morphism parts are decision lists in one form (`types/bdd.rs`; first reduced ordered decision diagrams with a complement linear in the nodes), so a complement flips the first block's value, O(1), and only literals grow a list, O(log n) expected each; any other union or intersection keeps its operands as an expression, built in constant time, and emptiness walks its paths exactly, expanding first on a subexpression two operands share and passing over paths whose taken atoms are already empty (docs/thresholds.md 9, which removed the 4,096 and 65,536 budgets; Kept). `l01_23_subtyping::scaling::the_parts_scale` (union of C differences `m(i) - m(i+1000)`, whose diagram has 2^C nodes: build about 48 ms at every C from 16 to 128 and complement about 1 µs; old DNF 18 s at C = 12). Since replacement 9 both queries are decided and asserted: `b <: b \| a` 4 µs at every C from 4 to 14 (87 ms at 14, ×4 per +2 C, without the shared expansion), `!b & a` on tuples 1.7 ms at 14 (181 ms without pruning). The walk is checked against evaluation of all 64 assignments on 3,000 random parts with shared operands by `types::bdd::tests::the_paths_of_a_part_are_its_assignments` (catches a shared expansion that pairs a cofactor with the wrong side), and against the value oracle by `l01_23_subtyping::oracle::deep_combinations_are_decided_exactly` |
| K2 | `types/empty.rs` `Search::product`: no pruning of disjoint negatives | n^k | fixed: the product is split outside each negated type in turn into disjoint pieces (outside it first in component `j`, inside it before `j`), and a negated type disjoint from a piece is passed over, with no cap on the splits since docs/thresholds.md 9 (Kept). A union or intersection of many types is joined in pairs (`Type::union_all`, `Type::meet_all`, used in `types/rec/unfold.rs` (was `rec.rs`), `store/product.rs` and `zir/text.rs`), since one at a time `k` tuple types, each ordered after the last, rebuild the diagram `k` times. `l01_23_subtyping::scaling::a_product_covered_by_its_cells_scales` (an `n × n` product less its `n²` cells: 4.3 s at `n = 5` before, 67 ms at 4,096 cells after; the cells built one at a time took 6 s at 1,024 cells, joined in pairs 45 ms), `negated_types_disjoint_from_the_product_are_passed_over` (13 decoys that would make `2^13` pieces, decided both ways), `passing_over_disjoint_negated_types_scales` (2 against 16 decoys over a tuple of bits, `O(k²)` allowed; without passing over, ratio 1,540 to 2,342 against 192) and `a_cell_left_out_is_found`. Mutants caught: no passing over (decoy scaling test), cut answers kept (a memo test, removed with the budget), overlapping pieces (grid tests), a wrong cover test (grid, oracle, `rec`), joining one at a time (grid). A check for a negated type containing the piece was dropped: with disjoint pieces it gives an empty component in every piece, and no test told the two apart Measured over the SCALE-ratio limit, then fixed in K86 (SCALE-fix-kernel): `a_product_covered_by_its_cells_scales` took 12.5 times the work at 512 and 4,096 cells on main's code against the n log n limit 11.7 (the cost was `c log² c` in `Bdd::restrict` from `split_classes`, see K86); now 8.05 times (2026-11-09, load 26 to 39), no longer ignored. |

Output identical to the old on 3,000 random terms and the nested shapes at six widths (26.5 MB). `l01_15_kernel_terms::scaling::the_printer_scales_with_depth` (old: ratio 84.5 for broken nested lambdas, 1.5 s at depth 4,000; head copy alone: ratio 57.7; new: 8 to 12). Broken calls nested in argument position have text quadratic in depth, from their indentation, and are measured by its length. A column is a character, not a byte (TESTS-small-sizes, 2026-11-12: a non-ASCII string literal broke a line that fit; `layout::a_line_is_measured_in_characters_not_bytes`); `fits` counts at most `room + 1` characters of a piece, so the bound holds |

A chain of `D` entries takes `D` Jacobi rounds; since K7 an entry postponed on an undefined key waits on that key and is tried again only once it is defined, so the chain takes `D` attempts under every schedule (old: `D²/2` in rounds, ratio 79 for 1,000 against 8,000 keys) |

The 9,997 pairs of `oracle::the_two_routes_agree_on_*` get the same verdicts as before. Hardness of the refused class: an NFA with states `q`, letters `1..k` and moves `q -a-> q'` maps in linear size to the group `X_q = cons(a, X_q') | ..` (with `| nil` where `q` accepts), and it accepts every word exactly when `list(1..k)` less `X_q0` is empty; the search is polynomial on every input and exact on every difference it does not refuse, so unless P = PSPACE the refused differences are not all decidable in polynomial time. The end family is the standard case: read from the front its smallest deterministic form has 2^n states. Easy differences refused with it, and why each has no simple fast path here: (a) the end family, Empty: reversed by hand (each list `cons(h1, .. cons(hk, t))` mapped to `cons(t, cons(hk, .. cons(h1, nil)))`, a one-to-one map, so emptiness is kept), it still forks at every n 1 to 64, between the lists with no 1 and those with a 1 past place n, both on cycles; (b) the same family with place 1, or place n, left out, Inhabited: reversed by hand, the search finds a value at every n 1 to 64 (skip 1: 2.5 ms at n 8, 17 ms at 64; skip n: 5.5 ms and 120 ms, 22 times, as the front family's cost), but the kernel keeps types as decision diagrams of tuple types and has no word view to reverse, so this is a new construction, valid only where the recursion runs through one component of one atom; queued as REFUSAL-reverse-words, after REFUSAL-front-quadratic, whose cost it inherits. A breadth-first search over pairs of one state of each side is no method: a list that leaves one run of the excluded side may be in another run of it, so its answers need the check of a candidate anyway, and which candidates to try is the open question; trying a candidate's tail as the left side's representative (`nil`) finds `[1]` only, not `[1, 0, ..]` with the 1 at place s > 1, which needs s choices past s forks; (c) the 5 periodic combinations: 2 of them, `(P(6,4) | P(12,4))` less `P(3,1)` and `(P(12,9) | P(12,3))` less `P(6,3)`, are decided Empty exactly by the split of `tuples_on` into its open tuple types if it runs before the open fork refusal (K26), but run there it is order n² on `refusals::a_difference_of_forked_unions_is_refused_in_its_size` (62.1 times the bytes from n 8 to 64; tried, not kept; both are now decided before the fork by the rule on pure cycles, K113); the other 3 meet two periods or subtract two (`((P(4,2) & P(4,3)) | P(12,1))` less `P(4,0)` less `P(6,1)`), the product of cycles, whose general form is unary NFA universality, coNP-complete (Stockmeyer and Meyer 1973), with a shortest value as long as the product of the periods. Still open (REFUSAL-front-quadratic): the lists less a 1 at a place from the front up to n, Empty, cost O(n²) in the decision, 49.6M and 2.29G at n 8 and 64, 46 times, the same on a70df51b; the far family, Inhabited, 69.5M and 2.48G at n 8 and 64, 36 times (154M and 37.6G, 244 times, before). Fixed (REFUSAL-refine-forks): `refine` turned `refuse_forks` off for its own narrowing and left `open_forks` off, so its searches followed a fork, the subset construction: the pairs of `W -> int` (`W` that type) and lists of length 2, less the pairs of `Never ->? (L | (S, L))` and `[1, _]`, nonempty lists or `cons(int, E)` with `E` the end family of n places, took 28.5M, 320M, 3.64G instructions at n 1, 2, 3 for the verdict and 23.1M, 47.4M, 1.58G for `is_empty` on 92e736cd. Now `refine` sets `open_forks` for its duration, so a forked piece counts as inhabited with nothing shown and the box keeps it; the row it ends on is checked as any candidate is: verdict 22.5M, 27.3M, 39.1M, 62.1M, 110M, 211M, 435M at n 1 to 64 (7.0 times from 8 to 64, n^0.94), `is_empty` 54.8M and 396M at 8 and 64. Test `refusals::refining_a_box_follows_no_fork_in_its_size` (n 8 and 64, both variants, and `is_empty`); control, run once, not committed: 92e736cd does not end it within 60 s. Given up: a value only a piece past such a fork shows; the same family without the nonempty lists and with place n left out is Refused(Fork) at n 1, Refused(NoWitness) before (the cause met is now named). The search `refine` calls was superlinear on unions of `k` disjoint pinwheels (27.7 times from k 16 to 128); fixed by the class split, K36. `refine` adds at most the factor of open atoms. Tests on a 2 MiB stack, 100,000 deep: `l01_15_kernel_terms::deep` (lambdas, a left-nested sum, `match` arms, a tuple pattern; the DAG dropped), `l01_23_subtyping::deep_rec` (unions, intersections, complements, differences, tuples, atoms, morphisms; copied, compared, written and checked by `Group::new`). Scaling at 20,000 and 160,000, inputs built before timing, instructions: `Term` copy, compare and `Debug` 7.96 to 8.11 times (copying nested lambdas 1.00, since a body is shared), the DAG compared 8.00 times; `rec::Expr` copy, compare, `Debug` and `Group::new` 7.96 to 8.02 times (limit 24; load 58 to 73). Controls, not committed: a pass over the work stack per step in the copy takes 60.2 times on a left-nested sum (16.1M and 968.8M at 1,000 and 8,000) and 59.8 times on `rec` unions. T2-types-rest, part 2(a): the emptiness search (`types/empty.rs`) runs on heap frames (`frames.rs`, copied from PRE-stack-explicit 5e8e0ee5): its methods are `async`, six start a frame of their own (`empty`, `decide`, `rep`, `member_known`, `tuples`, `morphisms`) and the state sits in a `RefCell` borrowed one statement at a time; calls keep the order of the recursive form. `split_classes` halves on an explicit stack of ranges, low half first; `Simulation` keeps its pairs to compare on a list. Tests in their own binary `deep_search`, on a 2 MiB stack: tuple, atom and morphism types 100,000 deep decided by `is_empty` and `verdict`, deep tuple types compared both ways by `subtype`; scaling at 500 and 4,000 for deciding, the verdict and `subtype` of each shape: work at most 9.1 times, bytes 4.5 to 9.0 times (limit 24; load 70 to 102). Controls, not committed: c277b594 aborts all five deep and tuple scaling tests with stack overflows; a pass over `reps` on each call of `rep` takes 50.0 times on tuples and 51.1 times on atoms. Constant factor (`// Complexity tradeoff:` at `Searching`): 1.2 to 2.5 times the time of c277b594 on types 20,000 deep. Unmeasured and pre-existing: the difference of morphism types 100,000 deep takes about 30 s (time in building types, `bdd::types`, not in the frames). T2-types-rest, part 3: (b) `Debug` of `Type`, `Row`, `Morphism`, `Part` and `Bdd` (`types/debug.rs`) writes from one stack the text the derived `Debug`s wrote, on one line under `{:#?}` too (`debug_text.txt`, written by the old code for 28 sample types, matched byte for byte); the derived `Debug`s overflowed a 2 MiB stack at 2,000 levels of a list type (1,000 of a numeral), the new one prints 20,000 (`l01_22_type_representation::deep_types`). (e) A diagram node or expression of a part reached by two edges or more is written once as `#k=Node(..)` or `#k=Expr(..)` and after that as `#k#` (Common Lisp's print-circle notation), the shared nodes found by one pass with a visited set and numbered from 0 in each part in the order written, so the text stays a function of the part (zedc's query keys read it); an xor chain of n one-tuples has 2^n paths: the old text was 2.9 MB at 12 operands and 183 MB at 18, the new 15.7 MB in 0.2 s at 16,000 on the default stack, scaling at 2,000 and 16,000. (c) `Part::eval`, the diagram walk of `eval3`, `substitute_all` and `Part::restrict` (one post-order `rebuild`, each expression once), `Bdd::restrict`, the atoms of a part and of a diagram (one visited set) and `union_rows` are loops with explicit stacks and memos keyed by id; `settle`, `pins` and `forced` use them. Tests in `types/bdd.rs`: `the_walks_over_parts_nested_deep_run_on_a_small_stack`, 100,000 deep on a 2 MiB stack, and `the_walks_over_parts_scale` at 4,096 and 32,768 (limit 24; load 49 to 51); the deep family is built of pair conjunctions under `Or`, since a chain of literals under `Or` meets the chain merge of `Part::zip`, quadratic by design. Control, not committed, 654e453f at load 67.7 to 69.6: nine of the ten walks overflowed (`union_rows`, `eval`, `atoms`, `forced`, `restrict`, `settle`, and the diagram's `eval3`, atoms and `restrict`); `eval3` of an expression was already a loop. (f) The `l01_23_subtyping` tests `x13`, `scaling`, `rec` and `cells` and the two `forced` tests of `bdd.rs` no longer set a stack size; they passed without it on 654e453f too (load 57.8 to 56.4). (d) The printer (`print.rs`) lays a term out as a flat sequence of tokens, each `Start` linked to its `End`, and the layout, `Display` of `Term` and `Pattern`, `fits` and the render of `pretty` are loops; the text is unchanged, checked against the old printer on 20,000 random terms at eight widths (not committed); `fits` still reads at most the room left, so a render costs O(n * width) plus its output, as before. Tests `l01_15_kernel_terms::deep`: ten shapes 100,000 deep displayed and broken on a 2 MiB stack, and scaled at 20,000 and 160,000 (limit 24); a left-nested sum, `match` arms and `else` branches, broken, put level i at indentation 2i, O(n^2) bytes of text, so they are scaled at unbounded width. The two printer tests of `l01_15_kernel_terms::scaling` run on a 2 MiB stack, not 512 MiB. Control, not committed, 654e453f at load 67.1 to 62.6: 8 of the 10 shapes overflowed, on one line and broken; `let` bodies and indices were already loops. T2-types-rest-4: `Bdd` `apply` and `flip` build each node after its children from an explicit stack, a pair's `hi` before its `lo`, with the memos keyed as before; `walk` and `paths` walk from an explicit stack in the old order and end at the first path where `f` fails; `Part` `not` and `zip`, and `choose`, `choice`, `choice_of`, `same_as_not` and `condition` through them, are `async` methods of `Connect`, each call of `not` or `zip` not answered at once on a frame of its own (`frames.rs`), in the order of the recursion, so the parts made and the ids they take are unchanged: 3,000 random parts gave byte-identical ids, digests, `Debug` texts and paths to the recursive code (control, not committed). Measured on an 8 MiB thread, the recursive code ran and overflowed at: `apply` and `flip` 30,000 and 60,000 deep; `walk` 100,000 and 400,000; `not` of a chain of choices and `zip` of two 6,000 and 10,000. Test `types::bdd::tests::the_connectives_on_parts_nested_deep_run_on_the_default_stack` on a test thread's default stack: diagrams 100,000 deep met, negated and united, paths 400,000 deep, chains of choices 20,000 deep negated and united; `the_connectives_on_parts_scale_by_depth` at 4,096 and 32,768, instructions: meet 7.99 times, complement 8.27, paths 7.80, union of two chains of choices 8.28 (bytes 8.00 each; limit 24; load 20 to 32). Constant factor (`// Complexity tradeoff:` at `Connect`), debug build, chains 500 deep: `zip` 1.4 times the old time, `not` 1.3 to 1.9 times; the diagram loops equal (load 18 to 25). `Debug` of a type writes a `Type` reached by two edges or more once, as `#k=Type(..)`, and after that as `#k#`, numbered with the diagram nodes and expressions from 0 in the order written over the whole text (no longer from 0 in each part); types are told apart by value (digest and comparison, never address), so the text stays a function of the type, and only types that hold other types are numbered (`int` and literals are written in full). Tests `l01_22_type_representation::deep_types`: `(t, t)` doubled 20,000 times (2^20,000 paths) printed on the default stack with 19,999 numbers and one reference each, scaling at 2,000 and 16,000: 8.00 times the instructions and bytes. Control, not committed: the old `Debug` ran into the 60 s timeout on both tests; its text was 3.6 MB at 12 doublings, 57 MB at 16 and 912 MB in 3.9 s at 20 (4 times a level), the new 6.2 KB, 8.0 KB and 9.8 KB. `l01_23_subtyping::rec_order::the_members_of_a_group_are_ordered_in_n_log_n` no longer sets a 256 MiB stack; it passed on the default stack with the old `bdd.rs` too. Instances nested deep in their own arguments (repair DEEP-types-regress): once REC-cycle (K68) freed instances, an `Env`'s `Drop` dropped its arguments, each holding the next instance, a recursion once per level of `Tree(Tree(..))`, which overflowed the 2 MiB stack at 10,000 deep; `Env`'s `Drop` now queues its arguments and members on `rec`'s queue. Tests `a_recursive_type_nested_deep_in_its_own_arguments_is_released` (10,000 deep, freed at the end of its unit and of its thread) and `releasing_a_recursive_type_nested_deep_in_its_own_arguments_scales` (1,000 and 8,000, built and freed on a thread of its own); the old `Drop` overflowed in both. Measured over the SCALE-ratio limit, then fixed in K86 (SCALE-fix-kernel): `the_connectives_on_parts_scale_by_depth` took 14.7 times the work at depths 4,096 and 32,768 (limit 11.0; the meet, on main's code) and `rec_order::the_members_of_a_group_are_ordered_in_n_log_n` 11.8 times at 512 and 4,096 (limit 11.7); now the meet 0.92, the complement 0.98, the union of two chains of choices 8.00, and `rec_order` 8.31 (2026-11-09, load 26 to 39), no longer ignored. |
| K40 | Memo and visited keys that were addresses (ADDR-keys, ledger PTR-memo and LOWER-addr; SYNTHESIS fact 2: memo keys are canonical structure or interned ids, never addresses): `types.rs` `Type::contains` (keyed by `xs.as_ptr().addr()` and the length), `deep.rs` compare and copy (`Items::addr`), `words.rs` `room_to_print` (`Items::addr`), `provenance.rs` `origins` (`Items::addr`), `zir/lower.rs` `body_uses` (`HashMap<*const Term, …>`) | `Type::contains` on a value whose halves share at every level: O(d) for `d` sequences and `2^d` paths with the memo, O(2^d) without; `body_uses`: O(n) over the lambdas bound by nested `let`s with the memo, O(n·depth) without | fixed (ADDR-keys): `Items` carries an `Id` drawn by `fresh_id` as a `Family`'s is (copies share it, an empty sequence has 0), and an atom's field names are a thin `Fields` holding an `Id` with the names, so `Value` stays 56 bytes (test `value::tests::a_value_is_56_bytes` now also holds `Items` to 24 and `Fields` to 8); every memo above keys by those ids. `zir::lower` numbers the subterms of the lowered term by one walk from the root (`Places`: the parts of occurrence `i` are `first[i]`, `first[i] + 1`, …) and keeps each body's uses by its occurrence id; a subterm shared at two places of the term gets two ids, so the numbering is linear in the term's size as a tree, the order lowering already has: a term of `d` levels whose two parts share one subterm costs `2^d` (as it did on main before ADDR-keys; open: hash-consed term ids, so that a shared subterm is numbered and walked once; `Complexity tradeoff:` comment at `Places`). A first version checked each part given against the term's list of parts in a `debug_assert!`, which costs `k` per part of a node of `k` parts and made a match of `n` arms `O(n²)` in dev and test builds (verify run: 4.3, 51.9 and 2252 ms at 1000, 8000 and 64000 arms); it is removed, and `l01_33_lowering::scaling::lowering_a_wide_match_scales` (4000 → 32000 arms, inputs built before timing) passes, while the assert put back, run once as a negative control, fails it at 61.3 times the bytes (269.1 MB → 16.49 GB, load 19). Tests: `l01_23_subtyping::rec::membership_of_a_value_whose_halves_share_scales` (depth 64 → 512, inputs built before timing), `membership_by_sequence_id_is_deterministic` (three allocation orders, depth 60), `l01_33_lowering::ports::ports_are_kept_by_place_not_address` (three allocation orders give one graph), and `l01_33_lowering::scaling::lowering_lambdas_bound_by_nested_lets_scales` unchanged. Negative control, run once and not committed: `Type::contains` keyed by occurrence (parent, column) instead of the sequence's id; both membership tests were stopped at the 60 s limit (load 31.7), against 0.05 s for the scaling test with ids. Cost, inferred and not measured on the K25 benchmarks: one more allocation for each field list built from a `Vec` (the `Names` box beside the `Arc`), shared after; no change in `Value`'s size. Still keyed by address, each a ledger item: `stage.rs` `Reader::ids`, `store/preimage.rs` and `store/preimage_ref.rs` `seen`. `zir/memory.rs` `alone` is keyed by occurrence id since ADDR-memory (K42); `store/cell.rs` `seen` is fixed by ADDR-cell (S35); the Presburger store's keys (`Id`, `BelowKey`, the `seen` sets of `Formula::conjuncts` and `and_held`) are ids since ADDR-presburger (K74) |
| K41 | num-bigint reads a decimal text one word of digits at a time into the number read so far, O(n^2) for n digits; a decimal `m.f` was reduced by num-bigint's Stein gcd of the digits and `10^k`, O(n^2); and `rat(s)` accepted text `String` never writes (`1/-3`, `2r/4r`, `-0`, `1/03`, `1r/3`): `words.rs` `read_rat` and `read_int` (`rat(s)`, `int(s)`), `num.rs` `read_decimal`, `Rat::decimal`, `Rat::in_lowest_terms` | O(n^2) in the digits | fixed (RAT-parse): `read_decimal` reads the text in two halves joined by `high * 10^(L * 2^i) + low` (leaf `L = LEAF_DIGITS`, 512 then, 1024 since KERNEL-leaf-digits), the powers built once by squaring, at the cost of the widest product, O(n log^2 n) with the number-theoretic-transform product of `num/fast.rs` (O(n^1.47) with num-bigint's Toom-3 when first fixed); a decimal is reduced by the valuations of 2 and 5 of its digits (`Rat::over_ten_to`), one division by 5 for most digits; a fraction is accepted only in lowest terms, one gcd that is linear when one part is a word. Tests `l01_18_scalar_interpreter::scaling::reading_a_rat_of_n_digits_scales` (power 1, limit 24; an integer, n digits over a one-word denominator, and a decimal; n = 160,000 and 1,280,000) and `reading_an_int_of_n_digits_scales`: int 88.7 M to 1,917.6 M instructions (21.6 times), 10.5 MB to 236.6 MB allocated (22.6 times), decimal 21.1 times. At 20,000 and 160,000 digits the bytes grow 30 times (Toom-3 scratch grows as n^1.46), which is why the sizes are larger. Negative control 1, num-bigint's own parse (not committed), n = 160,000 and 1,280,000: rat 712.8 M to 44,865.9 M instructions (62.9 times), int 356.1 M to 22,430.3 M (63.0 times), both fail. Negative control 2, the decimal reduced by Stein's gcd (not committed), n = 20,000 and 160,000: 56.6 M to 2,768.5 M (48.9 times), fails. Until NUM-subquad the lowest-terms check of a fraction whose two parts are both wide was num-bigint's Stein gcd, O(n^2): 5.48 M to 214.6 M instructions at 2,500 to 20,000 digits (39 times), 12,389 M at 160,000 (58 times). Fixed (NUM-subquad, `num/fast.rs`): three-prime number-theoretic transform multiplication, Newton division, a binary half gcd and printing by halves replace num-bigint's for wide operands, each beside num-bigint's below a leaf width; the check is one half gcd, O(M(n) log n) = O(n log^2 n), and `read_decimal`'s products are transform products, so reading is O(n log^2 n) (both accepted with a Complexity tradeoff comment at the site; the best known gcd is O(M(n) log n)). `reading_a_rat_of_two_wide_parts_scales` is no longer ignored and runs at 80,000 and 640,000 digits, both above the gcd's leaf of 512 words: work 18.6 times, bytes 15.2 times (22.4 and 19.6 times at 20,000 digits, 21.7 and 17.7 at 40,000, as the leaf's share falls; at 2,500 digits, under the leaf, the bytes grew 75 times across the crossover); load5 about 35. Negative control 3, num-bigint's gcd in place of the half gcd (not committed), n = 20,000 and 160,000: 215.4 M to 12,488.0 M instructions (58.0 times), fails. This also closes K30's open `to_string`, `gcd` and division. Fixed further (RAT-parse-scale): `read_rat` checked a decimal's digits and `Rat::decimal` checked them again; `read_rat` now calls `Rat::decimal_parts`, the reading after the check. The valuations of 2 and 5 (`valuation`) divided the whole number by `p, p^2, p^4, ...` while they divided and then by each power again on the way down, and `Rat::over_ten_to` found the whole powers and multiplied back the part above `k` with num-bigint's `pow` and product (Toom-3, O(n^1.46)); the decimals whose digits hold a high power of 2, of 5 or of both grew 18.7 to 47.5 times from 80,000 to 640,000 digits (probe, not committed, load 16 to 21: `0.<5^n>` and `<5^m>.0` through `rat(s)` 28.7 times, `<2^n 5^(n/2) 7>e<n>` 47.5 times). Now `valuation_upto` takes a cap (`k` for `over_ten_to`, none for an exponent); for `p = 2` it counts trailing zero bits; otherwise it tests `p^(2^i)`, built by squaring, by the remainder of `n` while it divides (O(n log^2 v) for a power `v`: O(n) for the few factors most decimals have), reads the power's binary digits from the top on remainders whose widths halve, and divides `n` once by the product of the powers of its digits, O(M(n)); `over_ten_to` divides out `2^min(v2, k) 5^min(v5, k)` and builds `5^(k - f)` with `num::fast::pow`. So the reduction is at most the order of the reading, O(M(n) log n) = O(n log^2 n), and so is the whole parse (the reading of decimal digits into binary is O(M(n) log n) by the best known method, so O(n log n) is not reached). A first version built every `p^(2^i)` up to the width of `n` before reading the digits, O(M(n)) whatever `v`; it made `literals::rounding_a_literal_of_n_digits_scales` (a mantissa with one factor of 5) grow 27.6 times, through long division of balanced widths, and was replaced by the test while it divides. Test `l01_18_scalar_interpreter::scaling::reading_a_decimal_with_high_powers_of_2_and_5_scales` (since CROSSOVER-bench four tests, `reading_a_decimal_with_{a_high_power_of_5, a_high_power_of_2, high_powers_of_2_and_5, no_high_power}_scales`, at 640,000 and 5,120,000 digits; power 1, limit 24; four families, a high power of 5, of 2, of both, and none, each through `rat(s)` and through `Rat::decimal` with an exponent; n = 160,000 and 1,280,000): 13.8 to 20.8 times in instructions, 10.4 to 23.4 times in bytes (load 22 to 32; both powers 20.8 and 20.1 times the instructions, the literal 23.4 times the bytes, the least margin). At 80,000 the family with both powers grew 28.3 and 32.5 times, its divisions lying where `num::fast::div_rem` takes long division (K30's crossover), which is why the sizes are larger. Negative control 4, the old `read_rat`, `Rat::decimal` and `valuation` (not committed), same test and sizes: fails, `rat(s)` of the high power of 5 at 24.1 times the bytes (1,412.9 M to 26,710.9 M instructions, 18.9 times), the literal 26.1 times the bytes, both powers 26.2 and 27.7 times the instructions. Correctness: `rat_text::a_decimal_is_reduced_as_by_the_gcd_whatever_its_powers_of_2_and_5`, 11 powers of 2 by 19 of 5 by 4 cofactors by 12 point positions, each through `rat(s)` and two exponent forms, against num-bigint's gcd. Peak heap at most 42.1 bits per digit over the families at 13,000 to 1,280,000 digits, below the 64 asked. Fixed further (P14-bigint-parse): the compiler's interval ends (`zedc-int` `Num`'s `FromStr`, used by the ZIR text reader for a class's modulus) were read by num-bigint, O(n^2); they are now read by `num::read_digits` (made public), with num-bigint's signs, `_` and errors, and `read_digits` builds no power of ten for a text of at most `LEAF_DIGITS` digits. Tests `l01_24_refinement_lattices::num_text`: equal values and errors to num-bigint's on every length from 1 to 1,500 digits and eight up to 20,000, with leading zeros, signs and `_`, and on 18 malformed texts; `reading_a_long_decimal_end_scales` (power 1, limit 24, n = 160,000 and 1,280,000) passes, while at 20,000 and 160,000 it grew 30.5 times (Toom-3 products, as above). Negative control, num-bigint's reading (not committed), n = 20,000 and 160,000: 6.1 M to 354.9 M instructions (57.9 times), fails. Writing: `Num`'s `Display` and every other `to_string` of a num-bigint number write by halves from 32 words and divide by Burnikel and Ziegler's recursion from 64 words (num-bigint 0.4.8 `convert.rs` `to_radix_digits_le`, `division.rs` `div_rem_core`), O(M(n) log n) with num-bigint's M; `writing_a_long_decimal_end_scales` (power 1, n = 20,000 and 160,000) passes; negative control, digits taken off by repeated division by 10^19 after num-bigint's reading (not committed): 62.9 times the bytes, fails. The leaf `LEAF_DIGITS`, below which a text is read by num-bigint whole, is 1024 since KERNEL-leaf-digits, set from timings at 32 to 2048 (Crossovers, below). Not fixed, measured; open: SCALE-fix-round-literal. `rounding_a_literal_of_n_digits_scales` allocates 13.2 times the bytes at 2,000 and 16,000 digits, against the n log n limit 11.2 of SCALE-ratio, on this branch and on main's code alike (2026-11-09); ignored. |

| K43 | `store/preimage.rs` and `store/preimage_ref.rs` `Terms::add`, the numbering of a term's parts, kept its visited set keyed by address (`HashMap<*const Term, Tid>`; ADDR-preimage, SYNTHESIS fact 2: memo keys are canonical structure or interned ids, never addresses) | O(distinct parts) with the set; without it, O(paths): `2^d` for `d` levels of `if` whose two branches are one shared subterm | fixed (ADDR-preimage): every `Arc<Term>` child of a `Term` is now a `Shared`, an `Arc` of the term with an `Id` drawn by `fresh_id` (as `Items` and `Family` have; a copy keeps it, `Shared::make_mut` takes a new one), and the visited set is keyed by that id. | K44 | `stage.rs` `Reader::ids`, the map from a part of the term `ends` reads to its number (ADDR-stage, ledger item found by ADDR-keys; SYNTHESIS fact 2: memo keys are canonical structure or interned ids, never addresses) | O(P) for P distinct parts with the part known by identity; O(tree size) with occurrence ids from one walk, `2^k` on k levels of shared `if` arms | fixed (TERM-id): the key is the id of the `zed_kernel::Shared` node that holds the part (`Shared::id`, drawn by `fresh_id` as `Items` and `Family` draw theirs; ADDR-preimage), `HashMap<u64, usize>`, in place of `Part<'t>`, a reference compared and hashed by address (ADDR-stage). The cause was not a long path: a parity is an expression over the `c` tuple types with order `c` distinct nodes, and each of the `c` values was checked on all of it; each new value was also compared with every earlier box. Fix (`types.rs` `Keyed`, `RowIndex`, `BoxIndex`): each tuple type is kept under the values of its column of fewest, where a column holds finitely many scalars and bare atoms, or only tuples of one length, keyed by their first components (to any depth); a tuple reads the tuple types that may hold it by one lookup per component, and is checked on the expression restricted to the smallest range of halves holding them, from a tree of restrictions built on demand (each restriction built once), so about `c log² c`; the earlier boxes read are those kept under its components. | F16b | declare before use (DBU-scope): a use above its definition in a block, a parameter list or a field list | O(uses·bindings) naive | new check, linear from the start: the naive check rescans the block for the binding's line at each use, O(uses·bindings) per block (a chain of n uses in a block of n bindings is O(n²)). `Resolver::order` compares the use's text position with its binder's span, recorded when the binder was made, in O(1), and keeps one entry per binder used too early (`Resolver::above`). `above_errors` then sorts the k early binders, O(k log k), and places each by binary search over the line starts and the block's statements, O(log n) each. Tradeoff: no memory beyond the binder table, the k entries and one list of statement spans per block. Kept, on the error path only: the repair for a reported binder reads the uses inside its definition (`uses_in`, `closed`), O(u log n); definitions of one block do not overlap, so this is linear per block, and only nested definitions that are all reported read a use once per level, O(uses·depth). A program with no error pays nothing. Blocks of 20,000 bindings in order, each used above it, and a parameter list of 20,000 defaults each naming a later one: 8.2x at 8n (limit 10.65); a negative control that rescans the block per use, run and not committed, gave 57.2x. `l01_14_name_resolution::above::checking_the_order_of_a_block_or_a_list_scales` |
| F17 | `Ty::union`/`meet` by deep equality; `derive_into`/`also` note dedup by scan; `ast::args` | O(T²), small | partly fixed, rest kept: `union` and `meet` drop repeated tuples and functions by hash sets, where each was searched for in the list built so far; `ast::args` finds a repeated argument name in a map; `derive_into` was fixed with F19. An `if`/`else if` chain of n branches each giving a different tuple type, debug build: 0.16, 0.50, 2.07 and 11.7 s at n = 200 to 1600 before (×4 to ×5.7 per doubling), 0.16, 0.50, 1.71 and 6.4 s after (×3.6). Kept: what remains is the size of the types themselves. Each `if` of the chain has the union of the tuple types of the branches below it, so the types the checker builds, stores per expression and walks (`pieces`, `closed`, `first_order`, `diff`) total Θ(n²); the same chain with one tuple type is linear (0.67 s at 1600). Removing it needs types whose tuple sets are shared between a union and its parts, with those properties cached, a redesign of `Ty`. The scaling test cannot separate the two (the old chain's ratio between 200 and 1600 is 74, inside the limit of 192 for order n²), so no test was added. `also` still searches an error's notes for the one it adds: an error inside n nested calls of different inferred functions gets n notes, and checking took 0.35, 0.66, 1.33 and 2.68 s at n = 500 to 4000, linear at those sizes |
| F18 | `check`: each run of a signature search checked the functions declared in its body again, so the runs of nested functions' searches multiplied until RUNS stopped them; past depth 6 the rerun with notes then found no error and indexed past the errors (a panic) | 2^depth | fixed, then removed: the signature search, and with it `Undo::Nested` and the `RUNS` budget, no longer exist since commit a494377b (undeclared parameters are union-find classes of carriers); the text below records the fix as made (CX-tradeoff-krows). Inside the outermost search a function's signature is found once per context, which is the context of the search around it and the types of the binders it reads from the function around it (`Tables::outer`); contexts are numbered, so a key holds only those types. A search inside another leaves its writes as one log entry, `Undo::Nested`, that the maps do not hold; finding it again pushes that entry in O(1), and the outermost search makes all the writes once, when it ends. Each key is written only by the search of the innermost function around it, so the order they are made in does not matter (asserted over the test suite). An enclosing search compares nested searches' adoptions by number: each search's adoptions that differ from before it are interned with those of the searches inside it. The rerun with notes starts from the work count the quiet run started from, and falls back to the quiet run's error. The cap on searches is a budget of work, not of runs: the outermost search may check `RUNS` (20000) times its function's size in bytes, each run counted at its function's size less the functions declared in it, whose own searches are counted as they run. The searches inside one function then cost at most `RUNS` times its size however they nest. Two other caps were tried and rejected: one count of runs for the whole unit (never reset, a defect of the old checker: a large program's later functions were left untyped once its earlier ones had spent it), and one count per search, which stops no search of a function nested in others, since the context multiplies the searches through each level (7^depth for parameters with no declared type). The memo and the context numbers are hash maps by key (a kernel type hashes by its digest), not lists scanned for the key, whose cost grew with the square of the contexts of one function. Mutants of the tests: with no memo hits, and with every instance of a search given a new context number, neither test finishes in 40 minutes; with a hit's writes made again, the test of functions beside 20 others fails at ratio 34–36. The searches still multiplied through nested functions until the budget stopped them: for functions nested n deep, each with a parameter of no declared type, all of which the innermost adds, the work spent was 68k, 253k and 1.09M bytes at n = 8, 10 and 12, and reached the budget at n = 16 (11.26M), 24 (17.5M) and 32 (23.7M); 72, 120 and 168 s at n = 16, 24 and 32 in a debug build. This is not a missing visited set: logging every lookup at n = 4, 6 and 8 gives 103, 336 and 953 misses and as many distinct keys, so no search ran twice. The contexts themselves multiply: each search runs its body with `_` and then with type variables (and with carriers if those fail), each run reaches the nested function in a context that is really new, and the searches at the deepest level number 9, 34, 58, 91, 142, 229 and 388 for depths 1 to 7, almost all patterns of `_` and type variables. Fixed for now by a cap, `CONTEXTS` (64): inside the outermost search a function is searched in at most 64 contexts, and in any further one gives `_` for its undeclared parameters and its result, without checking its body. The time is then 0.07, 0.19, 0.44 and 1.05 s at n = 8, 16, 32 and 64. The cap changes results once it binds: at n = 8 `main` is `_` where it was int, since the context typing `x7` as int comes after 64 others; up to n = 6 they are unchanged. The cap, like `RUNS` and `COMBOS`, is a threshold to be replaced by an algorithm with no parameter (the author's direction, 2026-10-30). `l01_16_elaboration::scaling::searches_through_nested_functions_scale` (without the cap it did not finish in 25 minutes). **Replaced** (docs/thresholds.md, replacement 1): the search, its memo, its contexts and its caps are gone; an undeclared parameter is a class of a union-find forest of carriers, and each body is checked once. Functions nested 8, 32, 128 and 256 deep take 8, 23, 94 and 188 ms, and the innermost signature is `(T) -> T` at every depth, where the cap gave `_` from 8 deep; a function of 100, 400 and 1,600 parameters all added takes 42, 171 and 716 ms. `l01_26_type_resolution::scaling::a_function_of_many_untyped_parameters_scales`, `a_chain_of_functions_with_untyped_parameters_scales`. Functions nested 200, 400 and 800 deep: with the memo and its writes made again at each finding, 3.65, 10.9 and 31.4 s (10n² writes; ratio 18.0 over 8×); with the context numbered by the instance of the search around, k+1 searches of the function at depth k; now 2.5, 5.6 and 11.1 s, ratio 8.3. The checker's output (adoptions, calls, fits, signatures, errors) is identical to the old one's on 1,900 random programs of nested functions. `l01_16_elaboration::scaling::checking_and_ordering_nested_functions_scales` |

A rule's reads of its own seed do not mark it, because that seed is finished when it returns; `Parser::low` and `Entry::depth` tell the two apart. As first built, marks stopped at a token's outermost rule, so a rule at an earlier token stayed unmarked and kept a match that a growth had made too short: on some grammars with `head`, it rejected an input or gave a wrong tree (2 cases in `leftrec.txt`). A marked entry now marks every rule on the path. `l01_08_parser::scaling`, three runs, ratio at 8 times the size, limit 24: 32,000 operators 8.6 to 9.6, 16,000 lines of chains 8.9 to 11.0, a long failed alternative 7.2 to 9.0, a lookahead before the recursion 8.9 to 9.9, a finished rung 6.4 to 8.8, a list at a later token 7.9 to 8.2, 64 rungs with the operators on the top rung 12.0 to 12.6. On 205 million random grammar and input pairs, with `head`, `nest`, `HEAD`, lookahead and layers, acceptance and trees equal those of every entry consulting the version, with 0 differences; the same search found 12 differences in 113 million pairs against the first version. Open, a loop in the rule itself: `A = 'x'* 'q' \| A 'x' \| 'x'` is Θ(n²) (2,000 tokens 52.6 to 55.6 times 250, limit 192), since a `*` is no rule and has no memo entry, and a loop's nodes go into its parent's list, so a memo entry for it would still copy them. Moved to a rule of its own it is linear, so LR2 must write such a prefix as a rule. The same holds for a head of a cycle of two or more rules, which stays marked, when a rung above re-reads it. Open, a cycle under a list: a cycle of two or more rules marks every rule that reads it, so a list that reads one after its first item is walked again at each growth at the list's own token: `Items = INT (',' Outer)*` read by `Sum` at each growth is Θ(n²) (2,000 items and operators 60.3 to 62.7 times 250, limit 192; 6.4 to 10.5 times with marks stopping at a token's outermost rule, which is the wrong result above). A rung that is directly left-recursive does not reach this, since its own reads do not mark it. Open: `S = (&E 'x')*`, `E = E 'x' \| 'x'` is Θ(n²) (2,000 tokens 68.5 to 89.1 times 250, limit 192; the paper states the case), since each lookahead grows its own match over the rest of the input and no memo entry covers another start. The grammar has no left-recursive rule yet, so nothing reaches it; `&('{' Item)` (syntax.peg:138) and `!(Name ':') Expr` (:123) need a scaling test after LR2 |

| PA-let-block | `store::product::arms` on a block of d bindings `y_k = y_(k-1) + (if n > k - 1 { n } else { 0 }); x_k = x_(k-1) + y_k` and a test `x_d == 1`, `n: int` (left by PA-plus-if, row F70) | Θ(d^2) in the arms, and the final test read every `n` where none meets it (d ≥ 2) | fixed by PA-let-block (branch wt/pa-let-block). **Two causes, traced.** (1) Cost: `Scope::bind` of a fresh name changed the names but not the caches of the last reduction, projection and enumeration, and the walk reduces a clone of the scope at each test and never the scope it binds in, so each test diffed every name bound since the start against the cache, Θ(k) at the k-th binding (measured: the cache fix alone took the arms at d = 128 from 207 ms to 28 ms). Fix: `Scope::seen_fresh` rebuilds each cache from the names with its own differing entries, so the cache keeps the names' shared nodes and a diff costs the entries that changed, O(changed · log n); a fresh name is mentioned by no conjunct and no written constraint and `bind` reduced its product already. (2) Exactness: a test of a name bound by `let` read the name as an input of its own over its forward interval, so `x == 1` after `y = n + 1; x = y + n` kept every `n`. Fix: each binding of an integer gets a summary (`preimage::LetPa`, `let_summary`) when it is bound: the sum of the summaries of the bound names it adds, kept unsummed, and the summary of the rest of its term over the one input it reads, so a binding costs its own term; `atom_names` then runs `let_preimage`, the backward transfer with the let names read through their summaries (`Walk::pa`, `back`, `fwd`, `clip` and `mentions` read `Tx::lets`), and meets the box into the products. A summary holds while its input is the binding it was made over and its integers lie within those it was made over (`Scope::summary`). The sum is formed when a test reads the name (`LetPa::sum`): the nodes in topological order on an explicit stack, each node's coefficient the sum over its paths, one `Pa::plus` per node; a node formed by an earlier test is added as its sum. `Drop for LetNode` runs on an explicit stack. Tests (load 13 to 27): `follow::a_block_of_sums_of_ramps_scales`, d = 32 and 256, 7.8 times the bytes (9.1 MB to 71.1 MB), limit 24; time of the arms 7.9, 11.8, 22.8, 48.7 and 98.6 ms at d = 16 to 256 (cache fix alone: 3.3 to 53.6 ms, still reading every `n`). `a_block_of_sums_of_ramps_reads_no_n` (`n = 1` at d = 1, none at d = 2 to 48, checked by the interpreter on -30..=30), `a_name_bound_by_let_carries_its_summary` (seven programs exact by the interpreter, three not covered by the summary and checked to keep every reaching `n`), `random_blocks_of_lets_are_read_exactly` (400 random blocks), `a_deep_chain_of_summaries_is_formed_and_dropped` (200,000 bindings; with the default `Drop` it overflows the stack, checked once) and `a_deep_chain_of_summaries_scales` (10,000 and 80,000). Negative control, run once on base 5db9f3b1 and not committed: the scaling test fails with 27.6 times the instructions (191M to 5,269M; limit 24), the arms took 11.0, 26.3, 69.4 and 207 ms at d = 16 to 128, and the three exactness tests fail (every `n`). (b) `product::walk` recursed on the nesting of `let`s: a block of 512 such pairs overflowed the stack of a scaling run, on base and fix alike; fixed by row PA-let-stack. (c) The checker (`check/walk.rs`) binds each name to `Var(name)`, so it gets the cache fix but no summaries (follow-up). Three causes, found by instruction counts per phase. (A) `Scope::bind` made the summary of each integer binding (`stage::free` and `let_summary` over the whole bound term) when it was bound, `O(\|e\|)` a binding. Fix: the summary is made when a test first reads it (`Lazy`, `Making`, `Lazy::get`), in the parts of the scope it was bound in that a summary reads (`Parts`: names, bindings, orders, each an `O(1)` copy of a persistent map; read through `View`, which `Scope` also gives, so no scope is built); a summary that reads names bound before it with pending summaries makes those first, on an explicit stack; a chain of kept `Parts` is dropped by a loop (`Basis`, thread-local `DROPPING`, as `zed-kernel` `deep::free_in`, which is private to that crate). (B) The value of an `if` whose arms are not literals walked the arms and then read the whole `if` again by `Run::forward`, which binds every `let` below again. Fix: one pass (`Run::walk_arms`, `Run::walk_if_value`); each arm's value is found in the arm's scope, and the premises of the tests met inside the `if` (`Run::premises`, a stack in walk order) are dropped from the join (`Product::without`, `Premises::without` in `zedc-lattice` `cell.rs`), which enters only the parts made since the first of them (`Node::newest`), each once, by id. (C) A shown arm no state reaches emptied every name of its scope, `O(n)` an arm, with a fresh name at each level. Fix: `Scope::empty_if_bottom` keeps the last emptied names (`Emptying`, in `Emptied`, shared by the scope's copies) and empties only the bindings whose orders differ, by the persistent maps' difference. (2) The checker records the type of each parameter at each binder bound while a narrowing is in place (`Ck::narrowed_at`, keyed by binder and parameter) and the type before the first narrowing, so a value bound under `is` has a summary over the narrowed type. (3) A summary is a separable sum `Sep` of one summary per input; `Tx::invert_sep` gives each input the Minkowski difference of the tested set and the other inputs' bounds, a sound box. Complexity tradeoff (the part of `Scope::summarize` fixed by PA-walk-multi): `Scope::summarize` keeps one input of a summary in the scope's terms, and `summarize_value` takes the domains of the inputs a value reads itself and of a name read through a summary over one input, not those of every input of the map, so `x_d` of a chain `x_k = x_(k-1) + q_k` with `q_k = n mod 4` is not narrowed by `x_d >= 3 d` (inputs given up: the bounds of `q_1 … q_(d-1)`, which would cost each binder all before it). The questions a part asks are replayed into the part that holds it, so an outer part's trie holds its inner parts' questions too. On the family above this gives (3d^2 + 17d - 6)/2 nodes, exact at d = 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, 96 (20 to 14637 nodes; 161 at d = 8), and 5, 10, 19, 42, 167, 671 ms at d = 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, 96 (debug, load 24). That quadratic is what the output needs (repair 4, after verify 4): `c` is run-stage, so every path stays in the mixed term; the `if` at depth k (k = 0 to d - 1) is reached under k + 1 functions `y + s`, s = k to 2k the sum of the steps above it, and the leftmost literal below it is 1 + s + d - k, so its k + 1 mixed forms differ as terms and no sharing can merge them. The output so holds exactly d(d + 1)/2 distinct `if`s (verifier 4 and repair 4 counted them by structure, hash-consed bottom-up, at d = 1 to 32: equal to d(d + 1)/2 and to the count by id), and (3d^2 + 17d - 6)/2 = 3 d(d + 1)/2 + 7d - 3. The node-count scaling test therefore allows power 2. Complexity tradeoff (stage.rs, `Mixer::eval`): a part is mixed once per distinct sequence of answers its questions get, and each answer is a value computed at build, so a family whose answers differ on every path still has as many mixed parts as answers; a part whose question or answer is not a value cheap to compare (a string not yet written out, a float zero, whose `==` and order disagree, a family or atom) is evaluated as written and numbered exactly, losing the sharing but not the result (`compared`, `Lookup::refuses`). Kernel change: the `Lookup` trait has a new default method `refuses(key)`, asked before the key is compared with keys read so far, since `Text`'s order writes a rope out in full. Closed (STAGE-print, row STAGE-print below): printing a term with shared parts in user-writable syntax within O(n log n) text and time, for `Report::left` and for `Term`'s `Display` and `Debug` in general. Why it is open: Zed has no form that names a part at its first place for later places to use; the forms that can name one are `x = e; body` and a lambda. A `let` placed above every place of a shared part is right only when each name the part reads resolves to one binder at all its places; on the composed family the part below each `if` reads `f`, bound differently on each arm, so it must be a lambda over such names, called at each place with them as arguments (lambda lifting), and the arguments written are the sum over places of the names lifted, which lambda lifting can make quadratic (a part reading k let-bound names at m places of one context and one place of another, (m + 1) k names on about 2k + m nodes, unless the m places share one `let` inside that context). An O(n log n) printing would need both: a `let` per part and context where the binders agree, and a lambda where they differ, chosen without blowing up either; no such algorithm was in the codebase; STAGE-print gives one, a part that reads such names taking them as one value, so each place passes one argument. Fixed (STAGE-store-probes): the replay above, at `Mix::Store`, asked again every question of each part held in the part being stored and copied it into the outer part's trie, so d nested held parts over a body asking p questions asked and kept `O(d * p)`: on n calls of a chain of n under n nested `if`s whose two arms are one part, 1383 ms at n = 400 when the calls are left to run and 9369 ms when they end (test profile, load 36 to 53), and 61.1 times the bytes at n = 400 and 3200. A memo per (part, question) would still hold d * p entries, so the design is different: a part's record (`Leaf::asked`) is a list of `Item`s, each a question with its answer or the leaf of a part held in it, and an outer part keeps one `Item::Part` per held part, not its questions; its trie has a `Node::Part` edge keyed by that leaf. The scope keeps a stamp per name, the count of entries pushed before its innermost entry (`Scope::stamps`, in `Maps`), and a part takes a held part's leaf whole (`Mixer::take`, `outside`) when the names that part asks of have the stamps they had where the outer part was entered, compared as one restricted map; otherwise it takes the held part's items one by one, each leaf once (visited set), keeping an answer whose name's stamp is unchanged and asking the others again. `Mixer::recall` walks a trie on an explicit stack, asking through `Mixer::answer`, which records nothing, and keeps the leaf each tree's walk reached by its root and the stamps of the names it asks of (`Mixer::recalled`), since what a name answers depends only on its entry; so the parts around a part do not walk its tree again under one scope, and each question is asked once per scope entry of its name. Now (load 28 to 33): 14.6, 142.5 ms at n = 400, 3200 when the calls are left to run, 33.3, 286.3 ms when they end, and 35.6, 328.1 ms when each arm also binds a name over the part; on the same family with each arm rebinding `f1`, a name the body calls, 21 and 50 ms at n = 400, linear in n, and its printed output equal to the tree form's at n = 1 to 8. Output unchanged: the stage groups' output, 400 random units, 400 random units under shared `if`s and 54 units of these families print byte-identical text and node counts before and after.
