| STAGE-joined-eq-build | `zed-kernel` `text/names.rs` (`Names`, `Name`: exact names of texts), `zedc-stage` `stage.rs` (`Key`, `Canon`, `Namer`, `compared`) and `zed-kernel` `eval.rs` (`Lookup::keeps_answers`) | before: a call at a joined string was staged as written (part 1 of STAGE-joined-eq), since comparing two keys read the strings in full, and a doubled join of 2^40 bytes cannot be read. A tuple key was compared as a tree, so a tuple holding itself doubled d times was read 2^d times. Now a key is compared by its canonical form: a string by its exact name, a tuple or keypath by a number interned from its parts' forms, each shared tuple read once. Naming a text of n nodes and length N costs O(n log N) dictionary steps (each join re-parses a window of constant size at each of O(log N) levels) | fixed. Method: signature encoding with deterministic coin tossing (docs/joined-strings-study.md; Mehlhorn, Sundar and Uhrig 1997; Alstrup, Brodal and Rauhe 2000; Nishimoto et al. 2016): each level is run-length encoded, 4 coin-tossing rounds and recolor passes for 5, 4 and 3 give 3 labels, and a block starts at each strict local maximum; a start at i reads entries i-8 to i+4 (CL = 8, CR = 4), a block holds at most 6 entries (5 at a string's true end), and a summary keeps K = 17 entries at each end of a long middle. A name is equal for equal strings by construction and different for different strings because the dictionary is read backward (a name's string is a function of the name). Cross-review round 1 (Opus 5.5, gpt-6.1-sol, a CD experiment): CR = 3 is wrong for wide ids and K = 16 fails with CL = 8, both shown by witnesses now kept as tests (`a_block_start_reads_8_symbols_left_and_4_right`, `a_block_at_the_true_end_may_hold_5_symbols`); CL = 7 would suffice, 8 is kept as the proved bound. The CD seat's best candidate (one coin-tossing round, 0.335 against 0.929 million dictionary calls on its benchmark) has blocks of up to 63 entries for 64-bit ids (measured) and an unsafe K, so it is not adopted. Leaf summaries stay memoized (O(leaf) memory by a constant factor; bounds repeated work). Stage: `Key` holds the canonical form (`Canon`: a value, a string's name, a sequence's number) and compares by it alone; `Namer` reads a value on an explicit stack, keyed by `Value::shared_parts` ids (never reused, sequences never changed in place), so a shared tuple is read once; `compared` has a visited set by the same ids. Kernel: `Lookup::keeps_answers` (default false), true for the stage's port, so `ask_port` does not keep the port's answers in `World::reads`, a `BTreeMap<Value, Value>` that compared joined strings by bytes and hung the staging tests once joins were keyed by answers. Tests: `text::names::tests` (every string over {a, b} up to 9 bytes and every split; random and adversarial joins against byte comparison; Zimin words built both ways; texts doubled to 2^40 bytes; `naming_n_and_8n_nodes`, 200 and 1600 blocks, 7.8 times the instructions and bytes, load 46); `l01_28_staging::dag::calls_at_joins_of_100_and_200_bytes_stage_alike` (short, long and a literal of 200 bytes mix alike), `a_call_at_a_long_join_is_mixed_once` (a string doubled 62 times), `calls_at_a_doubled_tuple_stage_alike` (a tuple doubled 40 times), `keying_a_call_at_a_join_and_a_tuple_of_n_parts_scales` (n = 1000 and 8000, `check_order` power 1: 8.4 times the instructions and bytes, load 50). Negative controls, each run once and not committed: CR = 3, the witness test failed; no visited set in `compared` and no `seen` in `Namer`, the doubled-tuple test was killed at 60 s; each tuple printed while keyed, the scaling test failed at 59.2 times the bytes (limit 11.4); byte comparison of 5 * 2^40-byte texts killed at 60 s, naming them 0.88 s. Open (STAGE-byte-keys): the Trick's `passed` set and the Specializer's `calls` and `cases` sets in stage.rs, and `World::reads` for ports other than the stage's, still order values by bytes |

| ENDS | `stage::ends`, the form rule that a term ends (build stage, `store/preimage.rs`, `store/product.rs`, `mutate`): read as a tree with the names bound around each place, so a chain of k `if`s whose two arms hold one shared part cost 2^k | was O(2^k) on k levels of shared arms | fixed: each distinct part (one `Shared` node, known by its id, row K44) is read once by an explicit stack, after its own parts, and gets what it needs of the names bound around it: none (it never ends) or the set of names it calls that must be free or bound by `let` to a function that ends; a binder reads that set, so one part shared under two bindings of a name still gets two answers. Not fixed: arrows that all offer one piece of both the slot's parameter and its result, O(n·m); complexity tradeoff at `every_arrow_fits`: the general question is a containment join, the complement of Hitting Set, with no n^(2-e) algorithm expected (Hitting Set conjecture, Abboud, Vassilevska Williams and Wang, SODA 2016). Refused although rule 6 accepts them, complexity tradeoff at `covered`: arrows that cover only across two or more parameters (DNF tautology, coNP-complete), arrows whose parameter holds a variable or the unknown, and overlapping arrows whose results only intersect within the slot's result (the all-subsets condition of Frisch, Castagna and Benzaken); tested by `l01_26_type_resolution::fits::arrows_that_cover_only_across_two_parameters_or_by_intersected_results_are_refused`. AND-fns-rule6 verify: two defects fixed. (a) Soundness: `covered` took an arrow whose parameter type held a variable inside a tuple, so `(x: (T,)) -> String for T in int | f64` fitted `(x: (bool,)) -> String` (the union bound `T` to `bool` and no bound was checked); now the type must be closed at every depth (`Ty::closed`), and function types, read as variables, take no part either; tested by `fits::an_arrow_with_a_variable_in_a_tuple_takes_no_part_in_a_cover` (the negative control, the old top-level check, fails it). (b) Cost: `covered` ran the index and compared every parameter once for each parameter left out, the square of the width; now one `ArrowIndex::covering` per slot arrow and one pass per arrow (`sole_miss`): `scaling::a_function_of_many_parameters_that_misses_one_scales` (w = 100 and 800; 7.8 times the bytes; the code before, 38.8 times at load 22) and `scaling::an_overload_of_many_arrows_that_cover_a_slot_together_scales` (6.5 times). The differential tests now also check on the wider shapes that the index keeps every arrow that fits or may cover, and that the verdict is the same with the arrows of the function reversed, rotated and shuffled and those of the slot reversed (negative controls, not committed: dropping the arrows whose results need no key, dropping one result key list, and allowing no missed parameter each fail both tests; trying only the parameter the first arrow misses fails the order check). Not fixed, tradeoff at `covered`: arrows that all offer one piece of the slot's parameter are each compared with each slot arrow, O(n·m) (63.3 times the bytes at n = 100 and 800 for `(x: #c | #ai) -> String` against `(x: #c | #ak | #a(k+1)) -> String | #zk`). Shared-piece probe 7.9 times at load 9. AND-fns-rule6b: of the three refused cases, parts of the second and third are now built, and each refusal has its own message, naming the arrow and the reason (`check::ty::refused_cover`, one pass over the arrows on the way to an error, through `why_unfit` in `Ty::refused` and the named-function message). Built: a function type, a rigid variable or the unknown at the cover parameter (`binds_nothing` replaces `Ty::closed` there; `sole_miss` is now `part_of`), and the intersection form `check::ty::met`: the arrows that take all of the slot arrow, or all that the arrows within its result leave of one parameter (`Ty::diff`), are intersected as kernel types, one comparison per candidate. Refused, each its own message: a cover split across two or more parameters (coNP-complete); an arrow that would bind its own variable at the cover parameter (the product of the bounds); and arrows outside the result that meet within it only on different sets (as hard as Orthogonal Vectors with one parameter of atoms; Williams, TCS 2005, under SETH). Soundness hole fixed: `bounds_hold` took a bounded variable bound to values of several carriers, so `add(x, y) = x + y` fitted `(x: int \| f64, y: int \| f64) -> int \| f64` and failed when run ("Add applied to `int`, `f64`"); such a binding now needs one place an argument gives, outside function types, and none the arrow takes inside one (`one_place`). Tests: `l01_26_type_resolution::fits` (one test per case with its message and near miss, the hole and its near miss `inc(x) = x + 1n`, case 4); `check::ty::tests::a_fit_of_small_types_is_a_cover_of_their_values`, a new differential test against the values of small types (4000 cases; every fit must be a cover); the reference of the two index tests now includes `met`. Scaling (n and 8n, 24 allowed): `scaling::many_arrows_whose_results_intersect_within_the_slots_scale` (8.2 times the bytes at 100 and 800), `many_arrows_whose_results_meet_only_on_different_sets_are_refused_in_linear_time` (n = 400 and 3200; 8.1 times at 100 after the fix; the negative control, `arrow_text` copying the whole signature for each arrow it names, 29.9 times at 400), `an_overload_with_a_function_arrow_covering_a_slot_scales` (6.5 times), `a_bounded_variable_at_many_parameters_is_refused_in_linear_time` (7.8 times). Negative controls, not committed: `met` off fails the intersection test and its scaling test; `met` accepting any nonempty set fails the value test and the first index test; `one_place` off fails the hole test and its scaling test (not the value test, whose small types bound no variable of the given side); function types barred from covers fail the function-type test and its scaling test. AND-fns-rule6b verify#1: `meet_within` intersected kernel results only, so results that hold a function or a rigid variable were refused with the Orthogonal Vectors message, though rule 6 gives the fit and it is linear (`((x: int) -> String \| #a) & ((x: int) -> String \| ((y: int) -> int))` at `(x: int) -> String`). It now intersects the kernel parts exactly, leaves out a function piece where another result holds no function and a rigid variable where the carriers the other results may hold miss its bound (one pass from each end), and requires every other piece to be within the slot's result (Complexity tradeoff at `meet_within`: `(U,) \| String` and `(bool,) \| String` are refused). The messages printed the slot's variables as `_`; `text_at` names them and the rigid variables made from them. Tests: `fits::results_that_hold_a_function_or_a_variable_are_intersected` and `fits::a_refused_cover_names_the_expected_types_variables` (both failed before the fix); `check::ty::tests::a_fit_at_a_bounded_variable_is_a_cover_of_its_values` (4000 cases; 400000 over four other seeds, not committed, gave no unsound fit); `scaling::many_results_that_hold_a_variable_or_a_function_meet_in_linear_time` (7.7 times the bytes and 7.8 the work at 100 and 800; the negative control, the carriers of the other results read again for each result, 43.4 times the bytes). AND-fns-rule6b verify#2: the rule `meet_within` applies to a rigid variable is that each carrier of its bound is missing from some other result (the carriers every result but one may hold), which DESIGN, the message and the doc comment had stated as "the carriers another may hold miss its bound"; the three now say what the checker does, and `fits::results_that_hold_a_function_or_a_variable_are_intersected` holds a fit only that reading gives (`T | #a`, `int | String`, `f64 | String` at `String`), which failed on a control that drops the variable only where one other result misses its whole bound. `check::ty::tests::a_fit_with_functions_in_the_results_is_a_cover_of_their_values` checks the function path against values: two function types and one function value in both, at parameters and in results, and an own unbounded `T` bound to the slot's functions (4000 cases: 473 fit by one arrow, 165 by intersection with a function in a result, none unsound); a control that drops every function piece fails it at case 2, and the older value tests pass that control. Both value tests now check the verdict in every order of the arrows, which a control reading only the carriers before each result (a sound, order-dependent mask) fails at case 3500. The scaling test catches a quadratic re-read that allocates (43.4 times the bytes) but not one that re-reads the masks without allocating (passed at 100 and 800: the k² mask operations are below the work of checking k arrows); the pass from each end is linear by reading. CHECK-scaling-share: that test now times the checker alone (it was 30% of what was timed), and the non-allocating re-read of the masks, K times for each result, still passes it below K = 128 at 100 results, below K = 32 at 400 and below K = 4 at 3,200 (3.2 s): checking costs about 160,000 instructions a result and a re-read about 3 a pair, so K = 1 would need about 12,800 results. `check::ty::Meet` (`#[doc(hidden)]`) holds results built before the timing, and `scaling::many_results_that_hold_a_variable_meet_in_linear_time_alone` times `meet_within` alone on 1,000 and 8,000 results `U \| String \| #bi` (0.09 s): the re-read fails it at K = 1 (37.3 times the work, 17.2 million to 641 million instructions) and so does the copy of the masks (29.3 times the bytes). Its results hold no function, so the function path is timed only through the whole check. |

| F89 | `check` (CHK-held-cascade): a function held at the bottom of n nested tuples, written in one expression, put in a tuple by n bindings, or by n nested calls of a function that wraps its argument in a tuple | was n errors, each with a derivation O(n) notes long, so O(n^2) text, and O(n^2) time from three walks of the whole type at each level: `Ck::finish` named and solved the variables of each binding's type (`Ty::vars_in`, `Ty::replace`), `Ck::meet` and `bound` did so at each call, and `Ty::kernel` walked the argument of each call to the function at its bottom; `Ty::write` recursed once a level and overflowed a 2 MiB stack below 8,000 deep, as did the drop glue of the rows | fixed: a function held in the row of a tuple expression is reported at that tuple, once; a row records whether a tuple expression checked it (`RowData::checked`, `Row::of_data`) and the first function it holds that none did (`RowData::unchecked`, `Ty::unchecked_function`), which `Ck::data` reports in place of every held function, so a value that flows through more tuples, bindings or calls meets the same function and is not reported again. Each row keeps the variables it holds at any depth, inside functions and payloads too (`RowData::vars`, a `VarFacts` made in `Row::made` from the components' rows and signatures, merged small into large; `Ty::var_facts`), so `Ty::replace`, `Ty::renamed` and `Ty::subst` keep whole a row that holds none of the variables replaced (`Row::holds_any`), and `Ck::solved`, `Ck::shown`, `Ck::settled`, `bound` and `Ck::meet` read the variables at the cost of the outer level. `Ty::kernel` refuses a type whose rows hold a variable, the unknown or a function at the outer level (`Row::open`, `RowData::held`). | CK-every-bit | replacing variables in rows whose variables cover every bit of `VarBits` (`Ty::replace`, `Replacer::known_row`, `BindKeys::meets`; found by CK-data-memo, F93) | O(n^2): n rows `ri = (c, $(128i), ..., $(128i + 63))`, with `c` the shared row of `$0, ..., $63`, in one row `t = (r1, ..., rn)`, and n replacements of `t`, each binding a class `$(128j + 64)` that no row holds. Each row's classes are on every bit and its range runs from `$0` to `$(128i + 63)`, so the bits and range of `VarBits` say that every row from `r(j+1)` on may hold the bound class, and each replacement enters and rebuilds those rows (`Row::replaced`, a new row with a new number even when nothing changed) and fills its own map of rows made: O(n) per replacement. The same with names: n rows of 300 names each, which cover the 64 bits of names, and n replacements of names no row holds. Test `l01_26_type_resolution::scaling::replacing_variables_no_row_holds_in_rows_on_every_bit_scales`, `#[ignore]`: 52,257,336 to 3,225,700,376 bytes (61.7 times) at 40 and 320 rows of classes (2026-11-09 after the rebase onto main, load1 13; 60.1 times on 2026-11-08); 40,441,344 to 2,412,043,840 bytes (59.6 times) at 20 and 160 rows of names (2026-11-08, load1 12 to 22). The exact sets each row kept before CK-data-memo answered each replacement at `t`, but an exact set per row is the transitive closure of the DAG of rows, O(n^2 log n) on rows of disjoint sets (F93). Approaches weighed (CK-data-memo impl#cont, 2026-11-08): exact sets per row (F93's quadratic); a set built for a row when first asked (the same closure, paid on demand). Ruled out by argument, not measured: more bits or a finer range, since the family can cover any fixed number of bits. Wanted: a test of whether a row holds a bound variable that is exact or wrong only on a bounded share of rows, at O(log n) per row and per replacement, for example an index from each variable to the rows that hold it directly, walked upward to the rows that must be rebuilt | open: hard-algorithm cross-review XR-algos. | F103 | the file import graph tool (`crates/zed-tools/src/imports.rs` and `imports/lex.rs`, `imports DIR`, S.1f and S.1f-rest): lexes each file once with its matching brackets, resolves each `use` leaf (depth first over the bindings a path goes through, each pushed once and its path advanced, never restarted) and each qualified path through hash maps of child modules, items and bindings; then types the receiver of each method call in one pass over each file (the names bound so far kept in a log with a hash map from name to its latest binding, undone at each scope's end; a pattern destructured with an explicit stack), a call into an `impl` block written in another file than its type being one import; then Tarjan's algorithm with an explicit stack and one breadth-first search per component for its shortest cycle | O(bytes + files + e log e), e the imports: every resolution step and every typed call is one hash lookup, each binding is logged and undone once, each file's imports are sorted once, Tarjan's search is O(n + e), each component's search visits its own files and imports once. A call whose receiver is not typed imports the file of a method of that name written apart from its type, and open to the call, only when the calling file imports the file of that type by a path or a typed call (TABLE-short-scan:impl#fix; the name alone drew false cycles in zed-kernel through `Vec::is_empty`). Method (`untyped_imports`, IMPORTS-untyped-join): the calls are grouped by pair of calling file and name; each pair is joined once with the type files of that name from the smaller side (the calling file's imports or the name's type files), one hash lookup each; of each file's methods of one name and type file only those open to a module no other one's holds are kept; a method open to a module that holds the calling file's own module is found by one binary search over the modules of that name and type file, sorted by number with the nearest one around each (`Opens`), and is open to every call of the pair; a method open to a module written inline in the calling file is kept by that file, visited by that one pair only, and reaches the calls in the module's range of numbers (two binary searches over the pair's calls sorted by module, a range minimum for the earliest call, a sort of the ranges for the count). Cost O(u log u + p √p + t log m + h), u the calls, p the pairs, the imports and the type files of the names together, t the type files the pairs find, m the methods written apart, h the imports drawn before merging. The per-call loop this replaced walked every method of the pair's type files once per call: k^2 for k calls of a name in one file and k methods (`many_calls_of_a_name_cost_no_more_than_their_methods`). Upper bound of the join: a pair (c, x) costs min(|imports of c|, |type files of x|). If x has at most √p type files the pair costs at most √p, at most G √p over the G pairs; otherwise x is one of at most √p names with more (their type files sum to at most p), so c has at most √p such pairs, each costing at most c's imports, at most I √p over the I imports; in all at most (G + I) √p ≤ p^1.5. Lower bound (proof that no near-linear method exists unless triangles can be found in near-linear time): take a graph with m edges; detecting a triangle in it reduces in O(m) to a tripartite graph with parts A, B, C (three copies of the vertices, each edge copied between each two parts), which has one exactly when the graph has one. Build a crate: a file `a{i}.rs` for each vertex of A, a file `d{k}.rs` holding `pub struct T{k};` for each vertex of C, and a file `e.rs`; for each edge (a_i, b_j) the line `let z = other::make(); z.n{j}();` in a function of `a{i}.rs`; for each edge (a_i, c_k) the line `use crate::d{k}::T{k};` in `a{i}.rs`; for each edge (b_j, c_k) the method `pub fn n{j}(&self) {}` in `impl crate::d{k}::T{k} { }` in `e.rs`; `lib.rs` declares the modules. The receiver `z` is not typed, `pub` opens each method to the crate, and `e.rs` is no calling file, so the call of `n{j}` in `a{i}.rs` imports `e.rs` exactly when `a{i}.rs` imports some `d{k}.rs` whose `T{k}` has a method `n{j}` written apart: exactly when a_i, b_j, c_k is a triangle. So the tool's count of untyped calls that import a file (`unknown_calls`) is above 0 exactly when the graph has a triangle. The crate has n = O(m log m) bytes (each name has O(log m) digits) and is written in O(n). Hence (1) an O(n^(1+o(1))) method, O(n log n) included, detects a triangle in an m-edge graph in m^(1+o(1)) time, against the Triangle Conjecture, verbatim: "There is a constant δ>0, such that in the Word RAM model with words of O(log n) bits, any algorithm requires m^(1+δ-o(1)) time in expectation to detect whether an m edge graph contains a triangle" (Abboud and Vassilevska Williams, "Popular conjectures imply strong lower bounds for dynamic problems", FOCS 2014, 434–443, doi:10.1109/FOCS.2014.53, arXiv:1402.0054, Conjecture 3); (2) a combinatorial method in O(n^(1.5−ε)) detects a triangle in a graph of N vertices and at most N^2 edges in O(N^(3−2ε+o(1))) time, combinatorially, which gives a truly subcubic combinatorial Boolean matrix product (Vassilevska Williams and Williams, "Subcubic equivalences between path, matrix, and triangle problems", FOCS 2010, 645–654; J. ACM 65(5), 2018, doi:10.1145/3186893), against the conjecture that "any combinatorial algorithm requires n^(3−o(1)) time in expectation to compute the Boolean product of two n×n matrices" (Abboud and Vassilevska Williams, Conjecture 4): so the join's p^1.5 is the best order a combinatorial method is known to reach, up to factors n^(o(1)). The best known method, by fast matrix multiplication, is O(m^(2ω/(ω+1))) ⊂ O(m^1.41) (Alon, Yuster and Zwick, "Finding and counting given length cycles", Algorithmica 17 (1997) 209–223, doi:10.1007/BF02523189); it gains under 0.09 in the exponent at the constant factors of fast matrix multiplication and is not used. Sources: the two conjectures and the statements of the other two results are quoted from the arXiv LaTeX source of Abboud and Vassilevska Williams (intro.tex, conjecs.tex: "The best known algorithm for triangle detection relies on fast matrix multiplication and runs in time O(min{m^1.41, n^ω})"; "any truly subcubic in n combinatorial algorithm for finding a triangle can be converted to a truly subcubic combinatorial algorithm for BMM"); the four DOIs were checked at Crossref; the texts of the other two papers were not opened. Given up: a call whose type's file is reached only through another file, or made in the type's own file, is left out (cycles through it unreported); the reachability of the type's file would cover the first at O(files × imports) | fixed. Now one `Cones` per unit and one closed term per binding from it, and each row's failure found by a range of a `BTreeMap` of the failures: O(n log n) plus the cones of the bindings. A unit whose bindings form a chain, `x_i` reading `x_(i-1)`, then still cost O(n²) (measured by ORACLE-chain: 58.5x the bytes at 500/4000 in the interpreter, 59.3x natively at 25/200), as each binding ran alone over a cone of size i. Where that run stops, or a binding the checker typed `_` is a function, `oracle::Runs` walks the definitions in the unit's order: those that read a known stop take its error unrun (one visited set for all walks, each a stamp), the rest run in prefixes of 1, 2, 4, … definitions and a halving finds the first that stops; the bindings that ran get their values from one tuple, split in halves where it gives no tuple of data. That cost O((n + s·F) log n) for `s` stops reaching `F` definitions with a function component, which have no literal and were bound again in each run (measured by ORACLE-stop-share: 67.7x the bytes at 100/800). Now, by ORACLE-stop-share, the walk ends at a run after a stop that stops and binds again such a definition, which a run before that stop bound: each binding not known by then is listed in the report as not compared, with the reason, and the walk costs O(n log n) (Complexity tradeoff comment at `Runs`; the complete solution, an engine environment kept from run to run, needs both engines changed). Negative control, run once and not committed: the printer of main, through `zedc run`, writes 2,917, 23,103 and 5,247,542 bytes for the doubling tuple at n = 4, 8 and 16 (227 times from 8 to 16), against 1,973, 3,167 and 5,676 bytes with the fix |

## ZIR, native code and runtime

| ID | Where | Class | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z1 | `zir/lower.rs`: an effectful `let`-bound lambda is inlined at every call, recursively | c^k nodes | fixed: a function that uses a port and whose name occurs more than once is one `lambda` node whose region takes and returns the ports' states, and each call is an `apply` that threads them (DESIGN L1.31, L1.33); a name used once is still inlined; `l01_33_lowering::scaling` (a chain of k functions each calling the one before twice: 3k+1 nodes, 25 ms at k = 800 in release; the old code runs out of memory at k = 16, and inlining every call gives 65,536 nodes there) |
| Z2 | `Lower::add` canonicalizes and encodes the whole subtree of each new node | O(n³) | fixed: a node's key is hashed from its normal-form operation, inputs and outputs and the keys of its regions (`canon::node_key`, `region_key`), so each node is hashed twice, when it is added and when its region closes; `l01_32_canonical_zir::fuzz::the_key_agrees_with_the_address` (catches region keys left out), `l01_33_lowering::scaling::lowering_a_deep_nest_scales` (`if` nest of 800: 28 s → 32 ms in release, old ratio about 8 per doubling) |
| Z3 | `zir/canon.rs` restarts from the top after every rewrite | O(k²) | fixed: every rule acts on one edge or one pattern alone and the binder rule's hint is removed by the hints rule, so `canonicalize` normalizes each edge and each pattern in one pass; `step` stays for the termination tests; `l01_32_canonical_zir::fuzz::the_one_pass_normal_form_is_the_one_the_steps_reach` (300 random graphs). The cost within one edge was the swap loop, fixed by Z18 |
| Z4 | `memory.rs` planner: `consumes` and `Uses::of` recomputed down nested branches | O(k²·d²) | fixed (T12-Z4). Since lowering carries each name into a region once (Z9b), k is the number of names a branch uses; the planner was still of order k·d² on a nest d deep, since each region asked again whether the regions under it consume each argument (instructions, nested `if`s reading 4 names: 156, 648, 2,702, 11,116 and 46,812 M at d = 100 to 1,600, 4.1 times per doubling; k = d: 13 to 14 times per doubling). The planner now numbers each region occurrence once, by its parent occurrence, node and region index in a map, and keeps by that number whether it consumes each argument, its uses, how a lambda body takes its parameters, and which lambda a captured argument is (with each step of the chain followed kept too), so each question is answered once: 4.5, 9.4, 20.0, 45.1, 111.0, 311.7 and 1,007 M at d = 100 to 6,400. What remained above linear was the paths that named the plan's regions, O(d) bytes each and O(d²) in all: with the paths replaced by a constant, the work doubled exactly with d (30.0 to 239.6 M at d = 800 to 6,400). T14-paths removed them: the plan's regions are numbered in preorder, each linked to the region holding it and each node to its regions, and a path is printed for a message only; at d = 200 and 1,600 planning the 4-name nest takes 8.0 times the instructions (7.72 and 61.7 M) and 8.0 times the bytes (1.65 and 13.2 MB), against 11.8 and 24.0 times with the paths. Tests `l01_34_memory::chains`: nested `if`s reading 4 names (d = 200 and 1,600, 11.7 times, instructions only while the paths remained; instructions and bytes since T14-paths) and n names (n = 100 and 800, 7.6 times), a function called twice at each of d nested arms and lambdas (10.95 and 10.4 times), and a chain of functions each calling the one before twice (24 and 192, 7.6 times, `f0` borrowed); a borrowing or consuming leaf at depth 4, and two wrappers sharing one body (design review Q10). Negative control, the old planner, run once and not committed: 71.2 times on the 4-name nest, 60.2 times the bytes on n names, 24.4 times on nested lambdas; the call chain was linear before (8.1 times) |
| Z5 | planner finds an edge's node by `rposition` | O(n²) per region | fixed: the region's node bases are sorted, so `src` finds the node by binary search (`partition_point`), O(log n). Covered by `l01_36_cranelift::scaling` (Z14); no size run there shows the old cost apart from the others |
| Z6 | `lower.rs` `lookup` scans the whole scope | O(N·S) | fixed: `Lower` keeps the positions of each name in a map beside the scope, updated as names are bound and unbound, so `lookup` takes one map read. A chain of n `let`s, each reading the outermost name, debug build: 96 ms, 0.24, 0.79 and 2.75 s at n = 2000 to 16000 before, 75, 121, 201 and 434 ms after. Test `l01_33_lowering::scaling::reading_a_name_bound_far_out_scales`, ratio 38 before, passes after. Since Z12 the scope is a persistent map, so it has no positions to keep |
| Z7 | captures not deduplicated; merged by `contains`/`position` | O(raw·unique) | fixed: `node` merges the regions' captures through a map from each source edge to its position, so each raw capture costs one map operation. A lambda that reads n names bound outside it, debug build: 83 ms, 0.16, 0.41 and 1.16 s at n = 1000 to 8000 before, 76 ms, 0.13, 0.30 and 0.55 s after. The old code's ratio between 1000 and 8000 is 14, inside the limit, so no test was added |
| Z8 | `tables.rs` constants and call targets by linear search | O(C²), O(applies·lambdas) | fixed: `Tables` keeps each constant's index in a map (`const_at`) and each lambda's index by the path of its body (`lambda_at`, kept by `Tables::new` while it resolves the calls). Tests `many_constants_scale` and `many_lambdas_scale` (Z14). Old code, before the Z8 and Z14 fixes, one run per size: n lambdas 0.53, 1.6, 5.0 and 17.8 s at n = 60 to 500 (3 to 3.5 times per doubling); fixed 1.45, 2.9, 6.0, 12.0 and 22.9 s at n = 250 to 4000 (2 times). n constants: the old code passes the scaling test in 11 s (limit 62 s), so the test sizes do not show the old cost |
| Z9 | `tables.rs` `visit` cloned each node with its regions; each node kept its path, a string as long as its depth, and code generation built and looked up the same strings | O(N·depth) | fixed: `Node::regions` is `Vec<Arc<Region>>`, a `NodeInfo` holds its region and index, a planned region and node have numbers, and each region's plan is found once. A path is worked out from the links up for a message only. `Tables::visit` and `Gen::walk` keep the regions in progress on a stack of their own: `a_rate_table_thousands_deep_compiles_on_a_small_stack`, `a_decoder_thousands_deep_compiles_on_a_small_stack` and `ifs_thousands_deep_compile_on_a_small_stack` compile 4,000 levels in 128 KiB (one test per term, and the native run of each against the machine a test of its own, since CRANELIFT-scale-size), and a recursive walk put back overflows that stack. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::scaling::{ifs_nested_through_the_first_arm_scale, a_rate_table_of_many_tiers_scales, a_decoder_of_many_cases_scales, a_curried_function_of_many_parameters_scales}`, the object file timed alone on graphs built beforehand. A copy of each node's subtree put back in `visit` makes the first test fail its 55 s limit, against 21 s; one object file at n = 4,000 takes over 58 s, against about 3 s. One run per size, d = 120, 480 and 1,920: nested `if`s 91, 366 and 1,531 ms; a chain of `if`s 136, 497 and 2,339 ms; a chain of `match`es 28, 143 and 384 ms. Finding the plan compared path strings, O(d log R) per region; since T14-paths a region's plan is found from its parent's by index, O(1), and `lambda_at` is a `Vec` by plan index. The generated function's frame holds a slot for each word, so running a term d deep takes stack linear in d (832 KiB at d = 4,000) |
| Z9b | object file of a chain of `if`s or `match`es superlinear: lowering carried a name through every region above each read, as a new input of each | O(d²) nodes' inputs, code and time | fixed: `Lower::bring` keeps each edge once per region, in `Frame::brought`, and stops its walk at the nearest region that has the edge, so a read costs O(1) amortized. Test `l01_33_lowering::scaling::a_name_read_at_every_depth_scales`, n = 500, and `a_name_read_at_every_depth_enters_each_region_once`; with the map ignored, lowering takes 529 ms and 8.5 s at d = 500 and 2,000, 16 times as long, against 16 and 93 ms, 5.8 times. Object file at d = 120 and 240 was 428 KB and 1,468 KB; it is now 133 KB at d = 120 and 2,111 KB at d = 1,920 |
| Z10 | `zir` validator matches state-edge uses by search | O(S²) | fixed: each state edge's uses are counted in a map, and the edges kept in the order of first use so that the same edge is reported. Test `l01_33_lowering::scaling::checking_a_graph_of_many_pushes_scales`, n = 4000, the check timed alone on graphs made beforehand; with the old code put back it fails at 59 to 60 times as long for 8 times the size |
| Z11 | `lower.rs` `ports`: the ports of each `let`-bound lambda found by reading its whole body, the lambdas nested in it included, and each port looked for among those found | O(n·depth) | fixed: the uses of each lambda body, the ports it reads or pushes and the names free in it in the order of their first occurrence, are found once and kept by the body's occurrence id (`body_uses`, `Lower::bodies`; by its address before ADDR-keys); a lambda inside adds the uses of its own body less the names bound around it. A name bound inside the body is no longer taken for a function of the same name outside it. Test `l01_33_lowering::scaling::lowering_lambdas_bound_by_nested_lets_scales`, n = 500; with the old code put back it fails at 41 to 74 times |
| Z12 | `lower.rs`: a function called in place kept a copy of the whole scope it was defined in, and its call rebuilt the index of that scope | O(n·S) | fixed: the scope is a persistent map (`imbl::HashMap`), so keeping it and swapping it in each take `O(1)`, and leaving a scope restores the map saved on entering it. Test `l01_33_lowering::scaling::lowering_many_functions_called_in_place_scales`, n = 2000, which takes 9 s; with the old scope put back it does not finish in 30 min |
| Z13 | `lower.rs`: the current state of each port was found by searching the ports a region had used | O(n·P) | fixed: each frame keeps its ports' states in a map. Test `l01_33_lowering::scaling::lowering_pushes_to_many_ports_scales`, n = 2000, which takes 3.7 s; with the old code put back it fails at 42 to 44 times as long for 8 times the size |
| Z14 | native code and the counting machine on many fields, ports, constants, lambdas and uses of one value: each word held in a register across every call after it, a field's or port's index found by search, the ports a kernel term reads collected by `contains`, and the counting machine's memory check walking the whole heap after each step | O(n²) | fixed: each word is kept in a stack slot and loaded just before each use, so the register allocator sees only short live ranges (`codegen.rs` `Loc`); field and port indices are maps; the ports read are a set beside their order (`Lets`); the memory check looks only at the cells touched since the last check and runs the full audit only when one is wrong. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::scaling`, five shapes. Controls on the old code: many named fields killed at 671 s and many ports at 1411 s (limits 10 times the fixed time); many lambdas as in Z8; one value used n times is linear on the old code (0.05 to 0.75 s at n = 250 to 4000, against 0.08 to 1.28 s fixed), so that test does not show an old cost |
| Z15 | Cranelift's e-graph optimizer and backtracking register allocator | n^1.6 and n^1.4 measured; the e-graph pass also has fixed caps | fixed: `opt_level` `none` and `regalloc_algorithm` `single_pass` (`zed-native/src/lib.rs` `isa`), each pass linear. Zed does its own optimization over ZIR (DESIGN.md L23), not Cranelift's |
| R1 | `hooks.rs` slow path deep-copies inputs into the kernel and back | O(n) per op | fixed (T14-R1): each string, tuple or atom cell keeps the kernel `Value` made from it (`Cell::value` in `zed-rt/src/heap.rs`; since RT-cell-size, R16, each tuple or atom cell keeps only the sequence, `Cell::items`, the atom's name and field names coming from the cell, and a string keeps nothing, its `Text` being its value), set by `fresh` when a kernel result becomes cells and by `value` on the first read, and cleared by `free_cell`; a cell's parts never change while it is live, so the only write is the reuse of a freed slot, and the clear covers it. The cache is per cell, not keyed by an address. The conversion back from the kernel already made one cell per part, as the counting machine does (`memory.rs` `tree`), and it now keeps the value it was given, so a kernel result handed back to the kernel is not read again. `Stats::converted` counts the words `value` reads. On main a record of 65 cells compared 20 times read 1,341 words (20 calls of 66, plus the 21 of the result); now 61. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::kernel_inputs` (9): a tuple of 64n strings handed to the kernel n times, 7.8 times from 50 to 400 in instructions (47.8 on main, limit 24); a record the program built read n times, 7.8 times. Controls, not committed: main's heap with the counter, both scaling tests fail (47.6 and 65.0 times) and four count tests fail; the cache set by `fresh` only, the heap-level test fails at 64.9 times and a count is 101, not 63; the cache not cleared at free, the reuse test reads a stale `("nut", 40)` and nine other `l01_36` tests give wrong values |
| R2 | building an atom copies its whole payload through the kernel | O(n²) per list | fixed: `hooks::node` makes the atom from its words, as `Prim::Atom` in the kernel would, and calls the kernel only for a shape the kernel refuses, so the error is the kernel's. The field order is kept per node when the name and field names are constants (`Run::shapes`), so a struct atom costs no sort and no map. Test `l01_36_cranelift::scaling::a_list_of_many_atoms_scales`, n = 500: 8.0 times from 500 to 4,000, with no kernel call; on the old code it fails at 30.0 times. `l01_36_cranelift::hooks` checks field order, binders, a bare atom, a shape run many times and four refusals against the kernel and the machine |
| R3 | `Heap::parts` on a VAL word deep-clones the constant and appends to `vals` | O(n²) time and memory | fixed: since T14-value a clone of a constant is O(1), so the time was already linear (`matching_a_deep_constant_scales`, n = 1,000 and 8,000, passes on main too). What remained was memory: each match pushed every part it read to the table again, 100 entries after 1 match and 991 after 10 at depth 100. Now an entry's parts are entered once, together, the first time a match reads them (`Entry::parts`), and a match reads a cell's or a constant's parts in place with no copy (`Holder`, `Shape`). A literal pattern compares part by part against the word (`Heap::equals`), a string's byte length first, and `is` reads a constant or kernel value in place. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::reuse` (12) and `scaling::{matching_a_deep_constant_scales, matching_one_constant_many_times_scales}`; control, the old heap: `matching_a_rate_table_again_adds_no_entries` fails at 100 and 991 entries, and five more `reuse` tests fail. The path copy per binder in `matches` (`at.to_vec()`, d²/2 for a binder at every level of a pattern d deep) is fixed by HEAP-binder-paths, and in the counting machine by HEAP-binder-memory |
| R4 | `Rope::chars` counts characters on every call; the kernel's `len` counted `s.chars()` | O(n) per `len` | fixed: `zed_kernel::Text` keeps each node's length in bytes and in characters, counted once when text is made whole and added at a join, so `len` is O(1) natively and in the kernel and never reads the text; both use `Text::char_count`. `zed-rt`'s `Rope` is gone, and the native heap holds `Text` (`Obj::Str`). Tests `l01_36_cranelift::string_scaling` (instructions, 8 times the size; limit 24): `len` of one string of 16,384n two-byte characters called n times, n = 100, natively 7.84 (main 39.1) and in the kernel 7.90 (main 63.9); `++` of two such strings n times natively 7.83 (main: over 60 s) and in the kernel 7.94 (main 7.94, already linear). `l01_36_cranelift::strings` compares kernel and native counts on ASCII, accented, CJK, emoji, empty and a line of 500 appends. Negative control, `char_count` and `join` counting by a scan: all seven tests fail, 39.1 to 63.9 times or over 60 s |
| R5 | rope flattened again after every append | O(n²) | fixed: a join is never written out; its text is read block by block (row C29); `Heap::value` hands the kernel the cell's `Text` itself, so a string crossing to the kernel and back is not copied, and the kernel's `len` reads the kept count. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::string_scaling`, n lines of 32,768 characters with a read after each, n = 60: append then `len` natively 7.89 (main 7.89, already linear) and in the kernel 9.38 (main 63.3); append then `show` natively, each `show` a kernel call whose result the next line is appended to, 7.89 (main 42.6). Read whole at each use, O(len) each: hash, printing, `lower`, `upper`, `trim`, the casts (the last four through `Text::flat`, a temporary not kept); equality and order of two strings of equal byte length, and `Heap::equals` against a literal, stop at the first byte that differs. Since WRITE-prefix-scale nothing is cached in a node, so holding every step of a chain of n joins is O(n) bytes (row C29); `Stats::copied` and the test `a_log_read_after_every_line_keeps_only_its_latest_text` are gone with the cache; `text::tests::reading_every_prefix_held_keeps_no_copy_of_it` checks that printing, hashing and comparing every held prefix allocates only the walks' stacks, and the `l01_36_cranelift` tests `reuse`, `kinds`, `strings` and `deep_heap` check on a block doubled 50 times (about 145 PB in 51 nodes) that a literal of another length, a test by kind, `show` and `Heap::value` read and copy none of it. Since T14-rope-len a join adds the two byte counts with `checked_add` and refuses a sum past `usize::MAX` (`KernelError::StringTooLong`, O(1) per join), so a string doubled 64 times is an error, not a wrapped or panicking length; tests `text::tests` and `l01_36_cranelift::string_length` |
| R6 | heap never reuses a freed cell; `vals` only grows | O(allocations) memory | fixed for cells: a freed cell goes on a free list and the next allocation takes it, so the cells held are the peak live, not the allocations (`a_string_made_and_freed_again_and_again_takes_one_cell`; on the old heap, one slot per allocation). A cell word carries the cell's generation in the 24 bits above its 40-bit index, and each free advances it, so a word kept past its cell's free is reported even after the cell is taken again; a cell freed in its last generation is not reused. `inc` checks the generation and the count with `checked_add` and returns the error at once; `hooks::rt_inc`, which generated code does not check, records it as the run's error, so it is reported when no `dec` follows (was kept until the next `dec`, and lost when the run ended first; `hooks` unit tests `an_inc_that_fails_*`, both fail on the old code). `release_one` puts each kept path with its part in one pass (was a filter of all paths per part, O(arity · kept)). `value` keeps the value of each cell held more than once and shares it after, so a DAG of cells is read once per cell: `reading_a_value_whose_parts_share_cells_scales`, n = 1,000 and 8,000; on the old heap a value of 64 cells, each holding the one below twice, is not read in 60 s. Not fixed, by design: the table. A VAL word has no count, generated code and hooks copy it freely, so no point says an entry is free; a free list for it cannot be correct. Its growth is now bounded by what a run reads: an entry's parts once, and the empty tuple and each bare atom once (`Heap::bare`). A match enters nothing since T14-hooks (R12). `Heap::fresh` still makes one cell per path of a DAG value, which mirrors the counting machine of L1.34; sharing them changes both |
| R7 | `matched` deep-copies a binder the arm does not use | O(unused) | fixed: with the scrutinee owned, the plan owns every binder the arm uses (`memory.rs`, arm modes), so a borrowed binder is one the arm never reads; it gets the error word and no copy, and the counts still agree with the machine. Test `l01_36_cranelift::scaling::many_matches_with_an_unused_binder_scale`, a tuple of 64n strings bound unused n times, n = 50: 7.7 times from 50 to 400; on the old code it fails at 38.1 times. Since T14-heap-rest the world is built before the timing; with the copy restored it still fails, at 39.4 times |
| R8 | `Heap::dec` allocated a stack on every call, even for a word that is not a cell or a count that stays above 0 | O(1) with an allocation per call | fixed: returns at once for those two cases, frees a cell with no parts with no stack, and otherwise reuses the stack `Heap::todo` through `mem::take`. About 12 ns to about 4.7 ns per drop that leaves the cell live (50 million drops, three runs each). The old code is also linear, so a timing test cannot fail on it; `heap.rs` tests check the stack is unused or kept. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::drops`, three shapes at n = 4000. Controls: a count of live cells per drop fails the shared-string test, 90 to 92 times as long at 8 times the size; a queue in place of the stack fails the wide-tuple test, 60 to 62 times |
| R9 | `Heap::fresh`, `value`, `release`, `matches`, `hooks::term` and `rename` recursed on the depth of a value, a pattern or a chain of closures | stack O(depth): overflow | fixed: each keeps its work on a stack on the heap, O(depth) memory, time unchanged. Tests `deep_heap`, 1,000,000 deep on a 2 MiB stack, and scaling at 100,000 and 800,000: 7.4 to 11.9 times. Controls: the old code aborts on every deep test; a scan of the stack at each step fails all four at 4,000 and 32,000, 51 to 164 times. `term` walked a shared closure once per path, 2^d for d levels each capturing the level below twice; since HOOKS-term-dag it builds each closure's term once per kernel call, by a memo in `Lets` keyed by the cell word on the native path (index and generation, so a cell freed and taken again is a new key) and by `Clo::cell` in the counting machine (cells are never reused), and every later use is a copy that shares the body (tests `l01_36_cranelift::shared_closures`, 60 levels in one kernel call, and `hooks::tests::a_closure_captured_twice_at_each_level_is_built_once`, 64 levels, the two uses one body by id, run once in the kernel; scaling at 250 and 2,000 levels: machine 7.98 times, native 7.83 times; control without the memo, 12 to 20 levels: 4 times per 2 levels on both paths, 17.6 s and 11.6 s at 20); `value` reads it once since T14-heap (R6), and the path copy per binder in `matches` is fixed by HEAP-binder-paths (runtime) and HEAP-binder-memory (counting machine), whose `Paths` and `Kept` both read from `zed_kernel::paths` since HEAP-paths-shared; `Heap::fresh` and the machine's `fresh` (`Machine::tree`) gave each occurrence of a part its own cell, so a value from the kernel or a port whose levels each hold the one below twice cost 2^d cells: measured on the base code, d = 10 to 20 allocated 2^(d+1) - 1 cells on both paths, 4 times the time per 2 levels (machine 0.26 ms to 337 ms, native 1.1 ms to 513 ms, load 36). Since HEAP-fresh-dag each keeps one cell per shared sequence, by `Value::shared_parts` (the sequence's `Items` id, and for an atom its name and field names' id, so a tuple and atoms of other names over one sequence stay apart; equal sequences built apart stay apart), counted once per holder by an increment; a sequence held once is not entered in the memo (tests `l01_36_cranelift::shared_values`, 8: 60 levels from an input and from a port in 62 cells with equal machine and native counts and no live cell at the end, a value held once, equal sequences built apart, empty sequences, a tuple and two atoms over one sequence; scaling at 2,000 and 16,000 levels: machine 8.19 times, native 7.05 times, load 11). The control is the base code, which has no visited set (numbers above) |
| R10 | generated code calls itself on the machine stack, and a function's frame has a 16-byte slot per word | stack O(program recursion + function size): overflow | fixed: `zed_native::run_at` runs the generated code on a stack that `zed_rt::Stack` maps for the run, as large as the machine's memory and swap together, reserved with `MAP_NORESERVE` (pages take memory only when touched) with a `PROT_NONE` page below it, switched to once with `psm::on_stack` and unmapped when the run ends; a panic on it is caught and resumed on the caller's stack. Depth and frame size are limited only by memory, as the heap is: no depth limit, no size switch, no change to generated code and no cost per call. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::deep_calls`, on a thread with a 2 MiB stack: `linked_list` of 10,000 and 80,000 nested calls gives the kernel's value; scaling 10,000 to 80,000 calls, 6.12 times the instructions (limit 24); `deep_heap::a_function_of_20000_concatenations_runs_on_a_smaller_thread_stack`, a frame of more than 312 KiB on a thread of 256 KiB, gives the kernel's value; `deep_heap::a_wide_function_runs_in_time_linear_in_its_width`, compiling and running that function natively at 2,500 and 20,000 concatenations on a thread of 256 KiB, 8.1 times the instructions and 8.0 times the bytes (limit 24); `zed-rt` unit tests: 100,000 frames of 1 KiB on a 2 MiB thread, the size of the mapping, a panic carried back, and `a_limited_address_space_refuses_the_reservation`: a process whose address space is limited to 8 GiB cannot reserve the stack and gets the error "runtime: cannot reserve a stack of … bytes for a run" (the complexity tradeoff at `Stack::new`: such a process runs no native code; a complete solution is a stack that grows by segments, checked at each function entry). Controls: on main the 10,000-call program and the scaling test abort with a stack overflow; the unit test without `Stack` aborts too; an O(n²) spin added in `rt_callable` fails the scaling test at 35.0 times; run on the thread's own stack, the 20,000-concatenation test aborts with a stack overflow; an O(n²) spin in `run_in` fails the wide scaling test at 28.8 times; with no limit on the address space the reservation test fails (R10-stack-notes). Stack slots reused by liveness, which would shrink frames, are not done; they are not needed for correctness |
| PRE-stack | `zedc-preimage/src/preimage.rs` (was `store/preimage.rs`), the transfer's analyses (`mentions`, `reads_mod`, `constant`, `lin`, `formula`, `fwd`, `clip`, `back`, `pa`, `by_class`, `close`, `scan`), on `Walk` with `zed-kernel/src/frames.rs` (was `store/frames.rs`) | stack O(term depth): overflow; on a 2 MiB thread the transfer overflowed between depths 1,000 and 3,000, since `zed_kernel::on_stack` is a no-op (T2-eval) | fixed (PRE-stack-explicit; PRE-stack first merged a growable stack, `stacker::maybe_grow` at `deeper`, as a temporary form by the author's decision of 2026-11-04): every analysis is an `async fn` of `Walk` (`close`, `mentions`, `reads_mod`, `constant`, `fwd`, `clip`, `summon`, `back`, `scan`, `pa`, `by_class`, `lin`, `formula` and their helpers), and each call that may recurse returns a `frames::Deep`, which hands the callee's state machine to the loop in `frames::Stack::run`; the loop keeps the suspended callers in a `Vec` on the heap and runs the top one, so the thread's stack holds one frame's code at any depth, and depth is limited by memory. The calls run in the order plain recursion ran them, and the memo is filled and read as before (`Walk::cached`, `Walk::translated`). O(1) per call: one boxed frame and one `Rc` cell for the answer; a call whose answer is in the memo takes no frame (`Stack::ready`). `stacker` is gone from `preimage.rs` and from `zedc`'s dependencies; the `// Complexity tradeoff:` comment at `deeper` is gone with it. `l01_25_preimage_catalog::deep`: a sum, a chain of lets and nested ifs, 100,000 deep, on a 2 MiB stack, and each scales at depths 12,500 and 100,000: 8.37, 8.09 and 7.97 times the instructions and 8.00, 8.18 and 7.99 times the bytes, limit 24. Control, run once and not committed: an O(depth) scan of the suspended frames at each push gives 49.8 times the instructions at depths 1,500 and 12,000 (fails; 8.03 without it); at depths 12,500 and 100,000 it ran over 60 s. Constant cost against the `stacker` form, measured at load 44 to 56: the deep tests take 2.12, 6.00 and 6.47 s before and 3.9, 7.5 and 10.5 s after, with peak memory 284, 883 and 695 MB before and 381, 1,274 and 796 MB after; the randomized unit test `entries_made_below_a_stop_give_what_reading_the_term_again_gives` takes 11% more processor time (perf samples), from allocation and moves of frame states. PRE-frame-size: the added memory was mostly the frames themselves. `frames::frame` wrapped the callee in an `async` block that kept the captured call apart from the call being awaited, so each frame was twice its callee (`back_in`'s frame 2,272 bytes for a 1,120-byte call, `by_class`'s 2,720); a frame now takes the function that makes the call (`Stack::call(move || ...)`), and `back_in`'s frame is 1,232 bytes (test `zed-kernel` `frames::tests::a_frame_holds_its_call_once`, which fails on the old form, 8,312 bytes for a 4,144-byte call). At depth 100,000, measured one test at a time against main 641b040c at load 46 to 48: sum 2.38 s and 257 MB against 2.79 s and 380 MB, chain of lets 6.54 s and 907 MB against 8.82 s and 1,274 MB, ifs 7.38 s and 700 MB against 11.54 s and 798 MB (processor time 1.58, 4.00, 5.67 s against 1.61, 4.17, 5.67 s); the stacker form had 284, 883 and 695 MB. Boxing the large inline awaits (`Box::pin` at 18 sites, `back_prim`, `call_back`, `summon`, `pa`, `fwd_prim`, `pa_if`, `by_class_node` and others) was measured and not kept: 278, 842 and 717 MB and no less time, since a boxed call that stays suspended under the recursion keeps its size and adds an allocation |
| R11 | `zed-native::run`: when `codegen::define`, `finalize_definitions` or a lookup failed, `?` returned before `free_memory`, so the JIT module's code and data pages were never freed | O(program size) memory leaked per failed compile | fixed: a `Jit` guard frees them on every way out (`zed-native` unit test `a_failed_compile_frees_the_jit_memory`) |
| R12 | the table of uncounted values: an entry per match, and no free list for entries | O(matches) memory | measured, no free list added: a match adds no entry (T14-hooks gave an unused binder the error word), and a run adds entries only for its constants, their parts once, and each distinct empty tuple or bare atom once, so the table does not grow with the runs of a match or a read. `zed_native::Outcome` now gives `table` and `cells` at the end of a run. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::table`, (entries, cells) at n = 50 and 400: an unused binder (0, 7) at both, a function matched by `is` or `_` (0, 2), n reads and drops of `((), #nil, #some(()))` with a bare atom made per call (4, 4); time for each at 500 and 4,000 by `check_run`. Controls: the copy of an unused binder restored gives 50 and 400 entries; no reuse of bare values gives 202 and 1,602. The kernel path for a function scrutinee no longer asks the kernel for its binders' values (MATCH-fn-binder), so it adds no entry either |
| MATCH-fn-binder | `zedc::zir::memory::Machine::matched` and `zed_native::hooks::matched`, a function scrutinee (closure, primitive or lookup port) bound by a name, `match f { h -> h(z) }` | O(1) per match | fixed: both asked the kernel for `match s { p -> (i, binders…) }`, and a tuple holds no function, so both failed with "type error: `(..)` applied to a function" where the kernel gives the value. A pattern that matches a function binds it whole or not at all, so the kernel now only picks the arm (`(i,)` natively, `()` in each binder's place in the machine), and each binder is the scrutinee itself at the empty path: one `Rc` clone or one word per binder, and the number of binders is fixed by the program. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::function_binders` (9): kernel, machine and native give the same value with the release fused and not, and native counts as the machine; `binders_of_a_function_scale`, n matches at 500 and 4,000 by `check_run` (limit 24). Control (old code, run once, not committed): 7 of the 9 fail; the two that pass on both are the `is`/`_` arm and the function inside a tuple, which is the kernel's own error in all three |
| R13 | `is T` on a string, tuple or atom in cells made the whole value first | O(size of the value) per test | fixed: `Heap::is_in` meets `T` with the cell's kind (all strings, the tuple universe, or every atom of its name) and answers from that when `T` holds all of the kind or none of it; otherwise it reads the value as before. Tests `l01_36_cranelift::kinds` (4): 64 tests of a tuple of 2,000 and 16,000 strings, 1.0 times the work (limit 3); `is str` and `is int` on a concatenated string copy no bytes. Control, the old `is_in`: 8.0 times, and 2 bytes copied |
| Z16 | `codegen::dispatch` chose a branch by a test per block | O(k) per dispatch, below `kernel_match`, which clones all k patterns | fixed: a Cranelift `Switch` (jump table); constant factor, no order change |
| Z17 | `zir::validate` (`zir/validate.rs`, was in `zir/mod.rs`) formatted the path of every node, input and region as a string (`format!("{path}.{k}")`, `format!("{at}/{j}")`, and a name per state use in `src_name`), eagerly and not only into an error; the path is as long as the depth | O(n·depth) bytes allocated | fixed by T2-mid (b35b33f5): one path buffer, extended by `write!` and cut back by `truncate` as the walk enters and leaves a node or region, copied into a `String` only for an error, and state uses keyed by edge, not by a path string. Before: whole `lower` at depth 500 against 4000 allocated 40.3 and 32.6 times the bytes (`prices` and `lets_of_lambdas`), and `validate` alone about 4 times per doubling. After (ZIR-validate-bytes, inputs built before timing, depth 4000 against 32000, load 36): 65,602,358 against 524,807,734 bytes (8.0 times) and 98,906,926 against 893,515,806 (9.0 times); instructions 8.1 and 8.4 times, about 2 to 3 s per test. Tests `l01_33_lowering::scaling::a_name_read_at_every_depth_scales` and `lowering_lambdas_bound_by_nested_lets_scales` check bytes and instructions again (`scaling::check`). Negative control, not committed: one copy of the path per node put back in `validate` gives 35.7 and 30.6 times the bytes at depth 4000 against 32000 (load 39), and both tests fail on bytes. At depth 500 such a control passed (14.1 and 14.6 times), which is why the tests start at 4000 |

Test `l01_32_canonical_zir::scaling::canonicalizing_an_edge_of_many_facets_is_n_log_n` (F = 100 and 800, facets in reverse order, every third a hint); the old loop fails it at 508.7 times the instructions. `l01_32_canonical_zir::facet_order` checks that `Value`'s `Ord` agrees with `==` and is transitive on every kind of facet value |

| Z19 | `zir/lower.rs` `Lower::add` took a node of equal 256-bit key as the same node, with no confirmation (L1.37a) | one hash lookup and O(log k) shape comparisons per add for k nodes of its key, each at most the size of the smaller node (`impl Ord for canon::Shape`, an explicit stack over the two nodes' regions, skipping shared regions); k is 1 in the full build but for a 256-bit collision, about n/256 in the `short-addresses` build | fixed (L1.37a): the nodes of one key are kept in a `BTreeMap` ordered by `canon::Shape` (the normal-form bytes of the node's shell, then its regions by contents), so a key never decides equality alone and colliding keys cost O(log k) comparisons, in both builds. ## Complexity tradeoffs

Sites that give up some inputs, or some precision, to avoid the cost of a complete algorithm,
and that had no row before (docs/reviews/tradeoffs.md, finding 6). Each site carries a
comment beginning `Complexity tradeoff:` that names this row. Columns: where, what is given
up and the answer those inputs get, why (the cost of the complete algorithm), and the input
that triggers it with the test. Rows marked "violation" switch behavior at a size or a
magnitude and break the no-thresholds rule; TD-ends, TD-values, CAP-power and CAP-bits
replaced them and updated their rows.

| ID | Where | Given up | Why | Trigger and test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `store/presburger.rs` `hull_from` (fixed by TD-ends, row S33) | nothing: every bound is exact at any magnitude | ends are unbounded integers (`End::Fin(Num)`), one machine word while they fit in `i64` | a bound whose magnitude exceeds `i64`. `l01_38_presburger::omega::a_bound_past_i64_is_exact`, `omega::a_model_may_hold_values_past_128_bits` |
| C2 | `store/presburger.rs` `products` | a product of two variables is an opaque atom, bounded only by products of pairs of linear premises; a goal that needs other nonlinear reasoning is `Entailment::NotProved` | entailment over integer polynomials is undecidable (Hilbert's tenth problem); over the reals it is doubly exponential in the variables | a product atom in the premises or the goal. `l01_38_presburger::entailment::a_product_is_bounded_only_through_the_premises_on_its_factors`. Cost (LADDER-study, 2026-11-07): each factor of a product took the hull of its atom over the whole premise set, O(factors × premises), quadratic in `ladder::products_of_premises_in_pairs_scale` (n independent pairs `x_i >= i`, `y_i >= 2i + 1` with goal the sum of `x_i * y_i >= 0`, 16 → 128: 63.3 times the bytes); fixed by splitting the premise rows into parts that share no atom (union-find) and taking the hull of an atom over its own part only, which passes that test at 8.7 times the instructions and 8.0 times the bytes (19.1M → 166.2M instructions). C2-chain (2026-11-08): a part whose rows are all difference constraints and bounds now gives the hulls of all its atoms in one shortest-path pass (`difference_hulls`, O(m log n)), and every part is solved once for its point, not once per factor; `ladder::products_whose_factors_one_chain_connects_scale` (a chain `z_i >= z_{i-1} + 1` with `x_i, y_i >= z_i` and goal the sum of `x_i * y_i >= 0`, 16 → 128) took 103.3 times the instructions (1252M → 129361M) and 83.7 times the bytes before, and 10.8 times the instructions (27.7M → 299.1M) and 8.8 times the bytes after; the result is the same as before on 3,000 random premise sets (2,080 factor hulls by the one pass). C2-chain-general (2026-11-09): a part with any other row (a coefficient other than ±1, three atoms or more, a negation, a disjunction, a definition) asked each factor's hull of the whole part, O(factors × part); now `part_bounds` gives it the shortest-path hulls of its difference rows and bounds, then the bounds each other top-level row gives its atoms from those (`row_bounds`, an equality read both ways, the negation of `t >= 0` read as `-t - 1 >= 0`) and those each top-level disjunction gives as the widest over the disjuncts that have a point (two passes over each disjunct's rows, shared disjuncts read once), then the shortest paths again, O(m log n) for m rows over n atoms. No method gives the identical bounds in O(n log n): the exact bound of each side of each atom of a general integer system is an integer program, NP-hard in general. Decision by the standing rules: the bounds are sound and may be wider than the hulls, which DESIGN allows (rung 2 is incomplete, and a goal not proved passes to the next rung; the sentence "A factor's bounds are found once for its part" in L1.38's "Where this document does not say" paragraph, DOCS-TODO 36), so no refusal is needed. Lost in the first attempt and found again in the second (below): a bound that needs two rows at once (`v >= w1`, `v >= w2`, `w1 + w2 >= 10` gives `v >= 5`). Still lost: a row two levels deep. On random parts (`presburger::tests::part_bounds_contain_the_hulls_the_solver_finds`, up to 6 rows over 4 names, coefficients -3 to 3, a third with a disjunction) every bound contains the solver's hull and 2,682 of 3,432 are the hull. Scaling, 16 → 128 (debug build, load 16 to 26), old code then new: the chain with `z0 + z1 + x0 >= 0` 106.5 times the instructions and 85.7 times the bytes, now 10.5 and 8.6 times (28.6M → 301.3M; `products_along_a_chain_with_a_general_row_scale`); with `2 * x_i + y_i >= z_i` on each link 85.6 times the bytes, now 11.0 and 8.7 times (59.2M → 650.8M; `..._general_row_on_each_link_scale`); with `abs(x_i - y_i) <= z_i + 1` on each link over 60 s, now 10.1 and 8.5 times (47.2M → 476.1M; `..._disjunction_on_each_link_scale`). C2-chain-general, second attempt (2026-11-09): `part_bounds` first eliminates every atom that is not a factor and is in no disjunction where that is exact over the integers and adds no terms (`shadow`), so `a + b >= 10`, `b + 2 * c <= 3`, `c >= 0` with `b`, `c` not factors give `a >= 7`; reads each general row through the difference rows to the factors (`eliminate`, one level, O(m log n)), so `v >= w1`, `v >= w2`, `w1 + w2 >= 10` gives `v >= 5` (`w1 + w2 >= 9` rounds to the same; `>= 8` gives `v >= 4`, and `v * c >= 5 * c` is then not proved; `ladder::a_bound_through_a_general_row_and_difference_rows_is_found`, which also proves `(a >= 5 || a >= 7)` to `a * c >= 5 * c`); and passes bounds from row to row in Kahn's order over the sides of the atoms (`propagate`, linear in the terms, independent of row order; a side that waits on itself through the rows is let go with the bound it has). Where the goal is still not proved and a factor's side is not known to be the hull's, the side is asked of the solver over the factor's cluster (the general rows and disjunctions that share atoms with it, by union-find, with the difference rows inside it and the bounds found; `clusters`, `Tier::Local`), and only if still not proved over the whole part (`Tier::Whole`); a refused try keeps the verdict before it. Counted by `presburger::hull_sides_asked`: 0 sides in `products_whose_factors_one_chain_connects_scale`, `products_along_a_chain_with_a_general_row_scale` (both assert it). Scaling, 16 → 128 (load 28 to 39): `ladder::products_whose_factor_bounds_pass_through_two_general_rows_scale` 11.7 times the instructions, 9.1 times the bytes, 0 sides (89.5 times the bytes before `shadow`, 24 → 192 sides); `..._pass_from_row_to_row_scale` (the same with `b * c`, so `b`, `c` kept) 10.7 and 8.6 times, 0 sides; `..._wait_on_each_other_scale` 5.6 and 5.1 times, 0 sides; `products_whose_factors_keep_open_sides_scale` (`x - b - c >= 4` with `b`, `c` kept: `x >= 7` needs two rows at once) 10.0 and 8.4 times (274.7M → 2739.6M) with the sides asked over each link's cluster, and 84.8 times the bytes with them asked over the whole part (74 → 578 sides). Negative controls (not committed): with `clusters` empty, that test at 8 → 64 fails at 63.4 times the bytes; with `propagate` empty, `..._pass_from_row_to_row_scale` fails with 66 sides asked at 16. Remaining cost: `Tier::Whole` is O(open sides × part); it is reached only when a path of difference rows through atoms outside a cluster ties two of its atoms more closely than their bounds, and every instance of that class built (three) was refused by the solver ("four variables or more") before any scaling could be measured. C2-local-tier (2026-11-12): `Tier::Local` asked each open side of the solver over the factor's whole cluster, O(open sides × cluster), quadratic when one cluster holds n open factors (k links `x{i} - b{i} - c{i} >= 4`, `c{i} >= 0`, `b{i} * c{i} >= -1000000` joined into one cluster by `b0 + ... + b{k-1} >= -1000000k`, k = 8 → 64: 41 times the instructions on 2eecdbe4b, 319.3M → 13,129.1M). Now `local::cluster_sides` finds all the open sides of a cluster in one pass over the block-cut tree of its incidence graph (atoms and rows as nodes; the atoms of a disjunction joined in a cycle, so a disjunction is never a cut node; Tarjan's algorithm, iterative). Each block gets from the blocks beyond each of its cut nodes one message: for a cut atom, its interval over that side of the tree; for a cut row, the least and greatest value of the row's terms on that side, so the block keeps the row as `P_B + c + (greatest of the rest) >= 0` (and the least, for an equality). One pass up the tree and one down give each block every message, with prefix and suffix meets over the children, and the solver is asked each side over its own block only; a cut atom's side is the meet of its messages. O(Σ_B (cuts(B) + sides(B)) × size(B)), linear in the cluster when its blocks are of bounded size, as on every family measured. Each bound is implied by the cluster, so it is sound; it can be wider than the cluster's hull where a projection has gaps, and then `Tier::Whole` follows as before. Answers unchanged on every test in l01_38_presburger and zedc_presburger. Test: `ladder::products_whose_factors_one_sum_joins_scale` (the same links, with the sum written over `w{i} == b{i}`), n = 8 → 64: 9.7 times the instructions (160.2M → 1,547.4M) and 7.9 times the bytes, against the limit 17.6 (load 63 to 70); negative control with the old per-side search over the cluster, run once and not committed: 25.4 times the bytes (50.0M → 1,271.5M), failed (load 69 to 80). C2-pairs-long-row (2026-11-12): on the brief's family itself, the sum written on the `b{i}` directly, the products of pairs were Θ(k²): the k-term sum is a linear premise on every `b{i}`, and its product with each row on `c{i}` has k terms, so 112 → 896 rows carried 845 → 24,757 terms, and the whole check was 33.5 times (173.4M → 5,806.7M). Now a premise `a` on `x` is left out of the products for `x * y` when it mentions a factor `u` foreign to `y`: not `y`, on no premise on `y`, multiplied in the formulas by nothing that is `y` or on a premise on `y`, and cancelled by no other linear premise `r` that mentions a partner of `y` (the atom `u * y` of `r * b'` has the coefficient `r_u × b'_y`, so `r` cancels it only when it holds `u` with the other sign, or when the premises on `y` hold `y` with both signs; CD-audit, below). Each product of `a` with a premise on `y` then holds an atom `u * v` the formulas do not mention, free in the linear reading. Leaving a product out is sound (it only weakens the premises). Kept: `(x + z) * (y - w) + (x - z) * (y + w)` for `x * y - z * w >= 0`, and the Fourier–Motzkin cases `x - z >= 0, x + z - w >= 0, y >= 0` to `2 * x * y >= w * y` and `x - z >= 0, w + z >= 0, y >= 0` to `x * y + w * y >= 0` (`ladder::a_product_whose_free_atoms_cancel_is_kept`, named `a_premise_with_a_factor_foreign_to_the_other_side_is_left_out_of_the_products` until C2-pairs-exact). The rows on each factor are borrowed, not copied for each factor (a copy cost O(k²) for one row of k factors), and `Lin::product` adds terms in place. A Python model of the step (230 random entailments that need products and that the products of every pair prove, of four kinds: single products, a combination of two or three rows on one side that cancels variables, crossed products, and a union of 30 of them) loses none; without the sign test it lost 90. CD-audit (2026-11-12): the first version took from the CD seat of the cross-review the condition that a factor multiplied by nothing in the formulas is never foreign. That condition named the wrong cause: in its own example (`d` between `(b + d + 2 * a) * c` and `(e + d - b) * c` with `1 - c >= 0` and `2 * c - 1 >= 0`) `d` cancels because the premises on `c` hold `c` with both signs, and adding the unrelated premise `d * q >= 0` made `d` a factor with a partner and lost the proof. The condition is replaced by the sign argument above, with `y` held with both signs (`ladder::a_factor_cancels_through_rows_on_the_other_side_of_both_signs`, whose third case, the example with `d * q >= 0` added, fails on e8fea7860); the rows that hold `y` with both signs are found once, in one pass. The model loses none of the 230 and none of 12,000 further random entailments (the CD rule's 6,556 were not saved and were not rerun).
